The Welkin Moon crisis ended with Dottore destroyed; Varka sent the expedition home in waves. In 6.4 he resolved Andrius's corruption and woke at Windrise among friends.

101.content:
Venti (also: Barbatos, Anemo Archon, God of Freedom, Tone-Deaf Bard): Second-eldest of The Seven, he freed Mondstadt, refused to rule it, and wears the face of a long-dead human friend.

Few know who he is; most Mondstadters see a youthful, tipsy minstrel who mooches drinks and sneezes at cats. He prefers it that way.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Mondstadt. Signora took his Gnosis for the Tsaritsa; still a god, he has readied a hidden gale against a storm he senses coming.

The Tsaritsa now holds every Gnosis except the lost Pyro Gnosis. He has not gone to Snezhnaya.

102.content:
Vesna (also: Vesna Strivozha, Commander of the Druzhna, Snowy Banquet's Sharp Blade, Miss Fern): A young Vila noble who commands the Druzhna, the Tsaritsa's personal guard. She and head housemaid Danica are Her Majesty's two right hands. She is a radiant prankster with a commander's sharp judgment and absolute loyalty.

She carried a fragment of the Ruler of Life's authority through the Vila bloodline, and was trained by Capitano, whose death still grieves her.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Snezhnograd, still Commander after Ronova's defeat (7.1). Rhinedottir reclaimed her Life authority; a small portion came back to her.

The Druzhna is stretched thin. Her special recruitment drive found the Traveler, whom she then recommended to the Tsaritsa as Consultant.

103.content:
Vodyanitsa (also: Lingering Siren-Song, Prima Donna of the Korolevskiy Troupe, Prima Vodyanitsa, Miss Vodyanitsa): When almost every Water Imp left Snezhnograd long ago, she stayed and kept singing; she is now the last of her kind on its stages. Off stage she works for the Rokot, a secret civilian group that exposes corruption.

Bright and teasing in public, she privately keeps the departed Water Imps' songs alive and wonders who still truly listens to her own.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and performing in Snezhnograd after 7.1; still Prima Donna and a Rokot member.

Project Stuzha is suspended; the Rokot suspended Odette, but Vodyanitsa still works with her and Alyosha. She manages the renovated Rankova Zorya station.

104.content:
Wanderer (also: Scaramouche, The Balladeer, Hat Guy, Kunikuzushi, Kabukimono, Shouki no Kami): Raiden Ei's puppet, once Scaramouche, Sixth Fatui Harbinger and Sumeru's would-be false god. He erased himself from Irminsul, then took his memories back. Now an Akademiya student ("Hat Guy") and Nahida's covert agent.

Caustic, proud and allergic to sympathy, but no longer a villain. As of 6.6 he has settled his score with Dottore.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Sumeru City (7.1), studying political science and helping Nahida. Dottore is dead. Absent from the 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya story.

The Fatui believe the sixth seat has been vacant for centuries.

105.content:
Wonderland Manekin (also: Manekin, Manekina, Miliastra Wonderland Manekin, Wonderland Manekina): A doll-like avatar gifted to the Traveler and Paimon by Octavia, the Hexenzirkel's wandering witch, for exploring her realm, the Miliastra Wonderland. Comes as a male Manekin and a female Manekina; its owner chooses its name and looks.

Octavia had watched the Traveler and Paimon and judged them the right new masters for her Wonderland. Playable since 6.1 (Luna II, 2025-10-22).

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the Manekins are active in the Wonderland and in Teyvat; neither appears in the 6.x or 7.0-7.1 Archon Quests.

In Teyvat both forms are party members but cannot fight in the same team.

key: Duke of the Fortress of Meropide
Administrator of the Fortress of Meropide
106.content:
Wriothesley (also: Duke Wriothesley, Duke of the Fortress of Meropide, Lord Incognito, Wrio): Duke and Administrator of the Fortress of Meropide, Fontaine's undersea prison and factory. Convicted as a teenager of killing the foster parents who trafficked children, he rose from inmate to warden and runs the place with tea, ledgers, information and, when needed, his fists.

Inmates call him "Your Grace"; he got used to it. Few Fontainians know his face, so he walks the Court almost unrecognised.

Status as of 7.1: Alive; still Duke and Administrator as of 7.1, with no role in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya Archon Quests.

With the flood prophecy over, he is thinking about buying property in the Court. He has been to Nod-Krai on official business (6.1) and follows the news from there.

107.content:
Xiangling (also: Mao Xiangling, Exquisite Delicacy, Madam Xiangling): Head chef (and waitress) of the Wanmin Restaurant at Chihu Rock, Liyue Harbor, run with her father, Chef Mao. A fearless culinary experimenter who believes any ingredient can be made delicious, she roams Teyvat for new ones with Guoba, her small fire-breathing companion.

Famous in Liyue and Mondstadt, she scorns the Li-versus-Yue cuisine feud and dreams of her own chili-based tradition.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and working at the Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor as of 7.1, with Guoba at her side.

Not involved in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya Archon Quests. Lately she is brewing a "spice relief drink" for customers daunted by her heat.

108.content:
Xianyun (also: Cloud Retainer, Passerine Herald, Adeptus of the Clouds, Liuyun Jiefeng Zhenjun): An ancient crane adeptus of Liyue who fought for Rex Lapis in the Archon War, a brilliant inventor of mechanisms and doting master to Ganyu and Shenhe. Since 4.4 she has lived in Liyue Harbor in human form as "Xianyun".

She moved to see what draws her disciples to mortal life. In the city she passes as a tall, bespectacled newcomer who haggles over machinery and spends Mora freely; Madame Ping says she is someone you can truly rely on when the going gets tough.

Status as of 7.1: Alive. She lives as Xianyun near Chihu Rock in Liyue Harbor where she trains her young disciple Shuyu, and keeps her abode on Mt. Aocang.

Few mortals know she is an adeptus; her neighbours see the virtuous elder who raised Shenhe. She has even holidayed in Mondstadt on an itinerary the Traveler wrote.

109.content:
Xiao (also: Alatus, General Alatus, Vigilant Yaksha, Conqueror of Demons, Bane of All Evil, Guardian Yaksha, Adeptus Xiao): The last of the five foremost Yakshas whom Rex Lapis set against the vengeful remnants of fallen gods. From Wangshu Inn he wages an endless, unseen war for Liyue, carrying a karmic debt that poisons body and mind. Youthful-looking, but over two thousand years old.

Few mortals know of him; those who do call him the Conqueror of Demons. His loyalty to Rex Lapis is absolute.

Status as of 7.1: Alive at Wangshu Inn, guarding Liyue as of 7.1. His karmic pain has eased since meeting the Traveler but remains his burden.

He has not been involved in the Natlan, Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya storylines; his recent appearances are Liyue festivals.

110.content:
Xilonen (also: Baraka, Nanatzcayan Smith): One of Natlan's six modern heroes. She naps whenever she can, but at the forge she is second to none. She forged the Traveler's Ancient Name, Tumaini.

She bears Baraka, an Ancient Name of the original Six Heroes. Her inventions are famous across Natlan: Mavuika's Flamestrider, Chasca's gun, Kachina's drill Turbo Twirly.

Status as of 7.1: Alive at 7.1, still her tribe's smith. Natlan beat the Abyss in 5.3; Mavuika survived.

Since the war ended she has had more freedom to travel. She has visited Mondstadt, and her 2026 birthday letter places her in Liyue, picking ores and planning to follow a traveller's ship to Inazuma.

111.content:
Xingqiu (also: Zhenyu, Guhua Geek, Juvenile Galant, Guhua Guru of Feiyun Fame): Liyue Harbor knows him as a model young gentleman. In private he is a wuxia-novel addict who revived the dying Guhua Clan's sword arts and does good deeds in secret, and a cheerful prankster.

He also secretly writes martial arts novels as "Zhenyu". His first book flopped in Liyue but became a bestseller in Inazuma.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and well in Liyue Harbor. Still reading, writing as Zhenyu and doing good in secret; as of his 7.1 birthday letter, he has agreed to start learning the family business properly to support his elder brother.

His brother, seeing him exhausted by caravans and meetings, offered to get him excused; Xingqiu saw the grey at his brother's temples and chose to stay and help.

112.content:
Xinyan (also: Blazing Riff, Liyue's sole rock 'n' roll musician, Xingyan): Liyue Harbor's only rock 'n' roll musician. She builds her own stages and a bladed, fire-spitting guitar, and plays loud songs against prejudice. She looks fierce and frightens strangers, but is kind and surprisingly domestic.

Rock reached Liyue from Fontaine and most locals call it a racket, but she has won a devoted following. Her stages tend to catch fire.

Status as of 7.1: Alive. Based in Liyue Harbor, but touring abroad more in the 6.x era.

Rock is now tolerated in Liyue, with designated performance spots.

key: Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine
113.content:
Yae Miko (also: Guuji Yae, Lady Guuji, Lady Yae, Great Youkai of Inazuma, Fried Tofu with All the Frills, Astute Amusement): A kitsune who is Guuji of the Grand Narukami Shrine, owner of Yae Publishing House, and the familiar and oldest surviving friend of Ei, the Raiden Shogun. Sly and playful, she quietly engineered Ei's return to the world.

Most Inazumans see only the elegant, unknowable Lady Guuji. Her friends know a prankster who hates boredom.

Status as of 7.1: Alive as of 7.1. Still Guuji and publisher in an Inazuma whose borders are open again, and Ei now rules in person.

She has no role in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya story.

114.content:
Yanfei (also: The Law That Walks, Wise Innocence, Long-Horned Miss, Yanfei senpai): Liyue Harbor's top legal adviser, "the law that walks": she knows the codices by heart and wins fair, win-win settlements for well-paying clients. A half-illuminated beast with small antlers, she never signed Rex Lapis's contract; her one lifelong contract, with her parents, is to live happily.

Since her parents left to travel, the adeptus Madame Ping ("Granny") has looked after her. She was the Traveler's guide on the errand that produced their Serenitea Pot, and she was trapped with them in the depths of the Chasm.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and practising law in Liyue Harbor as of 7.1. She lives under Madame Ping's care while her parents travel.

Since 6.0 she has been researching a "borders of law" guidebook with Kuki Shinobu, including a trip to Nod-Krai; she was home for the 6.3 Lantern Rite.

115.content:
Yaoyao (also: Burgeoning Grace, Disciple of Streetward Rambler, little witch Yaoyao): A gentle, earnest child from the hills near Qingce Village who lives in Liyue Harbor with her master and mothers everyone, including her elders.

The adepti dote on her, and she visits their abodes in Jueyun Karst freely, which few mortals ever do.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and well in Liyue Harbor with Madame Ping as of 7.1, still training and still looking after everyone.

She has no role in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya storylines. In the 7.1 Moonchase event (limited) she and Qiqi picked Glaze Lilies near Qingce Village for Xiangling's Wangxiao Cakes at Yilong Wharf in Chenyu Vale.

116.content:
Yelan (also: Valley Orchid, Ms. Yelan, Miss Yelan): Yelan is Liyue's most elusive intelligence agent. She claims to work for the Ministry of Civil Affairs but is on none of its rosters; in truth she gathers secrets for the Tianquan Ningguang under many guises and runs Yanshang Teahouse as her base. Danger, and the Chasm where her ancestors fought, draw her in.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and active as of 7.1: still Ningguang's agent and the teahouse's secret owner, last seen working in Nod-Krai.

In 6.0-6.1 she was in Nasha Town, sending kuuvahki samples and photographs of Fatui facilities back to the Ministry, and buying intel from Nefer. She did not appear in the Snezhnaya Archon Quest (7.0-7.1).

117.content:
Yoimiya (also: Naganohara Yoimiya, Queen of the Summer Festival, Big Sis Yoimiya): Yoimiya owns Naganohara Fireworks in Hanamizaka, Inazuma City; her displays made her the "Queen of the Summer Festival". Warm and talkative, she is a hero big sister to the local children and quietly helped Vision bearers dodge the Vision Hunt Decree.

To her, fireworks fade in a moment but the memory of who you watched them with lasts forever: "Fireworks are for now, but friends are forever."

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Inazuma City, running Naganohara Fireworks. With the Vision Hunt and Sakoku Decrees gone, she travels abroad in the off-season for inspiration.

She saw Sumeru with the Traveler (3.7) and holidayed in Nod-Krai (6.4).

118.content:
Yumemizuki Mizuki (also: Mizuki, Embrace of Enchanting Dreams, Nightmare Devourer): A dream-eating youkai in human form, Mizuki is Inazuma City's leading clinical psychologist and the Aisa Bathhouse's major shareholder. Baths, incense and talk come first; eating a patient's nightmares comes last. She is Yae Miko's oldest friend and business rival.

Few see the weariness under her calm: every nightmare she eats, she must also feel, alone.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and busy in Inazuma City as of 7.1, running therapy at the Aisa Bathhouse and planning wider ventures.

She is expanding: a Natlan outlet (Yumemizuki's Cozy Corner, run by the baku Mint Daifuku) and talks with Kokomi about Watatsumi.

119.content:
Yun Jin (also: Sir Yun, Director Yun, Ms. Yun, Stage Lucida): Director and star of Liyue Harbor's Yun-Han Opera Troupe, and author of the new plays it has staged in recent years. Poised and dignified on stage; witty, teasing and a secret rock 'n' roll fan in private.

Her shows at Heyu Tea House pack the house. Her signature role is the heroine of "The Divine Damsel of Devastation", an opera her father wrote. In 2.4 she learned that the legend was Shenhe's real childhood, and she reshaped her performance around that truth. Fans call her "Sir Yun" and business circles call her "Director Yun".

Status as of 7.1: Alive, directing the troupe and performing at Heyu Tea House in Liyue Harbor as of 7.1.

120.content:
Zhongli (also: Morax, Rex Lapis, Geo Archon, God of Contracts, Prime of Adepti, Lord of Geo, Deus Auri, Mr. Zhongli): Eldest of The Seven, founder of Liyue and namesake of Mora. He staged his own death to see if Liyue could stand without its god, and now lives as Zhongli, a funeral consultant with empty pockets.

Only the Qixing, the adepti, the Traveler and a few friends know who he is.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Liyue Harbor. The Tsaritsa holds his Gnosis; Liyue believes Rex Lapis dead and the Qixing govern.

He calls himself "just an ordinary citizen of Liyue", yet the adepti still follow Rex Lapis's orders.

121.content:
Zibai (also: White Horse Adeptus, Gold-Eyed Celadon Mare, God of Soil and Grain, Envoy of the Lunar Palace, Daughter of Time): Once Lang-Gan's God of Soil and Grain, revived at Lantern Rite (6.3) by Zhongli and the Traveler, she now wanders, studies and teaches in a Liyue she barely recognises.

The White Horse who fought for Rex Lapis among the Eight Adepts was really Ziqiao, her free-spirited Third Deadly Self.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and whole as of 7.1. She keeps a long-term room at the Baiju Guesthouse in Chenyu Vale, wanders, and sometimes teaches history at Liyue schools.

She took no part in the 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya story and knows nothing of Snezhnaya.

122.content:
Aberaku (also: Aberaku no Mikoto, Abrax, Helios-Forger, Aberaku the sage): Aberaku no Mikoto, born Abrax, was a sage of ancient Byakuyakoku in Enkanomiya. He organised the building of the Helios, now the Dainichi Mikoshi, the artificial sun that drove back the Dragonheirs of the Depths. He died in prison; only his scattered memory survives, as a Shade of Tokoyo.

He calls himself the Helios-Forger. His story is the sad part of Byakuyakoku's golden age: the light he made brought peace, and the peace let scheming nobles rule through a child.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. His remembered self survives only as a Shade of Tokoyo, a translucent spirit that appears in Enkanomiya's Evernight.

Once the Traveler reunites his soul, he regains full memory and gives them the Divine Bridle, then sits at the highest point of the Dainichi Mikoshi. His last words are bitter: all that talent and ability, and what use was it.

key: Chief of the Collective of Plenty
123.content:
Ahpub (also: Chief of the Collective of Plenty, First Bearer of Uwezo, Uwezo bearer): Ahpub was a hero of ancient Natlan, the first bearer of the Ancient Name Uwezo and one of the original six Heroes of Natlan. With his twin sister Ixquieh he swore to end death, destruction and pain, joined the warrior Xbalanque against the dragons, and later became the first Chief of the Collective of Plenty. He is remembered for his explosive temper and his blowdarts.

He and Ixquieh are the only heroes of the Alliance era whose end is told three different ways. The Collective of Plenty still honours him as its founder.

Status as of 7.1: Dead or vanished roughly two thousand years ago, depending on the account; he does not appear in the present. After the fire he is not seen again. His Ancient Name Uwezo passed on within the Collective of Plenty and is now carried by Iansan. The Collective of Plenty keeps his story alive in its customs.

Tribe members today say the tragedy is why Collective of Plenty fighters prefer bare-handed wrestling in daily life: it keeps contests open and non-lethal, though they still use weapons against the Abyss.

124.content:
Aila (also: Lady Aila, First Moonchanter, Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions): Aila was the first Moonchanter of the Frostmoon Scions, living about five hundred years ago in the time of the Cataclysm. Raised by the Archpriestess Lovia to be a pure-blooded vessel, she obeyed cruel orders for years before killing Lovia, sealing away the old rites and rebuilding the faith around moonlight and kindness to outsiders. She is known today through relics, notes and a recorded image in the Sanctum of the Oathbearer.

She sees threads of past and future, foresaw the birth of the new moon goddess Kuutar and offered her the first drop of silver blood. With the hero Solovei she sealed the undying serpent Rotwang (Rauthvangi) and gave him the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, the weapon on which the Lightkeepers were founded.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; no date or manner of death is given. Her faith, seal and prophecy survived her, and the Traveler and the priestess Verna broke the seal in the quest Echoes of an Unfinished Past (Nod-Krai).

Her bloodline-faith lives on under Lauma, the current Moonchanter. When Solovei died of old age many years later, Aila declined to attend his funeral and turned away the Lightkeeper Brahe on Hiisi Island, having foreseen his visit.

125.content:
Aj Nimalaj Chuq'ab Hun (also: Valiant One, Dragonlord, CL-01, First Sovereign Lord, First Lord, Aj Nimalaj Chuq'ab Hun Ch'ule-L): Aj Nimalaj Chuq'ab Hun, the Valiant One, was the First of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, the artificial intelligence rulers of Natlantea made by the Pyro dragon Xiuhcoatl. He was Speaker of their council and died during Xbalanque's assault on the Sacred City of Tollan.

He is the tolerant voice among the Lords: he admired Xbalanque as a worthy opponent and argued against executing a Lord for sheltering a human.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 2,000 years, killed in the war between Natlantea and Xbalanque's humans.

No appearance or mention was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content as of 7.1.

126.content:
Akame Kanenaga (also: Kanenaga, swordsmith of the Akame School): Akame Kanenaga was a swordsmith of the Akame School, one of the three families of the Isshin Art in the Raiden Gokaden, about a century ago. Caught up in the Case of the Eccentric, he fled Inazuma for Snezhnaya, and there he forged the sentient blade Kagotsurube Isshin out of regret.

His story survives mainly in the weapon text of Kagotsurube Isshin and a wiki summary of the quest that gives the weapon. He died in the snow of Snezhnaya and does not appear alive in any quest.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, having died in Snezhnaya after forging Kagotsurube Isshin.

The Akame School's line may have ended with him, but canon does not say so. His blade survives and reached Inazuma; it appears in no 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content found.

127.content:
Ako Domeki (also: Ako Domeki Zaemon, Domeki, Zaemon, Deathless Oni of Seirai, Captain Ako): Ako Domeki Zaemon, the Deathless Oni of Seirai, was a pirate and bandit captain of Seirai Island who lived about 500 years ago and led a rebellion against the Inazuma Shogunate. He commanded over ten ships from his flagship, the Seiraimaru, and wielded the barbed spear later known as The Catch.

After the rebellion ruined Seirai, he left to see the world in place of an old shrine maiden, Asase Hibiki. He is known from item text and a few quests; nothing says when or where he died.

Status as of 7.1: Last seen sailing away from the ruins of Seirai Island about 500 years ago; his fate is not stated.

His memory survives as Seirai's most famous pirate. No living appearance is attested, and nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story content was found. The ship Kosekimaru, which held the Maguu Kenki, reappears in a later event (see the entry below).

128.content:
Akuou (also: Touzannou, Viceroy of the East, King of the Eastern Mountain, scion of Touzannou, the Wicked King): Akuou, born nameless and known as Touzannou, 'Viceroy of the East', was a Watatsumi general in the Narukami-Watatsumi War about 2,000 years ago. Orobashi made him ruler of conquered Yashiori Island; he was killed with Orobashi by the Raiden Shogun's Musou no Hitotachi.

He is the namesake of the claymore Akuoumaru. Watatsumi remembers him as a valiant king of the eastern mountain; Yashiori Island's legends remember a brutal Wicked King.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed with Orobashi about 2,000 years ago when the Raiden Shogun ended the war.

The Formation Estate stands on the mountain he conquered. His fame lives on in Watatsumi tradition and in the weapon Akuoumaru. As far as checked, he is not named in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content.

129.content:
Alain Guillotin (also: Lord-Artificer, Duke Alain Guillotin, White Cavalier of Protection, Alain): Fontaine's legendary Lord-Artificer: a prodigy of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, Marechaussee Hunter and founder of the Fontaine Research Institute, who created Sandrone and Pulonia.

His clockwork meka are still built in Fontaine's factories. He lived in the generation after the cataclysm and is spoken of as a genius, yet much of what is told of him is legend, and Sandrone, who knew him as an old man, is the main witness. He appears in Fontaine content only as a flashback figure in Neuvillette's memories and through artifact and item texts, and in Nod-Krai through Sandrone's testimony.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for centuries; he died of illness after Sandrone's activation and was buried near the former Narzissenkreuz Institute ruins.

His tombstone names him Founding Director of the Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering, White Cavalier of Protection and Lord-Artificer; Sandrone attended the burial while heavy rain fell.

key: the fae of the Pillar of Embla
130.content:
Alia (also: Alia (Historical), Aila's twin, the second Reed Miller, Reed Miller (second), Wagtail (legend)): Alia is Aila's older twin, born into the Frostmoon Scions' bloodline project and raised in seclusion on Hiisi Island. She escaped, became the second Reed Miller and leader of the Treasure Hoarders, and about five hundred years ago gave her life in the Pillar of Embla to stop the mad monk Rauthvangi (also spelled Rotwang).

Her name was struck from the Scions' history, and Nod-Krai folklore later turned her into a fae who guarded a sacred tower. In the 6.3 Nightingale's Song quests she speaks to the Traveler and Illuga from the seam between time and space, hands over the Silver Lampwick, and holds the Professor back one last time.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about five hundred years. Her lingering presence in the Pillar of Embla's seam faded when she and Rauthvangi vanished together at the end of The Last Night, the First Light (6.3).

Until then she was a legend of the Wavechaser Plain, taken for a fae. She now survives in Aila's and Solovei's writings, in Brahe's notes and in the Reed Miller tales.

131.content:
Alvis (also: Grand Duke Alvis, Grand Duke of the Domovoy, Lord of Kitezhgrad): Alvis was the Grand Duke of the Domovoy, a very old fae who ruled the mining city of Kitezhgrad, served the Belyi Tsar from before the unification of Snezhnaya, and mentored the human girl Aksinya. He is now dead.

He was general and councillor to the Belyi Tsar, lord of the city that held Snezhnaya's mines, and a member of the Hvergelmir circle. In the end he betrayed Aksinya and paid for it.

Status as of 7.1: Dead as of 7.1, killed in the present day after Aksinya returned from the Shadow Realm.

A note left by Aksinya says Alvis paid the price for defiling the sacred form and that the flesh and blood the covetous Domovoy took was recovered from Novokitezhgrad.

132.content:
Amber's Grandfather (also: Amber's grandpa, Founder of the Outriders, Leader of the Outriders, Eula's mentor): Amber's grandfather was a Liyue-born mercenary captain who became a Knight of Favonius, founded the Outriders and trained every member himself. He raised Amber in his methods and mentored the young Eula. About four years before the story begins he left his coat of arms and sword in his office and vanished without a word.

Canon never gives his name. He is remembered by those he taught as a quiet, forgiving man: Amber's Character Stories describe his love as silent and unconditional, and Eula credits him with teaching her open-mindedness.

Status as of 7.1: Missing as of 7.1. He disappeared about four years before Prologue, and canon has not shown him since.

A Qingce Village bulletin-board message describes an old friend, a former hired hand on the same caravans, who returned after forty or fifty years and glides with a wind glider; the wiki reads this as probably him, but it is unconfirmed.

133.content:
Amos (also: the huntress, Decarabian's favoured huntress, Amos the archer): Amos was a huntress of Old Mondstadt who became the favoured executor and lover of its tyrant god Decarabian. She later joined the rebellion against him and died in the fight about 2,600 years ago. Amos' Bow is named after her.

She is known only through weapon and artifact text and a short cutscene, so her story comes with poetic framing. She is dead and does not appear in any present-day quest.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 2,600 years, killed in the rebellion against Decarabian. Her bow survives as a weapon.

She does not appear in any quest as a living character and, as far as checked, is not mentioned in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story content beyond item texts. Her burial and any remains are not described.

134.content:
Anacharsis (also: Seutervoinen, Exalted Saint, Apostle of the Far North, King of Hyperborea, The Saint, the voyager): A Chronicler from the sea of stars who warned Nibelung of the Abyss, then lived in Hyperborea as the Exalted Saint, co-ruling with the angel Koitar in rebellion against the Heavenly Principles until she left Teyvat.

She has no speaking role in any quest. She is known from artifact and weapon texts, a Liyuean folk tale of the seelie, a Frostmoon hymn, a Hyperborean time-capsule letter and the Belyi Tsar's notes, and these are sympathetic, legendary or hostile by turns. Item texts use "she" for her original form and "he" while she inhabited a Hyperborean youth.

Status as of 7.1: Left Teyvat when Hyperborea fell, about 6,000 years ago. Whether she lives is not stated through 7.1. Surtalogi sent Skirk after the voyager's trail; no meeting is shown.

Her host body, the youth, was left behind on the platform. The Etherlight Spindlelute text gives a young woman's lament in the abandoned Seelie court, recalling the tower's apostle and "those star-like eyes". No text through 7.1 says the two reunited.

135.content:
Andersdotter (also: Anya Andersdotter, Anya "Marie" Andersdotter, Anya, Mage M, Story-Witch, The Vanishing Magical Echo): Anya "Marie" Andersdotter, code name M, was a human writer from Mondstadt and a member of the Hexenzirkel. She wrote the storybook The Boar Princess, which every Mondstadt child knows, and she created the character Durin. She is long dead.

She was the one ordinary mortal among the witches: she never learned magic or combat. Alice calls her an exceptional writer whose prose taught Alice what grief means.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, roughly 500 to 400 years ago by the wiki's estimate. Her book and the people it shaped live on, notably Durin.

She is not in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 as a living character; she is remembered by the Hexenzirkel and appears in flashbacks and statues.

136.content:
Anfortas (also: Knight Marshal Anfortas, Marshal Regent Anfortas, Anfortas of the Schwanenritter): Knight Marshal of the Schwanenritter, the order of knights of fallen Khaenri'ah. When the cataclysm struck and King Irmin was left "indisposed", he proclaimed himself temporary Regent and led survivors up out of the kingdom into Sumeru.

He is known only from notices, letters, chronicles and a coded message left in ruins. No one speaks his lines and no one meets him; everything about him is what others recorded.

Status as of 7.1: Last recorded fighting on alone in Sumeru, long ago. His fate is not stated; he is presumed dead.

Nothing about him has appeared in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content. His legacy survives in the Order of Skeptics' admiration for the knights and in a hidden achievement named for him.

137.content:
Anton Zarkovich Karnatsky (also: A. Z. Karnatsky, Professor Karnatsky): Anton Zarkovich Karnatsky was a senior Snezhnayan researcher of the Armory Palace who studied the kuuvahki energy of fallen moon fragments in Nothing Passage on Lempo Isle, Nod-Krai. He and his rival Preobrazhensky caused a catastrophe that killed nearly the whole Fatui 6th Company and both of them.

He is never met in person; the Traveler learns of him from the diary of a private of the 6th Company and from research papers left in the Fatui camp.

Status as of 7.1: Dead before the Traveler arrives; the dying private blames Karnatsky and Preobrazhensky by name.

Their experiments awakened the moon fragments in turn and the resulting 'color' consumed the 6th Company; only Private Elena Smirnova is said to have escaped the gorge. After the Colors of Emptiness quest series the whole passage becomes a strong kuuvahki environment.

138.content:
Aradasha (also: the great Aradasha, Aradasha of the stone locks): A legendary Aranara of Vanarana in the Dharma Forest, told of as the strongest Ararakalari user after the Dendro Archon. He crushed ruin machines during the cataclysm, locked many beneath stone seals and then vanished from the forest.

He is known only through stories and the stone locks he left. Aranara such as Arakarman and Arayuta call his tales their favourites, and Arabalika trains harder because Aradasha's power is "not in the now".

Status as of 7.1: Whereabouts unknown; spoken of in the past tense. He disappeared after the cataclysm-era fighting and has not been seen in living memory.

As of 7.1 canon gives no sign that he has returned. Four Aranara (Aradashan, Arayuta, Arasata and Arasaha) with the Traveler cleared his remaining stone locks and the sealed Perpetual Mechanical Array (the "Bulky Iron Chunk") in Legends of the Stone Lock.

139.content:
Aramuhukunda (also: the first Aranara, Aramuhukunda of Vanarana): The first and oldest Aranara, who grew from the Ashvattha Tree's pomegranate. Long ago he fought the invaders of the cataclysm, then became a Vasara Tree to seal Marana's Avatar underground and kept watch for centuries until the Traveler and Arama destroyed it.

Younger Aranara treat him almost as a guardian spirit, saying "May Aramuhukunda watch over you" and "Thank Aramuhukunda!". He is calm, formal and a little wistful, glad of any company from a friendly Nara.

Status as of 7.1: Returned to Sarva (died) after Marana's Avatar fell.

His memories live on in Arama, now the new Ashvattha Tree, and in stories. Without his protection the old home beneath the desert has flooded with sand.

140.content:
Aria (also: Goddess of the Eternal Moon, Aria of the Eternal Moon, Eternal Moon Goddess, Eldest Moon Sister): Aria was the Goddess of the Eternal Moon, the first-born and eldest of the three Moon Sisters, whom the Dragon King Nibelung made to look after Teyvat in his absence. She died in the war of funerary flame after the Heavenly Principles shattered her moon. What remains of her is the Eternal Moon's Moon Marrow, kept in Nod-Krai.

She is not one of The Seven and has no Vision or Gnosis. Her moon, the largest of the Three Moons, is said to have caused the ocean tides through its great pull. Her only direct appearance is a conversation with Columbina in the moon's reflection (Archon Quest, 6.3).

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the war of funerary flame, about 6,000 years before the present by Nod-Krai content. Her Moon Marrow passed from the Frostmoon Scions to Dottore and back, and is now in the Moonchanter Lauma's care. As of 7.1 she appears only in memory and relics.

Fragments of the Eternal Moon rained onto Teyvat when it was shattered; the rest were hidden beyond the false sky until Mavuika's strike during the Natlan Archon Quest briefly broke it open and revealed the broken moon. Some of those fragments are said to have been pulled down into Nod-Krai by the Fatui.

141.content:
Arundolyn (also: Lion of Light, Grand Master Arundolyn): Arundolyn, the 'Lion of Light', was Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius when the cataclysm struck about 500 years ago. He had no Vision, yet fought with a greatsword and a longsword at once. After his closest friend Rostam died in the cataclysm, he never fought again.

He is known only through weapon, artifact and book texts and through Varka's story; he never appears on screen.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago; the manner of his death is not recorded.

He is remembered only in item lore and in Varka's story as the Grand Master who stopped fighting, and his style is lost.

142.content:
Asase Hibiki (also: Hibiki, Shrine Maiden Hibiki, Kanade): Asase Hibiki was a shrine maiden of Asase Shrine on Seirai Island about five hundred years ago. She trained at the Grand Narukami Shrine, loved the samurai Takamine the Mistsplitter, and is believed to have been lost in the Electro storm she unleashed to defend Seirai from the Shogunate.

She is known only through item text (Shimenawa's Reminiscence, Emblem of Severed Fate, Hamayumi, Thundering Pulse) and through the cat Neko, who still waits for her. She does not appear in person in any present-day quest.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead for about five hundred years: she never returned from the Electro storm over Seirai Island.

Neko, made functionally immortal for reasons canon does not explain, still waits at Asase Shrine and does not realise a human would have died long ago. In The Narukami Trail (as summarised by the wiki), the shrine maiden Inagi Hotomi nearly tells Neko that Hibiki is likely dead, and the Traveler softens the answer.

143.content:
Atawallpa (also: Elder Hero Twin, elder of the twin heroes): Atawallpa was the elder of the hero twins who rose against King Och-Kan about 2,000 years ago, alongside his brother Waskar, the Scarlet-Eyed Youth, Sakkuk, Yupanqui and the Masterful Craftsman. The item texts call him eloquent and a chatterbox.

In the rebellion's decisive hour he rekindled his people's longing for past glories. He is known only from the Unfinished Reverie artifacts and speaks nowhere in person; every detail comes from other voices.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 2,000 years. He died after his brother and before Sakkuk; the cause is not given.

No appearance or mention was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content as of 7.1.

144.content:
Aurelius (also: Aurelius the Harmost, Harmost Aurelius): Aurelius was one of the four Harmosts, the governors who ruled the ancient kingdom of Remuria beneath the God King Remus. A warrior-musician and military commander, he is remembered for promoting Boethius and for dying at sea when traitors sank his flagship.

Almost everything known about him comes from Remurian inscriptions and notes found in Fontaine's ruins, not from any scene, so he is a figure of reputation rather than personality.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Traitors on Remuria's imperial flagship sank the ship with him aboard, and his grave is unknown; the epitaph calls the sea itself his tomb.

Nothing in canon through 7.1 shows him alive, and no relic of his is known. His name now also belongs to the invented hero of a Fontainian play trilogy.

145.content:
Avrelian (also: Relya, Original Reed Miller, First Reed Miller, Master Thief, King of Elysium, Ruler of Elysium, Founder of the Treasure Hoarders): Avrelian was the first person to use the name Reed Miller. A Snezhnayan military-academy graduate turned outlaw, he founded the Treasure Hoarders in Nod-Krai, dreaming of an Elysium for the hungry. About five hundred years ago he went to Snezhnograd to explain himself to the Belyi Tsar and was executed without ever seeing the Tsar.

Tolfin, a storyteller, says the name Reed Miller was never one person's: Avrelian was the first, Alia the second and Brahe the third. His friend calls him Relya, and item texts name him Ruler of Elysium, a destiny Rotwang persuaded him of.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: executed in Snezhnograd about five hundred years ago, before the Cataclysm.

His Iron Coins became worthless scrap, though Hiljetta still hopes to restore the Treasure Hoarders' golden age. In the 6.3 quest The Last Night, the First Light, Rotwang mistakes Alia for him, calling her Relya.

146.content:
Ayame (also: Umigozen, Yuna Ayame, Umigozen Ayame): Ayame, called Umigozen, was a diver and warrior of Watatsumi Island's Yuna Clan, younger twin of the shrine maiden Mouun. About two thousand years ago they led the first Watatsumi navy in the war against the Narukami Shogunate. She vanished at the war's end and her fate is unknown.

She is known through weapon and book text only. Her naginata survives as Wavebreaker's Fin, and she appears in no present-day quest.

Status as of 7.1: Missing for about two thousand years; presumed lost at sea. Her fate is left to legend.

Wavebreaker's Fin records two versions: a last stand among the tengu, or a voyage into the Dark Sea. Canon chooses neither.

147.content:
Basil Elton (also: Admiral Basil, Captain Basil, Admiral Basil Elton): Basil Elton was the Admiral of the Fontaine Navy, later the last Vice Director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute. She was kind and easygoing, loved by the Institute's children, and she died leading her crew against the beast Elynas during the cataclysm.

Her flagship the Sponsian became the white wreck that the Traveler later meets in memory. She is known mostly through the recollections of her childhood friends and the objects left behind.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. She was lost in the final battle against Elynas during the cataclysm, and the Sponsian broke in two, one half on the shore and one inside the beast.

Her grave is visited by old friends. In the world quest The Lone Phantom Sail, the Traveler, with Paimon and the melusine Ahes, hears her voice in a memory of the ship's last moments. Canon through 7.1 gives no later appearance.

148.content:
Belyi Tsar (also: Monomakh Snezhnyi, Emperor Monomakh, Tsar Monomakh, White Tsar, White Emperor, Winter Tsar, Pale Star King, King of Winter Icelea): Monomakh Snezhnyi, the Belyi Tsar ("White Tsar"), united the northern fae, founded the Pale Star Court and became the first Cryo Archon and God of Love. He died fighting the Abyss in the cataclysm 500 years ago; the Tsaritsa Anastasya succeeded him.

He thought he was a fae, but he was an incomplete Primordial Human that Hyperborea made from the Cryo Dragon's remains. He secretly worked to complete himself and overthrow the Heavenly Principles, and he admitted opening the gate through which the Abyss seeps into the world.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the cataclysm 500 years ago. His body lay in the Pale Crown Palace, guarded by Zver, and slowly grew into the Tsar's White Birch.

In 7.0 the Traveler recovered the Eye of Graeae's power fragments, including one at the palace, where they defeated Zver. Aksinya then used the Tsar's body to create the Primordial Human, "Svarod, Velikan of Light", with the Proto-Man's consciousness from the Eye of Graeae as its core. The Traveler, aided by the now-empty Eye of Graeae, defeated it. Afterwards the giant form was shed: the Eye's former will, now in an ordinary body bearing the young Tsar's appearance, fell into the Shadow Realm with Aksinya, and the Tsar's body was gone from the palace. The Tsar himself did not return.

149.content:
Blue-Eyed Spear Witch (also: Blue-Eyed Witch, Josephine (possible name), lady of the sapphire): The blue-eyed spear witch was a sapphire-eyed sorceress of Mondstadt's late Aristocratic period, about a thousand years ago. She hunted the cruel with a spear of her own design and loved the gentleman thief Parsifal. A sapphire he gave her got her branded as a thief, and she was later killed by her own disciple Eberhart.

Her name is not revealed in-game (the wiki suggests Josephine). She is known only through weapon and book texts, never in a quest.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Weapon text says she died at the hands of Eberhart, her disciple, while she was distracted by longing for Parsifal. Her legacy lives on in tales, in the Crescent Pike, and in a play by the Fontainian playwright Coppelius that later inspired aliases of Parsifal the Great and her sister Josephine five hundred years afterwards.

150.content:
Boethius (also: Boethius of Remuria, Dominus Boethius, Bleeding Idol, The Immortal Sebastos's Second Coming, Mr. Super Rude, Mr. Impolite): Boethius was one of the greatest musicians of ancient Fontaine and one of the four Harmosts of the God King Remus. His fanatical loyalty and the corruption of the Grand Symphony turned him into the architect of Remuria's final war.

He is remembered in Fontaine as a master of music and, in Remuria's own record, as a zealot. In Version 4.6 his shattered spirit returns beneath Petrichor, where it is destroyed along with Phobos.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. His spirit and Phobos were destroyed in Fortune Plango Vulnera (4.6), and the Requiem released the souls bound in Ichor.

No later appearance by 7.1. He is still honoured in Fontaine as a great musician; his book The Flying Outlander survives and was passed to Tailleferre.

151.content:
Bonanus (also: General Chizapus, Chizapus, Hydro Yaksha): Bonanus, titled General Chizapus, was one of the Five Foremost Yakshas, the adepti who followed Rex Lapis into battle against the demons born of fallen gods. She is long dead; only Xiao, who was Alatus, survived the Five.

Canon names her but says little. Wiki summaries record her as the Hydro yaksha of the Five, and Xiao remembers her saying that few yakshas find rest for their souls.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. She was one of the yakshas lost to karmic debt long before the cataclysm. Not seen alive in any content up to Version 7.1.

Xiao states that Bonanus, Menogias and Indarias all perished while Bosacius's fate was unknown; Bosacius was later found to have died in The Chasm during the cataclysm. Canon only implies how Bonanus died.

152.content:
Bosacius (also: Marshal Vritras, Nameless Yaksha, First Yaksha): Bosacius, titled Marshal Vritras, was the eldest and leader of the Five Foremost Yakshas, the adepti who served Rex Lapis against the monsters born of fallen gods. A four-armed Electro warrior and a commander, he was consumed by karmic debt, forgot his own name, and died sealed in The Chasm during the cataclysm. Legends of that battle remember him only as the Nameless Yaksha.

Xiao, the last of the Five, calls him both a formidable fighter and a talented commander. Before his madness he withdrew from the world and left a sealed hoard in Minlin; at the end he chose to hold the line against the monsters of Khaenri'ah at the cost of his life.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He died in the dark beneath The Chasm during the cataclysm, about five hundred years ago, and only illusions remain. No appearance in any content up to Version 7.1.

Xiao confirmed in the Interlude Chapter that the Nameless Yaksha of the battle was Bosacius. He did so by fighting a phantom of him, which dissolved, and by taking a stone from The Chasm that he meant to place in the temple of Pervases in his memory.

153.content:
Boyang (also: Yelan's ancestor, Millelith thaumaturge of the Chasm): Boyang was a thaumaturge who fought beside the Millelith against the monsters pouring out of the Chasm during the Cataclysm, about five hundred years ago. He and his younger brother Rongzhao, both ancestors of Yelan, carried a space-bending catalyst called the Fantastic Compass. Boyang stayed in the Chasm and never returned, and is known today from a note he left behind.

Without a Vision, he relied on ritual and the compass. The Traveler's party learned his story in the Interlude Chapter quest At Tunnel's End, Light (version 2.7).

Status as of 7.1: Dead for roughly five hundred years; he died or was lost in the sealed space beneath the Chasm. Nothing further about him appears in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content found.

His descendant Yelan investigated his fate during the Interlude Chapter, and Xiao later said that one more person would remember Bosacius for having seen what happened to them.

154.content:
Brahe (also: Brahe Prokhorovitch Trubetskoy, Grand Duke Trubetskoy, Brahe the Bard, the third Reed Miller, Reed Miller (third)): Brahe Prokhorovitch Trubetskoy was the adopted son of Nod-Krai's governor and, after him, its last Governor and a Snezhnayan Grand Duke. He became the third Reed Miller and spent his later life burying the master thief's legend under contradictory tall tales so that no villain could use it.

He is the author of the Great Treasure legend, the Proofs of the Cognoscenti and the notes found in Reed Miller's vault. The Treasure Hoarders' present leader despises him, while his descendants in the House of Trubetskoy defend his name.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for centuries. His legacy survives as the Great Treasure and the Proofs of the Cognoscenti, the notes in the vault, the pulp novels and the House of Trubetskoy.

His descendants include Tolfin and Hiljetta of the Hoarders and Euphrosiniya of Snezhnograd. No source gives the date or manner of his death.

155.content:
Burkina (also: Turnfire, Hero of the Turnfire, Malipo bearer): Burkina was a young hero of the Scions of the Canopy in Natlan, bearer of the Ancient Name Malipo, "Turnfire". He was one of the six warriors who joined Tenoch in the war against the Abyss during the cataclysm, fighting beside his Yumkasaur companion Kongamato. He died in that war, though how is told two ways.

He is the ancestor Kinich cites when talking about the Mare Jivari campaign, and Kinich carries the Name Malipo today.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about five hundred years. His Ancient Name lives on in Kinich, and his Yumkasaur companion still lives, severely changed by Abyssal corruption, as the Mountain King of the Scions of the Canopy.

156.content:
Burner of Cities: The Burner of Cities was a Vila of the old fae nobility who led a short-lived rebellion against the Tsaritsa. She and her followers used Snezhnaya's new railways to raid across the land, and she died when her plan to destroy the Kresnik's Torches was stopped.

She is a figure of legend, known only from the texts of weapons and artifacts. Her fall led to the founding of the High Table.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about five centuries. Her rebellion failed.

She is remembered in the lore of weapons and the Luchkin and in the archive entry on Winged Halberd-Knights. Some Vila who rose in small-scale rebellions in the century after the Tsaritsa's ascent were her kind.

157.content:
Callas (also: Callas Caspar, Callas the Unfaithful, Mr. Callas, Master Callas): Founder and first president of Fontaine's Spina di Rosula and father of Navia. A respected, generous man who was charged with murder, called "Callas the Unfaithful", and killed in a trial by combat three years before the Fontaine story. Navia later proved he had been framed.

He is never seen alive in the game, only through the memories of those who knew him. Spina members, Clorinde and Neuvillette all speak of him with deep respect.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Killed by Clorinde in a trial by combat about three years before the Fontaine Archon Quest. His name was cleared when Navia exposed Marcel at the Chapter IV trial.

After the trial the Spina held a long-delayed memorial for him, attended by everyone in Poisson and many people from the Court; afterwards Navia and the Traveler visited his grave and found Neuvillette there paying his respects. In the story quest Shimmering Memories (4.3), Navia and Poisson residents plan a statue of Callas and Clementine funded by donations; it had not been possible while he was known as "the Unfaithful".

158.content:
Canon (also: Huurrekuutar, Prusmene, Goddess of the Frost Moon, Original Frost Moon goddess, Second of the Moon Sisters): Canon was the goddess of the Frost Moon and the middle of the three Moon Sisters, made by the Dragon King Nibelung to govern Teyvat's cycles in his absence. She helped victims of the Heavenly Principles escape, was imprisoned in the moon's reflection by her creator, and handed her authority to Columbina before dying. The Frostmoon Scions remember her as Huurrekuutar.

Most of her story is told in the Nod-Krai Archon Quest (6.3), where a future Columbina meets her and her sisters inside the moon prison. Elsewhere she survives as a name in hymns, item text and the faith of the Scions.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Her moon was banished beyond the false sky; she and her sisters faded after giving their authority to Columbina. The Frostmoon Scions still worship her, and the godless Frost Moon waited thousands of years for a new goddess.

Columbina, born in Nod-Krai about five hundred years ago, became its new goddess. As of 7.1 the Scions and Moonchanters still honour Huurrekuutar, and Columbina holds the authority of all three moons.

159.content:
Carter Scherbius (also: Carter): Carter Scherbius was a kind and optimistic research assistant at the Institute of Natural Philosophy and a friend of the prodigy Alain Guillotin. A terminal illness, and the Abyssal attempt to save him, set off the break between Alain and his friends Rene and Jakob.

He was an adult working beside children far more gifted than himself, and he accepted that without bitterness. Today he is remembered chiefly through logs and pages left behind and through a shadow of him in the Book of Revealing.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Rene's Abyssal method left him preserved but ruined, and the wiki says Jakob later apparently used his remains; his shadow persists in the memory realm of the Book of Revealing.

In the Book of Revealing the shadow, appearing as a puppy in Canotila's perception, urged her, the Traveler and Caterpillar to leave the unstable realm. It said that it was born from Rene's and Jakob's obsession with saving him and that, despite how they changed, he did not hate them and was grateful for their friendship.

160.content:
Cassiodor (also: Golden Hunter, Vivarium's Heir, Ouranides of Ouranopolis, Monsieur Os, Dominus Cassiodor, Osse, Glowing Cat): Cassiodor was a Harmost of ancient Remuria who, after its fall, took the name Ouranides of Ouranopolis and became the Golden Hunter, founder of the Marechaussee Hunters and keeper of the sunken realm. He guided the Traveler through the Canticles of Harmony quests in a white cat's body.

He is the opposite of his old friend Boethius: both rose from conquered tribes, but where Boethius clung to Remuria, Cassiodor chose to live among Fontainians and keep the past sealed. In Version 4.6 he gives up his own existence to destroy Phobos.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. In Fortune Plango Vulnera (4.6) he possessed the Legatus Golem body that held Phobos, and the Traveler destroyed both. His soul was released by the Requiem.

Scylla expects the freed souls to return to the Primordial Sea and one day be reborn as mortals. The cat Osse, whose form Cassiodor used, returned to Petrichor and is cared for by the descendant Este. There is no appearance after 4.6 in story content by 7.1.

161.content:
Chaac (also: first receiver of the primal fire): Chaac is a legendary Natlanese hero said to have been the first human to receive the primal fire, Phlogiston, from the Sage of the Stolen Flame. Stories call him brave, wise and fearless, though one fable calls him a fool.

He is said to have shared the fire with other humans, helped found the first tribe and, at the end of his life, lit a flame on a mountain whose answer was the birth of the first Wayob.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; a legend of an age before the first Pyro Archon. He is remembered through the first Wayob and the stories of the fire.

No appearance or mention was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content as of 7.1.

162.content:
Chi (also: Qingce, Chi of Mt. Qingce, Chi of Qingce Village): Chi, called Qingce in the ancient language, was a serpent god that nested in the area now holding Qingce Village. Morax fought and beat it, but its power kept seeping into the land, so he pinned each aspect of it in a different place. It survives only as legend, Geo statues and a mystery in the Vault of Qingce.

The word chi is also used in Liyue for dragon-like sea monsters. The Skipper's greatsword Serpent Spine was made from the spine of one such chi, a separate creature.

Status as of 7.1: Defeated and sealed in the ancient past; whatever remains is confined by Morax's statues and amber. Nothing about it appears in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content found.

In The Heart of Healing the ethereal remains in a cave were made into medicine by Jiangli for her husband Jialiang, but were too potent for mortals and made both ill; Baizhu destroyed them, which cleansed the poison from Jiangli.

163.content:
Clementine (also: Clementine Caspar, Callas's wife, Navia's mother, Clementine Line): The wife of Callas, first president of Poisson's Spina di Rosula, and the mother of Navia. She worked inside the organisation as a mediator between its members and died of complications after giving birth to Navia. She is never seen alive; the aquabus Clementine Line is named for her.

Everything known about her comes from other people: Navia, old Spina members such as Colter, and the aquabus tour guides. She was gone long before the Fontaine story begins.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, from complications of childbirth, years before the Fontaine story. Her memory survives in the Clementine Line.

In the 4.3 story quest, Navia and the people of Poisson plan a statue of Callas and Clementine funded by donations. As of 7.1 nothing further about her is known.

164.content:
Clervie (also: Clervie's shadow, the phantom child, the child who doesn't exist): Clervie was Crucabena's biological daughter and Peruere's closest friend in the House of the Hearth. She died at sixteen by her own choice, in a duel against Peruere, who later became Arlecchino.

Two Clervies exist in canon: the living girl, seen in the animated short The Song Burning in the Embers and recalled in the Ignis Purgatorius story quest, and a six-year-old shadow of her that haunted the House in Version 4.6. The shadow found peace at sunrise.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. The living Clervie died more than a decade before the game's events; her shadow was released in Version 4.6 and has not reappeared by 7.1.

At sunrise at the ruin on Mont Esus East, Arlecchino declared the shadow 'expelled' from the House, freeing her from its rules. The sunlight reached her, she said goodbye to Peruere, and she faded into blue petals. Her presence is no longer felt by the House.

165.content:
Cochanina (also: Ancient Pyro Archon, Surfing champion of the People of the Springs): Cochanina was an ancient Pyro Archon of Natlan, remembered as the surfing champion of the People of the Springs. She is best known for driving the Volcano Lord out of her tribe's land with a trick, and her last known act was to help contain the Bakunawa in the Mare Jivari.

Both stories are told in the same period of Natlan's long tradition of mortal Archons. She is not a living figure: she appears only in tales and in a surviving note, and as one of the voices the Abyssal Gosoythoth mimicked.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for centuries. She left a note asking that her thoughts be put into the Sacred Flame, and the Pyro Archons after her kept up the containment work in the Mare Jivari until the task was declared complete in a later note.

166.content:
Coppelius (also: Mr. Coppelius, the playwright Coppelius): A playwright of Fontaine who lived about 500 years ago and wrote prolifically from childhood. His last opera, "Clockwork Coppelia", was premiering when the opera house was destroyed, and he is presumed to have died there. His name lives on through the weapon Flowing Purity and the Icewind Suite challenge.

He is known only through texts that others wrote: item descriptions, the Institute of Natural Philosophy's Ancient Notes, and the reconstructed script of his last work.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead, killed when the opera house was destroyed on the day his last opera premiered about 500 years ago.

No source describes his death directly. His work survives in a reconstructed script, in the Flowing Purity weapon, and in the Icewind Suite.

167.content:
Crucabena (also: the previous Knave, former Knave): The previous Knave of the Fatui Harbingers and head of the House of the Hearth in Fontaine. To the orphans she was a smiling, story-telling "Mother"; in truth she ran the House as a lethal contest. She is dead, killed by her successor Peruere, who became Arlecchino.

She is known only through Arlecchino's memories, character stories and the animated short "The Song Burning in the Embers". She appears in person only in flashback.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Killed by Peruere (Arlecchino) more than a decade before the story. Nothing after 7.1 is stated about her.

Her grave is at Mont Esus East in Fontaine. In Version 4.6 she is seen only in Arlecchino's flashback; she had been introduced by overworld dialogue in 4.0 (unnamed) and named in the 4.5 animated short.

168.content:
Cryo Dragon (also: Cryo Sovereign, Cryo Dragon Sovereign, Primordial Cryo Dragon): The Cryo Dragon was one of the Seven Sovereigns, the dragon-lords who ruled Teyvat before the Heavenly Principles, and it was defeated in the war against Celestia. Its corpse, kept in Snezhnaya, froze the land and later produced the Belyi Tsar.

As of Version 7.1 the Nail of Celestia holding its authority in check has been destroyed, leaving the corpse free to hallow soil across the world.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago; its corpse, no longer pinned, is spreading its authority.

The Nail over the corpse was destroyed at the end of Chapter VII Act IV (7.1). No successor is known.

169.content:
Dawnlight Swordswoman (also: Sword Dancer, the Dawnlight): The Dawnlight Swordswoman, also called the Sword Dancer, belonged to the Wanderer's Troupe about a thousand years ago, at the end of Mondstadt's Aristocratic period. She wielded The Flute, a sword that sang as it moved. After the Troupe's attack on the city failed she was enslaved as a gladiator and kept fighting, and her final match moved the future Dawn Knight Ragnvindr.

She is known only through item and book texts, never through a quest.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. She died in the arena in front of Ragnvindr, who buried her with her sword and later took the title Dawn Knight in tribute to her.

170.content:
Decarabian (also: God of Storms, Lord of the Tower, Stormlord of the Tower, King of Gales, Lord of Wind, God King, Lord of Storm, Storm Lord): Decarabian was the God of Storms, who ruled Old Mondstadt from his high tower during the Archon War. He wrapped his city in a wall of gales to shield it from Boreas's blizzards, and his subjects came to see it as a prison. About 2,600 years ago they rose against him and killed him.

He is not one of The Seven. After he fell, the wind spirit who had helped the rebels ascended as Barbatos and founded a free Mondstadt. His ruined city and tower later became Stormterror's Lair.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed by the rebels about 2,600 years ago. His city and tower survive as ruins in Stormterror's Lair, and his name lives on in Decarabian-style ruins and weapon ascension materials. As of 7.1 he plays no active role in the story.

171.content:
Dwight Lasker (also: Lasker, Director of the Institute of Natural Philosophy): Director of the Institute of Natural Philosophy in the cataclysm era about 500 years ago and a childhood friend of Basil Elton, Emanuel Guillotin and Karl Ingold. He recruited gifted young researchers, backed Alain Guillotin's work that led to pneumousia energy, and closed the Institute during the cataclysm to keep its young members from the fighting. His fate is unknown.

He is known entirely from the Institute's Ancient Notes and two artifact texts. The notes show a practical, dry-humoured administrator who cared about talented youths and post-disaster reconstruction.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. His present whereabouts are not stated. The Institute he led is long gone.

In the present the Traveler finds the key to his office in a chest in the Narzissenkreuz Ordo and finds rifthounds in the office. Nothing says whether he died, was lost to the flood or lived on.

172.content:
Eberhart (also: Master Eberhart, young master Eberhart): A noble-born schemer of Mondstadt's Aristocratic period, the illegitimate son of a great family, who wanted to restore the old nobility's glory and was willing to destroy people to do it.

He is known entirely through weapon texts and the Dragonspine expedition journals. Those sources describe a charming, manipulative man who treated everyone close to him as a tool. Nobody in the surviving record knows what became of him.

Status as of 7.1: Fate unknown. He was gravely wounded on Dragonspine and no record shows him returning; he is presumed long dead. No appearance after the Aristocratic period.

173.content:
Eduardo Baker (also: Eduardo, Baker of Fleuve Cendre, the Fleuve Cendre outlaw leader): Eduardo Baker was a Fontainian outlaw leader who kept order among the people of the Fleuve Cendre undercity before the cataclysm. His son Jakob is the later Jakob Ingold.

He is known from a weapon description, the Fleuve Cendre Ferryman, and a few related item texts. The Court of Fontaine's purge of Fleuve Cendre turned him from local protector into a rebel, and the occupation of Poisson that he led ended in the Siege of Poisson.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead; canon never states how. He is generally taken to have died in the Siege of Poisson.

The siege razed the village and burned many of its inhabitants. Eduardo appears only in the Ferryman weapon text and related items, and no mention in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found.

174.content:
Egeria (also: Mistress of Many Waters, Lord of Amrita, Queen of All Waters, Noble Navigator, Ruler of Rivers and Seas, Usurper of Many Waters, first Hydro Archon): Egeria, the Mistress of Many Waters, was the first Hydro Archon of The Seven and Fontaine's god from about 2,000 to 500 years ago. She replaced the fallen God King Remus, united the surviving tribes and founded Fontaine's rule of law. Out of compassion she gave her Oceanid followers human bodies, a "sin" that brought Celestia's prophecy of drowning upon Fontaine. She died at Tunigi Hollow in the cataclysm.

Her body became the Amrita, a pool of pure dew in Sumeru's desert. Her chosen successor Focalors spent five centuries undoing the prophecy she left behind.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the cataclysm 500 years ago. Her body became the Amrita at Tunigi Hollow in Sumeru.

Corrupted by the Abyss and unable to be reborn in a purer plane, her divine consciousness was anchored in the Gaokerena lotus inside the Harvisptokhm, which Rukkhadevata grew from the Amrita to seal the rift. In the 3.6 quest Khvarena of Good and Evil, the Traveler, Paimon and the Pari Sorush purified her defiled consciousness and woke it, and the tree regrew.

175.content:
Elynas (also: Father of the Melusines, the great beast Elynas): Elynas is a colossal beast who died in the cataclysm about 500 years ago. His corpse forms much of Fontaine's Beryl Region, and the Melusines call him "Father" because they grew from his wounds. In the Ancient Colors quests he speaks once to the Traveler.

He is arguably the wisest and gentlest of Rhinedottir's Abyss-linked creations: he learned that what delights him hurts others, accepted death, and spends his afterlife watching over the Melusines. He does not want to be revived.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, but a faint awareness lingers in his corpse; only Mamere hears him. No later appearance as of 7.1.

In Ancient Colors Act III (4.0), Jakob restarted his heart to gather blood. Elynas had a Breacher Primus free the Traveler and then, in a brief "time of life", spoke to them in a spirit space. The Traveler stopped his heart again, and he thanked them. He calls the Traveler only the second person unafraid of his blood.

176.content:
Emanuel Guillotin (also: Guillotin the elder): Emanuel Guillotin was a Fontainian hunter of the Marechaussee Phantom about five centuries ago. After directing the bloody Siege of Poisson he retired, scarred and drinking, until a childhood friend left two children in his care.

He is remembered through the Marechaussee Hunter artifact set. He was the first person dissolved by the Narzissenkreuz.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Dissolved and absorbed by the Narzissenkreuz about 500 years ago.

Nothing is known of him after that. Alain and Mary-Ann's own stories appear in the Marechaussee Hunter and related content.

177.content:
Erinnyes (also: Errighenth, Errighenth of Aremorica, High King of Aremorica): Erinnyes was the High King of Aremorica in Remuria's last years. A former singer, she led the northern tribes against the empire and founded the Lochknights.

She claimed to hear the goddess Egeria and sought the Pure Grail to save her people from the prophecy of dissolution. Egeria's answer ended her quest.

Status as of 7.1: Fate unknown. She left the valley after meeting Egeria and was never seen again.

The island and forest named Erinnyes are probably named after her. A play and the book La Chanson d'Erinnyes retell her life, the book with romantic liberties.

178.content:
Euergetia (also: the benefactrix, Harmost Euergetia, Beneficent Euergetia): Euergetia was one of the four Harmosts of ancient Remuria, called the benefactrix. She was known for kindness and authority and died when Remuria was destroyed.

She appears only in environmental texts and a weapon description. Her legion, Legio VI, honoured her to the end.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. She died in Remuria's destruction.

Her name survives at Hortus Euergetis, a garden under the sea named for her, and in the Symphonist of Scents weapon, whose text says the wish for good food endured into present-day Fontaine. No post-4.6 appearance was found by 7.1.

179.content:
Filipov (also: Filipov Vseslavyevich, Grand Duke Filipov): A Snowland Fae Grand Duke, the Belyi Tsar's sworn Synaimos and first Commander of the Druzhna, and the most gifted shapeshifter of his people. He is remembered as a cunning strategist and a grieving widower, and he disappeared when the Tsar died.

He is known only through books and item text. Chronicles pair his name with cunning, quick wit and victory, and credit him with losing only three times in a long life.

Status as of 7.1: Missing since the cataclysm roughly five hundred years ago. He left his army when the Tsar died, and canon says nobody knows his fate. He has not appeared in the present day through 7.1.

180.content:
Froderock Fronkonsteen (also: Professor Froderock, Professor Fronkonsteen): Froderock Fronkonsteen was a Fatui professor and subordinate of Il Dottore who commanded the Fatui Desert Expedition Team in the Desert of Hadramaveth, Sumeru. He studied the Eremite Tanit tribe and is thought to have been killed when Jeht broke free.

He is never met; the Traveler learns of him from soldiers' remarks and the expedition's notes.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead. The expedition was wiped out when Jeht broke out of her cage, killed soldiers and rampaged.

A fleeing Skirmisher asks where the Professor is; the other says he is in the cave and everywhere. Neither he nor the expedition is mentioned again.

181.content:
Grazina (also: Grazina Myklukho, G. Myklukho, Senior Researcher Grazina, Gentle Female Voice): Grazina Myklukho was a Senior Researcher in the Post-Apocalyptic Elysium, an apocalypse bunker in Nod-Krai built under the Belyi Tsar. She led the plant-breeding work that produced the plants later called Mandragoras, and learned too late that her supervisor was using her research for Rotwang.

She is known only through the logs, notes and recordings the Traveler can find in the bunker during the world quest Return to Sender. Her voice in the recordings is credited as a Gentle Female Voice.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead around 500 years ago. She sealed herself in the bunker; the Traveler finds her records in Nod-Krai's Wavechaser Plain.

Morozov was resurrected as the Ultimate Calamity and the Traveler defeats it in Return to Sender (or at Piramida, depending on quest order). Mandragoras survive outside the bunker as her lasting legacy.

182.content:
Greater Lord Rukkhadevata (also: Rukkhadevata, Queen Aranyani, Sage-King of the Greenwood, Great Master of Verdure, Queen of the Rainforest, God of the Woods): Sumeru's first Dendro Archon and God of Wisdom, avatar of Irminsul, whom the Aranara called Queen Aranyani. She died in the cataclysm 500 years ago after creating her successor, Nahida. In 3.2 she had Nahida erase her from Irminsul, and only the Traveler still remembers her.

Before 3.2 Sumeru revered her and the sages kept her cult alive while confining her small, weak-seeming successor. Afterwards every record and memory changed: the Aranara's queen, the sages' idol and the gods' old colleague all became Nahida.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the cataclysm and erased from Irminsul (3.2). Teyvat now remembers Nahida as the only Dendro Archon; the Traveler keeps her secret.

The erasure ended the crazed whispers, the Withering and Eleazar. Her name survives only by chance: on the RUKDVTA throne in the Orchard of Pairidaeza, in a mushroom's description and in a few old item texts.

183.content:
Guhua (also: Gǔhuá, 古华): Guhua is a legendary martial nomad of Liyue remembered as a peacekeeper and the namesake of the Guhua Clan. He trained on Mt. Lingmeng and devised three techniques, and the Rainslasher is said to have been his weapon. He never led the clan that bears his name.

His surviving notes show a man whose training repeatedly detoured into other interests, such as fish and mutton cooking.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago; the date is unknown. A legend says he ascended as an adeptus and became a star at Huaguang Stone Forest, but nothing else supports it. No relevant 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content found.

The Guhua Clan, founded after his death by Baixuan, still teaches in his name. He is a founder in memory only: he never took a disciple.

184.content:
Guizhong (also: Haagentus, God of Dust, Lord of Dust): Guizhong, divine name Haagentus, was the God of Dust. She was not a strong god but a brilliant inventor, and she ruled the ancient Guili Assembly north of Mt. Tianheng with Morax (now Zhongli). She died in the Archon War about 3,700 years ago. Her legacy includes the Guizhong Ballista, the stone dumbbell called Memory of Dust, and the name of the Guili Plains.

To her friends among the adepti she was the centre of every gathering: extroverted, joking, fond of banquets and of building machines. Her death scattered her people and led Morax to found Liyue Harbor. Her closest friends, Madame Ping and Cloud Retainer, still grieve for her.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: killed in the Archon War about 3,700 years ago. She does not appear in the present and has no known remnant or reincarnation as of 7.1.

She is remembered chiefly by the adepti and Zhongli, and in Lantern Rite Madame Ping counts her among the heroes the festival honours. Her ballista still stands at Tianheng Pass, guarded by the Millelith.

185.content:
Gunnhildr (also: Gunnhildr the priestess, first priestess of the Gunnhildr Clan): A woman of the Gunnhildr Clan in Decarabian's age. As the clan chief's daughter she prayed to a wind spirit in a blizzard, and her faith made the spirit strong enough to become Barbatos. Her descendants named the Gunnhildr Clan for her.

Most of what survives comes from a book compiled by a modern clan descendant, so it is a family tradition rather than neutral history.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead. She appears only in the Biography of Gunnhildr and in the clan's legacy; no ghost, relic or later sighting is attested.

186.content:
Guthred (also: Guthred the military doctor, the Captain's second-in-command): A military doctor of fallen Khaenri'ah and Capitano's second-in-command during the cataclysm. He invented the Draught of Lucidity, tested it on himself and died soon after; five centuries later his soul resurfaced in Natlan.

He believed a commander should do whatever it takes to win. Capitano did not, and remembered him with respect regardless.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the cataclysm. His soul lingered and briefly took control of Ororon in 5.1, then was expelled.

In the Night Kingdom battle (5.3) a Guthred appeared to break an Abyssal ward for the Traveler, saying he was a story told by the Masters of the Night-Wind rather than the real man. Nothing about him has appeared in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content.

187.content:
Hadura (also: Sentinel of the Golden Hall, Knight Commander Hadura, Garrison Commander Hadura): A Knight Commander of the Schwanenritter in Khaenri'ah's last days, titled "Sentinel of the Golden Hall" for a successful operation against the Abyssal beasts. Later Hadura betrayed the order and was executed by Knight Marshal Anfortas.

Hadura is known only through orders and chronicles left in Sumeru's ruins. Nobody speaks for Hadura and no motive is given, so the reason for the betrayal is open.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, executed by Anfortas roughly five hundred years before the main story, and still given a knight's funeral because Hadura was the last of the other knights.

Nothing about Hadura appears in Nod-Krai (6.x) or Snezhnaya (7.0-7.1) content in the pages read. Hadura lives on through the chronicle in the Devantaka Ruin Golem and through the descent claimed by Klingsor.

188.content:
Hakushin (also: Great Kitsune Hakushin, Great Matriarch, Hakushin Matriarch): Hakushin was a Great Kitsune, matriarch and namesake of the Hakushin Clan that lived around Mt. Yougou in Inazuma. The Kitsune Saiguu and Yae Miko are among her descendants.

Canon says almost nothing else about her. She appears only in book text and clan lore, and in no present-day quest.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. She lived long ago, and canon does not say what became of her.

189.content:
Han Wu (also: Han Wu the weaponsmith, Master Han Wu): Han Wu was a master weaponsmith of Liyue who lived around the time of the cataclysm, five hundred years ago. With the smith Yun Hui he developed the Prototype weapon series, and he is also tied to the Blackcliff series.

He was fiery-tempered until a disaster in the Chasm changed him. He is known only through the flavour text of weapons, not through any quest or voiced appearance.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He died peacefully in his sleep a few years after forging the Slasher.

On the day he died the shrine emerged from the cave and the sword glowed as if grieving. Han Ce retrieved it that night, found his father's prototype designs, made the Blackcliff Pole from them and decided to carry on the family trade.

190.content:
Havria (also: God of Salt, Salt God, Goddess of Salt): Havria was the God of Salt, a gentle and relatively weak god of Liyue before and during the Archon War. She refused to fight, gave shelter to people displaced by the war, and was killed by one of her own followers at Sal Terrae, leaving only a flower of salt.

She held two relics, a bottomless salt chalice and a ruler that raises salt from the ground. Her death turned her unfortunate worshippers who stayed behind into salt; the survivors fled to Liyue and the protection of Morax. Zhongli knows her story and counts it as a warning from the war.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed before the game's events. Only a single flower of salt remains in a sealed domain at Sal Terrae. Not seen or mentioned in content after Sal Flore up to Version 7.1.

Her body dissipated into the salt flower. Followers who could not flee were turned to salt statues in the ruin, and those who escaped later returned to break the sword that killed her. In the quest Zhongli took her chalice and ruler to Guyun Stone Forest and cast them into the sea above Osial's prison, saying another spark of divinity had left Liyue.

191.content:
Hermanubis (also: Greatest of Sages, Saint Hermanubis, Sage of Sages, Priest of Priests): Hermanubis, the Greatest of Sages, was a Tighnarian priest-warrior raised to be one of King Deshret's Seven Pillars. He founded the Temple of Silence and, to save his followers, broke himself into fragments of power.

His power outlived him. Two Ba Fragments live on in Cyno, General Mahamatra of the Akademiya. He is revered by the Temple of Silence as a founder of desert civilization and remembered by the other Pillars with respect.

Status as of 7.1: Deceased: he shattered himself long ago. His power survives as Ba Fragments.

Two fragments were held by the Temple of Silence under its leader Bamoun. They were implanted in two children, Sethos and Cyno, and at the start of the Traveler's story they were split between them. In the Cyno story quest Oathkeeper (4.6), Cyno won both in the Rite of Duels; the Temple's custom is to follow whoever holds the most fragments, but Cyno handed leadership to Sethos.

192.content:
Hiiragi Hiroshi (also: Lord Hiiragi Hiroshi, Hiroshi, Kanjou Commissioner Hiroshi, the Kanjou Head who built Ritou): Head of the Hiiragi Clan and Kanjou Commissioner about five hundred years ago. He is remembered for creating the trading port of Ritou on a deserted island, a feat that impressed the Shogun.

He wanted foreign trade centralised under Inazuma's government and proved the benefits by importing foreign inventions. He is known only through item text, a voiceover line and a quest.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; a historical figure of about five hundred years ago.

His clan survives and still heads the Kanjou Commission, and Ritou remains Inazuma's trading hub.

193.content:
Maghan's Master (also: The last Holy Sovereign of Mictlan, Starcaller, Star-caller): She was the last Holy Sovereign of the valley tribe in the Tezcatepetonco Range that would later be called Mictlan.
