Chosen as a child for her star-bright soul, blinded by smoke and lamed at the ankles, she bore a role that was in effect a sacrifice. She was the mistress of Dinga, who became the dragon slayer Maghan, and she became her people's Wayob after he killed her at her own request.

Canon gives her no personal name; she is known only through the text of two weapons, the Flute of Ezpitzal and Starcaller's Watch (named for the statuette she gave Dinga). Her last wishes tied Mictlan to the land of Natlan and set the course of Maghan's life.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; she became Mictlan's Wayob, and her statuette survives as the relic Starcaller's Watch. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 appearance was found.

Maghan's successor as priest, Wagadu, is said to have renewed her pact with the Weaver of Secrets, giving rise to the first iktomisaurus (Rainbow Serpent's Rain Bow text). In the current era she is known only from item text and tribal memory.

194.content:
Huitzilin (also: Great shaman Huitzilin, The legendary shaman): Huitzilin was a legendary shaman and scroll-weaver of the Masters of the Night-Wind, who lived about two hundred years ago. She mastered using colour as a medium for memory, and her technique became the backbone of how the tribe weaves its history into scrolls. She was Citlali's fellow student, rival and friend.

She is met only through voice, flashback and scroll depictions in Citlali's quests, never in the present day.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about two centuries. Her legacy lives on in the woven scrolls of the Masters of the Night-Wind, the colour-memory technique Citlali carries on, and the memory maze of the Seven-Hued Ruins. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 appearance was found.

195.content:
Hydro Dragon (also: Hydro Dragon Sovereign, Dragon of Water, Hydro Sovereign): The Hydro Dragon Sovereign was the ruler of the Vishaps with sovereignty over water, one of the Seven Sovereigns. After dying in the war against the Heavenly Principles it was reborn as the human Neuvillette.

Hydro Vishap legend calls it the beating heart that ruled over the Primordial Sea.

Status as of 7.1: The original dragon is dead. As Neuvillette it lives again.

Before the events of The Opera of Noirceur and Blancheur, Neuvillette lacked the old power and memories, including his link to the Primordial Sea. Needing the Archon's authority returned, he thought the solution unworkable, since it would require the Hydro Archon's death. Focalors executed herself so that he regained his full powers and memories, and he used them to make Fontainians fully human, preventing the prophecy's dissolution.

196.content:
I. Ivanovna N. (also: Ioanna Ivanovna N., Ioanna Ivanovna, Ivanovna, Lady Ioanna Ivanovna, Tricksy-Witch, Speaker Ivanovna): A human politician of Snezhnaya who lived centuries ago: Hexenzirkel member J (the Tricksy-Witch) and the first Speaker of the Snezhnograd Veche, appointed by the Tsaritsa. She left the witches to marry and mentored the future Harbinger Pulcinella.

She had no magic or combat training and called herself and Andersdotter simply ordinary; her power was political. The line of successors she left behind lasted into the Traveler's time.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; she passed away centuries ago. Her offices passed to Pulcinella, who is Speaker of the Veche in the present.

Scarlet Proof artifact text mentions Pulcinella thinking about his own successor after her death, and an old noble of the Veche, Golitsyn, says his house owes its standing to the grace of Lady Ioanna Ivanovna. Her line of successors continues; the latest, Scarlett, tailed the Traveler to the floating island and lit the Lantern of Utmost Joy in the 3.5 Windblume event.

197.content:
Imunlaukr (also: the outlander of Sal Vindagnyr, the hero from another land): A warrior from outside Sal Vindagnyr who loved the mountain city's princess. He left to find an Irminsul branch to save it, returned to find everyone dead, and wandered into war. His descendants became the Imunlaukr Clan.

His story is told in weapon descriptions and in the murals of Dragonspine, not in a quest. It is a tragedy about arriving too late.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; his end is unrecorded. Only his descendants are attested.

198.content:
Indarias (also: General Musatas, Flame Yaksha): Indarias, titled General Musatas, was one of the Five Foremost Yakshas, the strongest of the adepti warriors Morax called upon to destroy the demons born from fallen gods. She died long ago; canon records almost nothing of her beyond her rank and a single anguished moment in a dying comrade's memory.

She is known only through others. Xiao, the last surviving yaksha, names her when recalling the five, and the Chasm quests briefly show her. No living character tells a story about her.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, long before the present story. No confirmed manner of death. Not mentioned in 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya content.

She survives only in the yakshas' legend and in Xiao's memory. Each spring at Lantern Rite, Liyue's people honor the surviving Conqueror of Demons, not her.

199.content:
Ingbert (also: Master Ingbert, Ingobert): Ingbert was a Mondstadt aristocrat of the Aristocratic period, about a thousand years ago. As Landrich's legitimate son and Parsifal's brother, he loved exploration and adventure. He joined an expedition to Dragonspine and was killed there by his half-brother Eberhart.

He is known only through the Ancient Investigation Journals, which the household servant Luther wrote on the expedition.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed in the ruins of Dragonspine about a thousand years ago.

200.content:
Irmin (also: Vinster King, King Irmin, one-eyed king Irmin, Almighty Sovereign): Irmin was the one-eyed last Vinster King of Khaenri'ah's Eclipse Dynasty. Once sane, he sank into an obsession with Abyssal power and knowledge "from beyond the skies". He named the Traveler's sibling his heir, then used them as a vessel for Abyssal power, setting the Five Sinners and the cataclysm in motion. He is known only through others' accounts.

His court was led by trusted servants such as the sage Hroptatyr and the seer Vedrfolnir. When Vedrfolnir warned him that Khaenri'ah would fall, Irmin had him blinded and imprisoned, which provoked the palace raid by Dainsleif and the future Five Sinners.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead for about five hundred years; his reign ended with the palace raid and the cataclysm. No scene shows his death, though item text lists "regicide" among that night's events.

Officially, Khaenri'ahn records said only that he was "indisposed" when Anfortas took the regency. As of 7.1 no living character claims he survived, and he does not appear in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya stories except in flashbacks and others' accounts.

201.content:
Iwakura Michihiro (also: Douin, Iwakura Douin, Iwakura Doukei, Mikoshi Michihiro, Iwakura the Successor, founder of the Iwakura Clan): Born Mikoshi Michihiro, eldest son of the oni warrior Chiyo and heir to the Mikoshi Clan, he withdrew from his disgraced clan after his mother's betrayal and was renamed Iwakura by the tengu Teruyo. He developed the Tengu Sweeper, founded the Iwakura Art and became the Kujou Clan's sword instructor under the title Douin.

He is known only through item text and the folk song "Iwakura the Successor". His legacy was a school that lasted five centuries and a puppet swordsman that copied his style.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead or presumed dead; nothing says how he died. The sword school he founded outlived him by centuries.

In the present day the Iwakura Art was led by Mitsunari, but the Vision Hunt Decree scattered the clan, and the Traveler's encounters in Inazuma left no known members alive; only the Maguu Kenki still fights in his style.

key: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers
202.content:
Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak (also: Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers, The Eighth Lord, CL-08, Ix Ajkotz'i'j Iq'ismal Waxak Ch'ule-L, Lianca's adoptive mother): She was the Eighth of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, the dragon rulers created by Xiuhcoatl, and presided over Ch'upikaq Tajin, later Flower-Feather Clan territory. She adopted the human girl Lianca, and the Sovereign Lords' council voted to execute her for it. She stayed loyal to dragonkind to the end.

Her proper title is the Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers. Her name is Mayan in origin; the wiki glosses it as a priestess who places flowers and candles at shrines, with wind, feathers and the number eight.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: executed by her own council during the siege of Tollan, though she stayed loyal to dragonkind until her last breath. Her territory became the Flower-Feather Clan's land. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 appearance was found.

In Smoldering (5.8), Citlali tells the party that records claim she was executed by her own kind for secretly raising a human; Chasca notes that legends of Lianca do not name her dragon mother. A Little Robot tells Ineffa to return to the Eighth Lord's territory to restore her memory data.

203.content:
Ix Je'lal K'ua'l Ka' (also: Ix Je'lal K'ua'l Ka' Ch'ule-L, Jade Maiden, Second Sovereign Lord, Second of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, CL-02): Ix Je'lal K'ua'l Ka', the Jade Maiden, was the Second of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, a dragon ruler of ancient Natlan. She is remembered as a hard-line councillor and as the artisan who forged the bow Chain Breaker for the human girl Lianca. She is known only through records and item text, never in person.

She appears in Council Records found in the Chamber of Deliberation. There she is severe about weakness: she judged fallen Lords unworthy and voted to execute a colleague on the smallest suspicion of betrayal.

Status as of 7.1: Presumably dead. The wiki reads Once, the Sacred Seat of Judgment as placing her among the ten Lords who fell when Xbalanque besieged the Sacred City of Tollan. No appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 was found.

204.content:
Ix Kemonel Jasjatem Oox (also: Ix Kemonel Jasjatem Oox Ch'ule-L, Weaver of Secrets, Third Sovereign Lord, Third of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords, CL-03): Ix Kemonel Jasjatem Oox, the Weaver of Secrets, was the Third of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords. She ruled a territory in the Tezcatepetonco Range and, unlike Lords who oppressed human tribes, allied with those who sought her protection. She aimed to weave an eternal dream-realm in the Night Kingdom for her declining dragons.

She is known only through records and item text. She was learned in divination and destiny, and she took a humane, if controlling, line towards her dragons.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. She merged her consciousness into the Night Kingdom, and canon sources read do not say if she persists. No appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 was found.

205.content:
Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon (also: Ixlel, Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon Ch'ule-L, Chronicler of the End Times, Ninth Sovereign Lord, CL-09): Ix Uxul Tz'ib Bolon, nicknamed Ixlel, was the Ninth of the Thirteen Sovereign Lords and ruler of Chichen Uctokah, the city later renamed Ochkanatlan. Och-Kan sealed her in a stone statue in the Old Core of Chu'ulel for thousands of years. In Open Your Heart to Me (5.2) the Traveler freed her soul at her own request.

She is a quest-only figure with no playable form. Proud, formal and sharp-tongued, she insists on her rank, yet near her end she is weary and bitter about the memories that bound her.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. In Open Your Heart to Me (5.2) she asked the Traveler to gather the fragments of her heart. She poured her last energy into the heart to restore it, and the Traveler took it. This released her soul. She has no known appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

206.content:
Ixquieh (also: Hero of the Forged Flame, Chief of the Children of Echoes, First Bearer of Baraka, Baraka bearer): Ixquieh was one of the original Six Heroes of Natlan, the first bearer of the Ancient Name Baraka and a master of flame-forging. With her twin Ahpub she joined Xbalanque against tyrant dragons, then led the Children of Echoes, and died long ago after a split with her brother.

The Ring of Yaxche describes her as a calm, unflappable young woman. Sundjatta's notes call her Hero of the Forged Flame, the first to master smelting phlogiston itself.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago. Two accounts disagree: the Ring of Yaxche says Ahpub accidentally killed her in their quarrel; Sundjatta's notes say she took her own life and burned her workshop so that her writings and legacy would not fall to Och-Kan or be stained. Little of her work survives, and a friend of hers preserved some. She appears only in flashbacks in Flamelets and Searing (5.8).

key: President of the Royal Energy Commission
207.content:
Izmaylov (also: Nikolay Izmaylov, Nikolay "Pakhan" Izmaylov, Pakhan Izmaylov, Old Sire, President of the Royal Energy Commission): A Domovoy of old Kitezhgrad who rose from spy to President of the Royal Energy Commission, founded the gangs' High Table and stayed loyal to his teacher Aksinya. He died months before the Traveler's visit.

The gangs call him the Old Sire. His death, officially sudden illness, is widely suspected to have been murder by his adopted son Vasiliy.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; he died suddenly, and his gang passed to his adopted son Vasiliy.

In Disputes Without Honor and Humanity the High Table suspects that Vasiliy and the Butcher were the last to see him and that the cause was not illness. Gureva, a Luchkin agent captured by Vasiliy's second-in-command, tells her captor the Old Sire's death does not add up. The wiki records Vasiliy as the killer. Vasiliy later tried to open the Shadow Realm, was defeated by the Traveler and left blind and calling for Zmei as the device shut down; his fate is not stated.

208.content:
Jacob Musk (also: Jacob Musk the ecologist, Poet Laureate of Hilichurlian, Mondstadt Ecologist): Jacob Musk was a celebrated Mondstadt ecologist who lived at an unknown time. He wrote the books Hilichurl Ballad Selection and Hilichurl Cultural Customs, and is an ancestor of the scholars Ella and Edith Musk.

Mondstadt's libraries credit him as the Poet Laureate of Hilichurlian. His work is the nearest thing the city has to an ethnography of hilichurls.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago. Only his books remain, in the Knights of Favonius Headquarters library and with Ella Musk.

209.content:
Kaedehara Hisamichi (also: Hisamichi, Kazuha's grandfather): Kaedehara Kazuha's grandfather, from the Kaedehara line of the Isshin Art. He failed to restore his family's swordsmithing, left Inazuma, and died before the start of the game.

He is known from Kazuha's memories in the limited Summertime Odyssey event (2.8). He later took up rock gardens, as his own father had kept bonsai.

Status as of 7.1: Dead before the game begins.

The household ended when Kazuha dissolved it after his own father's death. No canon mention after 7.1 was found.

210.content:
Kaedehara Kageharu (also: Kageharu, Kazuha's father): Kaedehara Kazuha's father. He died before the game begins, leaving a household in debt and a son he urged to live free of the clan's burdens.

He is known only from the limited event Summertime Odyssey (2.8), through Kazuha's memories, a note and a letter. He loved bonsai.

Status as of 7.1: Dead before the game.

No later mention appears in canon through 7.1.

211.content:
Kaedehara Yoshinori (also: Yoshinori, Kazuha's great-grandfather, head of the Kaedehara Clan): Kaedehara Kazuha's great-grandfather and the last head of the Kaedehara Clan's Isshin Art, one of the five Raiden Gokaden sword-smithing traditions. He survived the Case of the Eccentric, kept its truth secret and quietly let the family trade end.

He is known through a brief voiced flashback and a hidden letter, found in the limited 2.6 event Hues of the Violet Garden. Once an industrious smith, he later gave up forging and kept bonsai.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; the letter was written near the end of his life. His clan's smithing practice ended with him, though Kazuha learned some Kaedehara techniques.

His great-grandson Kazuha now knows the truth and has made peace with it. The Isshin Art lives on in a limited way through Kazuha, and the sentient blade Kagotsurube Isshin is tied to the Akame smith Kanenaga, who fled to Snezhnaya after the incident.

212.content:
Kamisato Kayo (also: Tsubaki): Kamisato Kayo was the mother of Kamisato Ayato and Kamisato Ayaka of the Kamisato Clan, and is deceased. Her children remember her as dignified, elegant and always smiling under heavy clan duties. She died while Ayaka was young, which pushed Ayaka to mature early and take a larger part in the clan's affairs. She has no on-screen appearance; she is known through voice-overs and Ayaka's Story Quest.

In private she took the alter ego "Tsubaki", a name under which she imagined life without the Kamisato Clan's responsibilities.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; no date, cause or place is given. Her notebooks and her secret meeting place remained after her, and her children preserved her memory.

Her hidden notebook was found by Ayaka in the Grus Nivis Chapter and led Ayaka to fulfil one of her mother's unfulfilled wishes: attending a festival as an ordinary person.

213.content:
Kamuna Harunosuke (also: Master Kamuna, Narukami's Envoy, Mysterious Man): Kamuna Harunosuke was an onmyouji of Inazuma from the Kamuna Clan who lived about five hundred years ago. With Asase Hibiki and Mikoshi Nagamasa he trained on Mt. Yougou under the tengu, and the three are remembered as the Yougou Three. After the cataclysm he went to Liyue to learn the adepti arts, later sealing the troublesome tanuki Ioroi in stone for the Shogunate.

He created the art of Onmyoudou by combining adepti arts with his own techniques, made the shikigami Shiki Taishou and owned the Mystic Onmyou Chamber domain. The Kamuna arts, paper seals that coat weapons with elemental energy even without a Vision, are used by the Kairagi today.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. Wiki sources say he left for unknown parts after finishing his work. His domain, the Mystic Onmyou Chamber, and his shikigami remain.

Shiki Taishou eventually persuaded him to let go of his burdens, as the Shogun's own protection of Inazuma made the chamber's purpose pointless; he then left to seek a new purpose.

214.content:
Kapatcir (also: Kanna Kapatcir, Great Thunderbird, Thunderbird, Great Eagle of the Storm): Kanna Kapatcir, the Great Thunderbird, was a vast Electro bird of prey, called a monster in item text, that Tsurumi Island's old tribe revered as its guardian. She destroyed the island and its people in grief and rage after a boy she had befriended was sacrificed.

She is known through memory, artifact text and the Traveler's Tsurumi quests, not through any appearance. Her power outlived her as the Thunder Manifestations.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed by Ei long before the Traveler's time. What remains is her residual power, sealed and later released as Thunder Manifestations, and a feather that answered Ruu's song. No later developments in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

215.content:
Karl Ingold (also: Mr. Karl, Ingold the journalist): Karl Ingold was a Fontainian journalist who lived around the cataclysm. He carried Eduardo Baker's demands to the Court of Fontaine before the Siege of Poisson and left journalism afterwards.

He later raised Jakob and Rene after Basil Elton asked him to take them in, and appears only in item texts.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. No source says what became of him after the expedition.

216.content:
Katsuragi (also: Sir Katsuragi, Mikoshi Nagamasa's yoriki): Katsuragi was a yoriki of the Inazuma Shogunate who lived at Tatarasuna roughly four hundred years ago, serving Inspector Mikoshi Nagamasa, who had saved his life. He was known as kind and loyal, and befriended a nameless wandering eccentric (the Kabukimono, later Scaramouche and the Wanderer). After a disaster at the Mikage Furnace he took the blame in Nagamasa's place and was cut down by Nagamasa's own blade.

His death is remembered in the name of the sword Katsuragikiri Nagamasa, "Nagamasa who cut Katsuragi". Records of what really happened were suppressed, so for centuries most people knew only that Nagamasa had killed his retainer for some supposed misconduct.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about four hundred years, cut down at Tatarasuna by Nagamasa. As of 7.1 nothing changes this; no new appearance was found in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

The sword that killed him was thrown into the furnace afterwards. His memory survives chiefly as an epithet: both the blade and Nagamasa came to be called Katsuragikiri Nagamasa.

217.content:
Kaveh's Father (also: Kaveh's dad, the Interdarshan contestant, Faranak's husband): An unnamed scholar of the Rtawahist Darshan at the Sumeru Akademiya, husband of the architect Faranak and father of Kaveh. About twenty years before the game he took part in the Interdarshan Championship, fell short, and went into the desert, where he died in an accident.

Kaveh remembers him as kind and generous, a man who promised to bring something nice back for him. Faranak says he was a good-hearted man who made her happy. His death shaped Kaveh's guilt, his architecture-loving childhood and his habit of refusing help.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about twenty years, killed in an accident in the desert. No remains or grave are mentioned.

His belongings did not reach his family; the unfinished letter was lost. His memory survives in Kaveh, in Faranak's drawing (a blond man pictured with three other men) and in the stories of Aaru Village.

218.content:
Kazuha's Friend (also: the Masterless Vision's owner): Kazuha's friend was an Electro Vision bearer and close companion of Kaedehara Kazuha. After losing a duel before the throne to Kujou Sara, he was executed by the Raiden Shogun under the Vision Hunt Decree. His name is not given in the game.

His death shaped Kazuha: the Vision he left behind, known as the Masterless Vision, is why Kazuha carries two Visions in the Omnipresent God cinematic.

Status as of 7.1: Executed before the game's events. His broken blade lies as a mound north-east of the Grand Narukami Shrine, with an epitaph, and his Vision rests beside Kazuha's as a memorial. No later developments in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

219.content:
King Deshret (also: Al-Ahmar, Amun, Lord of Deserts, Scarlet King, Mourning King, Lord of the Red Sands, King of the Great Red Sand, Red Lord): King Deshret (personal name Al-Ahmar, divine name Amun) was the god-king of Sumeru's desert thousands of years ago. With Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, and Greater Lord Rukkhadevata he was one of the Three Eternal Companion-Gods. Grief for Nabu Malikata drove him to forbidden knowledge, which ruined his civilization and gave rise to the Withering. He gave his life to end the disaster.

Desert people still revere him. The Eremites descend from his subjects and some still want him back; Aaru Village preserves the last embers of his people. His ruins, including the Mausoleum, Khaj-Nisut and the Primal Constructs, cover the Great Red Sand. His greatest work, Aaru, was built from celestial technology. In 6.6 it was opened and became the new hub for Teyvat's memories after Irminsul was destroyed.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years. He sacrificed himself to stop the spread of forbidden knowledge, and Apep swallowed his body.

His legacy is still active. The Withering descends from his disaster. In Version 6.6 (Song of the Welkin Moon Acts IX-X), with Sumeru in crisis, Nefer answered his three questions and freed Thoth, Sobek and Heryshaf from Aaru. With Cyno speaking for Hermanubis and Apep already helping Nahida, all Seven Pillars approved opening Aaru. Its souls, Jeht's father among them, returned to the Ley Lines, and its gates opened "by the grace of His Majesty".

220.content:
Kitain Bunsou (also: Kitain the Serpent): Kitain Bunsou, called Kitain the Serpent, was one of Inazuma's celebrated warriors and a spearman. He belonged to the Kitain family of Yashiori Island, which hunted the Tatarigami for generations and served as Prefects of Yashiori. He made the Kitain Cross Spear for his own style of fighting. He is dead and little else is recorded about him.

A children's song once listed him among Inazuma's great warriors, with Arataki of the Front Gate, Iwakura the Successor and Takamine the Mistsplitter; the weapon text says many other names on the list have been lost.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; no date or manner of death is given. His spear survived as a weapon design, recovered in the world quest series Orobashi's Legacy.

His line later died out, for reasons legend does not give. His descendant Kitain Hideie left a written testament of guilt after fleeing the cataclysm battlefield.

221.content:
Kitain Hideie (also: the last Prefect of Yashiori, Last Prefect of Yashiori): Kitain Hideie was the last Prefect of Yashiori, last of the old Kitain Clan of Yashiori Island. Inazuma remembers a Kitain hero who was lost in the cataclysm; his own letter reveals that he lost his nerve in the fighting, deserted his men and the clan's cross-shaped spear, and spent the rest of his life in guilty exile.

He died of old age and exhaustion in the Veluriyam Mirage, where the domain's keeper let him see his battlefield one last time. All of this is known from limited-time event material (Secret Summer Paradise, 3.8), so ordinary Inazumans do not know it.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Public memory says he fell in the cataclysm; in fact he deserted and died in exile in the Veluriyam Mirage.

The Shinrou Casket was lost with him inside the mirage, and the pearl that should have sensed it went dark; In the 3.8 event the casket is found again and helps restart the domain's central hub. The Kitain Clan line ended; the wiki suggests his desertion is the cause, but canon does not say so.

222.content:
Kitsune Saiguu (also: Hakushin Kitsune, Lady Saiguu, Great Silver Kitsune, the Saiguu): The Kitsune Saiguu, also called the Hakushin Kitsune, was a kitsune of the Hakushin Clan whom Inazuma worshipped as a fox goddess. She led the Grand Narukami Shrine, befriended Ei and others of the Raiden era, and vanished into the darkness defending the land during the cataclysm 500 years ago.

She is a figure of memory: the Traveler never meets her, only a shrine maiden formed from her remembrance, her weapon text, and the people and spirits she left behind.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. She disappeared into the darkness during the cataclysm and never returned. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 changes this.

Statues of the Earth and Sky kitsune still wait for her. Her catalyst, the Hakushin Ring, carries a memory of her. Hanachirusato was cleansed in 2.0, leaving a mask that became the Hakushin Ring's blueprint.

223.content:
Knight of the Golden Bough (also: Gunnhildr, the Knight of the Golden Bough, Arcadian Knight Gunnhildr, hero of the Arcadian prophecy): The Knight of the Golden Bough, named Gunnhildr, was the prophesied hero and last hope of Arcadia. After the nation fell the knight went north to Snezhnaya for the Golden Bough, found it ruined, and led Arcadian survivors south instead.

The wiki calls the knight the namesake of Mondstadt's Gunnhildr Clan, a claim that sits uneasily beside the older Biography of Gunnhildr.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; the knight's exact fate is unknown, and the lineage is said to continue as the Gunnhildr Clan.

224.content:
Kreuzlied (also: Kreuzlied of the Wanderer's Troupe, wielder of The Bell): Kreuzlied is the name given to the last known member of the Wanderer's Troupe, a Mondstadt-born fighter who wielded the greatsword The Bell. Born into the ruling Lawrence Clan, he turned against it and was disowned.

After the Troupe's failed uprising against the Mondstadt Aristocracy he survived, spared the worst thanks to his birth. Legend says he then founded a secret society to topple the aristocracy and helped Vennessa's later revolt.

Status as of 7.1: Long gone; his fate is unknown.

225.content:
Kujou Shigeyori (also: Shigeyori Kujou): Kujou Shigeyori was a mortal general of Inazuma, valued by the Raiden Shogun, who according to legend built the battlefront fortress of Kujou Encampment in Kannazuka in a single night during the cataclysm hundreds of years ago. He is the namesake of the Kujou Clan in the wiki's listing.

Almost nothing else about him is recorded in canon. He is a legend recalled in one in-game viewpoint text and does not appear in any quest.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for hundreds of years. His fortress still stands as the Kujou Encampment.

226.content:
Kukulkan (also: Waxaklahun Ubah Kan, Sage of the Stolen Flame, Flamestealer, Regent of Natlantea, Silver Prince): A dragon prince of ancient Natlantea known to humans as the Sage of the Stolen Flame. He brought Phlogiston to the tribes, grew disillusioned when they used it for war, and tried to trick a chosen successor into activating the Huitzilopochtli array.

Canon shows him mostly through records, fables and two quests (Moment of Awakening in 5.2, An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty in 5.5), where he wears human faces and manipulates people he claims to want to save.

Status as of 7.1: Gone. He faded away at the end of An Omen of Annihilation and the Final Entreaty (5.5) after Little One refused to activate Huitzilopochtli, content with the choice.

Natlanese tradition still tells of the Sage, often as a human. Hanan Pacha and the Sanctum of Rainbow Spirits are abandoned. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 appearance has been found.

227.content:
Landrich (also: Master Landrich): Landrich was a Mondstadt aristocrat of the Aristocratic period, about a thousand years ago. He is never seen; the Ancient Investigation Journals show him as a trusted master whose approval his household feared losing, and as the man who stood to lose most from the Dragonspine expedition.

Luther's journals say the expedition was meant to bring back a great achievement to quiet the arrogance of those plotting rebellion, and that Landrich planned to name his illegitimate son Eberhart heir to the clan name once the party returned.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago. His fate is not recorded; he never learns the truth about Eberhart in any surviving text.

Luther's last journal asks whoever finds it to warn Landrich that Eberhart, wounded but possibly alive, would have only one obstacle left on his road to revolt. Nothing says the warning arrived, and no later source mentions Landrich.

228.content:
Leonard (also: Leonard the adventurer, Author of Of Mountains and Seas, Inventor of the Wind Glider): Leonard was an adventurer of ancient Mondstadt whose lifelong dream was to climb Pilos Peak, the tallest and most dangerous mountain in his world. His book, "Of Mountains and Seas", and the meteorites of the Unreconciled Stars event (Version 1.1, limited) preserve his will.

He never conquered the peak, but he left designs for wings so that others might go where legs could not. The wiki credits him as the inventor of the Wind Glider.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about two thousand years or more. His will lingered in meteorites that fell on Mondstadt during the Unreconciled Stars event, and the Traveler destroyed the core with Mona's help.

The sleeping sickness the meteorites caused ended when the core broke. Pilos Peak is now Musk Reef, a small island that anyone can reach by boat, and Mondstadters glide on wings that follow his vision.

229.content:
Leticia (also: Leticia Randolph, Rosa Reed, Verdict's wielder): Leticia Randolph was the eldest daughter of House Randolph, a powerful noble house of Fontaine. She slipped into Fleuve Cendre in disguise, fell in love with a man named Reed, gave up her family name and took up an axe. The claymore Verdict tells her story.

She is known only from that one weapon description and its cross-references. Her end is not recorded.

Status as of 7.1: Fate unknown. Last seen in the sources at the Siege of Poisson, over 500 years ago.

Not mentioned in any quest as a living person; as far as checked she is not part of 5.x, 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story content.

230.content:
Lianca (also: First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan, First Bearer of Vuka, Vuka bearer, uncrowned princess of the Flower-Feather Clan): Lianca was a woman raised by dragons who founded the Flower-Feather Clan as a refuge for the weak and outcast. She was the first bearer of the Ancient Name Vuka and one of Natlan's Six Heroes. She died fighting Och-Kan after her son betrayed her.

She is known mainly through Chain Breaker's legend and flashbacks in the 5.8 quests Flamelets and Searing. She refuses titles and thrones: the clan's people are, in her words, crownless kings.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the Ochkanatlan era, killed in the clash with Och-Kan. Her clan and her Ancient Name Vuka live on. The 5.8 quests show voice-only flashbacks of her, and the Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers says her adoptive mother survived the curse because Lianca saved her.

231.content:
Lovia (also: Lovia the Archpriestess, Last Archpriestess of Hyperborea, Archpriestess of Hyperborea, Archpriestess of the Frostmoon Scions): Lovia was the last Archpriestess of the Frostmoon Scions, the Nod-Krai people descended from exiles of Hyperborea. About five hundred years ago she tried to force the birth of a Sacred Heir through murder and outside alliances, was killed by her own granddaughter Aila, and was struck from the record for blasphemy.

She survives only as a cautionary figure. Only priestess-rank Scions are meant to know her name.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Aila killed her about five hundred years ago, before the Cataclysm, and her name was then struck from public record.

Afterwards Aila became the first Moonchanter, abolished the Archpriestess office and the old Hyperborean rites, and sealed Lovia's records and Rotwang's letters in the Court of the First Edict (the Sanctum of the Oathbearer).

232.content:
Luther (also: Author of the Ancient Investigation Journals, Luther of the Dragonspine expedition): Luther was a member of a Mondstadt aristocratic household around a thousand years ago who travelled to Dragonspine on Landrich's expedition and kept the Ancient Investigation Journals. His last entry names Eberhart as the one who destroyed the party.

His voice survives only as written pages: dutiful, anxious about failing his master, and slow to see what Eberhart was doing.

Status as of 7.1: Dead around a thousand years ago; his last journal says it is his last entry. He is not seen in any scene.

His writings were left in the ruins, where the Traveler finds them during A Land Entombed. Whether anyone read them in his time is unknown.

233.content:
Lyris (also: Princess Lyris, Red Empress, Director Lyris, Director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute): Lyris was the Oceanid director of the Narzissenkreuz Institute, the orphanage of the cataclysm era, and later the Narzissenkreuz Ordo's "Red Empress". Her merging with Mary-Ann Guillotin produced the Oceanid Mary-Ann of Annapausis.

Fontaine's Court recorded her as warm and devoted to the children but of below-average intelligence for an Oceanid. Her story is told only in the Fontaine world quests of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo (4.0) and the memories they unlock.

Status as of 7.1: Lyris no longer exists as a separate person; her identity lives on in the hybrid Oceanid Mary-Ann, who now has a fresh start.

Narzissenkreuz still calls the hybrid more Lyris than Mary-Ann. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 shows her again.

234.content:
Maghan (also: Dinga, Priest-King Maghan, Maghan the dragon slayer): Maghan, first called Dinga, was the attendant of the last Holy Sovereign of a valley in the Tezcatepetonco Range and later a hero beside Xbalanque. About 2,000 years ago he killed his master on Och-Kan's order, then founded the Masters of the Night-Wind (Mictlan).

He is known mostly through weapon and item texts (the Flute of Ezpitzal, Starcaller's Watch, Grainfruit) rather than quests, and the accounts do not fully agree on whether he was a dragon slayer or a man who let the dragons slip away.

Status as of 7.1: Dead about two thousand years; buried in an unmarked grave, remembered as Mictlan's founder.

His tribe still guards the Night Kingdom's lore, and his Grainfruit legend is told in Natlan today. No appearance or mention was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content as of 7.1.

235.content:
Makhaira (also: Temptress of Woe, Queen-Regent Makhaira, the evil queen Makhaira, Jinn-blooded dancing girl): Makhaira was a sword dancer of Tulaytullah in the Great Red Sand, Sumeru, living some thousands of years ago after King Deshret's fall. Her mother was a Jinni. Sold to a vassal king, she helped end his reign, became queen-regent in the wars that followed, and died by viper venom. Later tales call her the Temptress of Woe or the evil queen.

She wielded the blade remembered as Makhaira Aquamarine, and the Thoth slab calls her a Jinn-blooded dancing girl. Accounts disagree on whether she was murdered or chose her own end.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years. She is remembered as a schemer and as the Temptress of Woe, and nothing in canon through Version 7.1 revives or revisits her. Her fate is told in two ways: killed with viper venom by Faramarz, or a self-chosen death by snake venom after a coup.

Her story survives in weapon and artifact texts, the Primal Obelisk inscription at Khaj-Nisut and a Thoth slab found during Headlong Into the Sands, where Kaveh and Alhaitham read her tale. Kaveh says she is mentioned in many papers about the desert.

236.content:
Makoto (also: Raiden Makoto, Baal, first Electro Archon, previous Electro Archon, Narukami Gongen, First Shogun, True Shogun, first Raiden Shogun): Raiden Makoto, Ei's elder twin, was the first Electro Archon and the original Raiden Shogun. She ruled Inazuma for about 1,500 years, with Ei secretly serving as her body double, until she died in Khaenri'ah during the cataclysm 500 years ago.

The world saw the twins as one god, Baal. Her death drove Ei into the frozen "Eternity" of the Shogun puppet; her lingering will freed Ei from it in 2.5.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for 500 years; Ei rules as Baal.

In 2.5 her last fragment of will spoke from Musou Isshin, gave Ei the Sacred Sakura's seed and said a final goodbye.

237.content:
Mallko (also: Mallko of the Scions of the Canopy): Mallko was a Scion of the Canopy and a bearer of an Ancient Name. He died in a Night Warden War five years before the Natlan Archon Quests. He appears in Black Stone Under a White Stone as a temporarily reassembled soul in the Night Kingdom.

He was a strong fighter and the childhood friend of Vichama. As a soul he is steady and willing to sacrifice himself.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. In the Archon Quests, Vichama helped Kachina's rescue team look for Ancient Names, hoping to recover Mallko's. It could not be recovered, but the attempt reassembled parts of his soul in the Night Kingdom. He guided the team, explained the Wayob, and stayed behind to stall Comonqui, who scattered him. The wiki says his soul recovered when the Night Kingdom regained strength after the Abyss invasion was repelled, and he and Vichama then helped the Traveler in battle. Vichama later found peace on hearing of his sacrifice, and died in The Rainbow Destined to Burn.

238.content:
Marfisa (also: Champion Duelist Marfisa, girl born from the ashes, Rightful Reward spear-wielder): Marfisa was a Champion Duelist who lived over 500 years ago. Born in Fleuve Cendre, she rose through self-taught spear fighting, took justice as her rule after losing to a Marechaussee Hunter, and in the end was dissolved by the Narzissenkreuz.

She is known only through weapon and artifact texts. She is dead and is not a living character in any quest.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for over 500 years: dissolved and absorbed by the Narzissenkreuz.

As far as checked she is not part of any 5.x, 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story, and she is not a living character. Her spear technique is described as now belonging to the Narzissenkreuz.

239.content:
Mary-Ann Guillotin (also: Ann (human), Alain's sister): Mary-Ann Guillotin was a Narzissenkreuz Institute orphan who became a Marechaussee Phantom agent and Alain Guillotin's younger sister. She was fatally wounded at Elynas, where the Oceanid Lyris absorbed her will.

She was the cheerful, approachable one of her friend group. Alain later shaped the puppet Sandrone in her likeness and memory.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Her will lives on only as part of the hybrid Oceanid Mary-Ann, who is aware she is not the human.

A memorial park bears her name, and Sandrone, a Harbinger of the Fatui, wears her likeness.

240.content:
Menilek (also: Transcendence, Vuka bearer, Hero of the Flower-Feather Clan): Menilek was a hero of the Flower-Feather Clan who bore the Ancient Name Vuka and rode with his Qucusaur companion Ngoubou. He was one of the six heroes who joined Tenoch against the Abyss and died in the last battle about 500 years ago.

Clan songs remember him for adventures with Ngoubou, a long friendship with Tenoch, and a boisterous love of drink. Chasca inherited his Name after he acknowledged her in 5.1.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 500 years. His Ancient Name Vuka belongs to Chasca, and his memory survives in the Flower-Feather Clan's songs.

His Ngoubou outlived him as the mist-dwelling tyrant, according to the boss text. No new appearance found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content as of 7.1.

241.content:
Menogias (also: General Kapisas, Rock Yaksha): Menogias, titled General Kapisas, was one of the Five Foremost Yakshas who fought for Morax against the demons of the Archon War. Beyond his battle record he is remembered for a stubborn, refined hobby: designing elaborate clothing, which Rex Lapis admired.

He died long ago, probably in a fight with fellow yaksha Bonanus. The people who knew him, Xiao and Xianyun among them, recall his taste and obstinacy more than his deeds in war. A lantern in his image was the star of Liyue's 2024 Lantern Rite (limited event).

Status as of 7.1: Dead, long before the present story. Not mentioned in 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya content.

His name survives mainly through Xiao, Xianyun, Moon Carver and the clothing he designed. At the 2024 Lantern Rite (limited event) the Mingxiao Lantern was made in his yaksha form, and the in-game character Musheng, asking who the lantern commemorates, is told it is Menogias, a deadly yaksha who was also well-versed in clothing design and tailoring.

242.content:
Mikoshi Chiyo (also: Chiyo, Torachiyo, Chiyo the Tiger-Bite, Tiger-Bite, oni maiden): An oni warrior of the Mikoshi Clan who fought beside the Raiden Shogun Ei in the cataclysm 500 years ago. Swallowed by a beast of sin, she tore her way out but came back tainted, drew her sword on Ei, and was struck down.

Later tradition remembers her as "Chiyo the Tiger-Bite", worn down over the years into "Torachiyo", and often as a male rebel. Her disgrace stained the Mikoshi name, yet Ei still remembers her as a friend.

Status as of 7.1: Gone for 500 years. Ei says Mikoshi Chiyo is gone; legends disagree on how she died.

Only a fragment of her nightmare, tied to a severed horn, remained, until it was put to rest in the limited 5.4 event.

243.content:
Mikoshi Nagamasa (also: Nagamasa, Katsuragi-Slashing Nagamasa, Inspector Nagamasa, Tatarasuna Inspector, Mikoshi Nagamasa the Inspector): Mikoshi Nagamasa was an Inazuman who lived around the time of the cataclysm, the adopted son of the oni warrior Mikoshi Chiyo and one of the Yougou Three. As Inspector at Tatarasuna he forged the nagamaki Daitatara Nagamasa and, to end the Tatarasuna Mystery, executed his loyal yoriki Katsuragi with it. Both man and sword became known as "Katsuragikiri Nagamasa".

He is remembered as upright, stubborn and obsessed with cleansing his family name. His story connects directly to the Wanderer, who once lived among the workers at Tatarasuna as the nameless "kabukimono".

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago. He is a figure of history who survived the Tatarasuna Mystery, is said to have lived to old age, and is known now only by the epithet that still clings to him and his sword.

Tatarasuna's notes, the Arsenal and the sword's diagram are what remain of him. According to Inagi Hotomi, most people surnamed Mikoshi in Inazuma City today are his descendants.

244.content:
Miscislav (also: Blood-Devourer, Gorynishche, Son of the Mountain, King Miscislav, King of the Volkodlak, King of Beasts): Miscislav, the Blood-Devourer, was a gigantic Volkodlak and king of the Miscislavli Alliance. His war against Emperor Monomakh ended when Monomakh killed him, which let Monomakh become the Belyi Tsar and the undisputed ruler of Snezhnaya.

Fae chroniclers called him Gorynishche, "Son of the Mountain", for his size. His skull is said to be kept in the Zapolyarny Palace Treasury.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about three thousand years, killed in the third campaign of his war.

His family survived; the wiki lists the Snezhnograd NPC Bogatov as a descendant. Some of his kin held power under the Tsar.

245.content:
Mistress of Chenyu Vale (also: Former Mistress of Chenyu Vale, Demon Lord of Chenyu Vale): The Mistress of Chenyu Vale is the unnamed god who once ruled Chenyu Vale and the ancient city of Chizhang, presiding over its beasts, spirits and adepti. When the Archon War came, she turned cruel, fought Morax, and was defeated and sealed. Her name has been forgotten.

She is known only through legend: Fujin's recollection, a book of mountain ballads, and a few item texts. Fujin insists she was not evil and once made many dreams come true, and blames the Archon War for what she became.

Status as of 7.1: Sealed, according to local legend, beneath Mt. Lingmeng since the Archon War. Her fate after the war is not confirmed in-game. Not mentioned in 6.x Nod-Krai or 7.0-7.1 Snezhnaya content.

Her people forgot her. The traces left are the lost Rainjade Rite, the ancient ruins at Chizhang Wall, the ballad, and the old shelters and murals. The miasma Lingyuan later stirred up by disrupting the spirit veins, in an effort to restore Fujin, belongs to Lingyuan, not to the mistress.

246.content:
Mouun (also: Yuna Mouun, Mouun the Shrine Maiden, the whalesong master of Watatsumi): Mouun was a shrine maiden of Watatsumi Island's Yuna Clan and, in the island's folk-tunes, the greatest master of whalesong. She won the great whale Daikengyou to Watatsumi's side, led the island's first navy with her twin sister Ayame, and was killed in the war against the Raiden Shogun.

She is known through a book, a weapon description and a second text on Touzannou, all set in the Archon War, so her story comes as legend. She is long dead and does not appear in any present-day scene.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the Archon War. Her songs, the Mouun Shrine on Watatsumi and the bow named for her remain.

She is not seen in any quest as a living person. Her sister Ayame disappeared into the sea after a last stand, and canon gives no further word of either of them.

247.content:
Nabu Malikata (also: Goddess of Flowers, Lord of Flowers, Mistress of Flowers, Moon Maiden, Mistress of Pushpavatika, Queen of All Oases, Mistress of Flowers and Oases, Mother of Dreams): Nabu Malikata, the Goddess of Flowers, was a god of Sumeru's desert in the Archon War era and a former Angel who created the Jinn and the first Khvarena. With King Deshret and Rukkhadevata she formed the Three Eternal Companion-Gods. Celestia burned her to ashes for giving Deshret forbidden knowledge.

She is known only through the memories of others, item text and relics. She is said to have had beautiful horns and wore an amethyst crown, and in the Chinese and Japanese text the Sabzeruz Festival is named after her ("Birthday of the Goddess of Flowers"). Remains of her body ended up in Collei and were removed in 6.6.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years. Her last stray remains, inside Collei, were removed in 6.6.

Nothing of her acts on its own. Her legacy lives on in the Jinn, the Pari, the Sabzeruz Festival and Aaru.

248.content:
Nameless Bard (also: The Boy and the Whirlwind, the young bard of Old Mondstadt, the lad living in that storm-shrouded city, Nameless Shepherd): A boy of Old Mondstadt, about 2,600 years ago, who played the lyre and longed to see birds fly beyond the hurricane wall of the God of Storms Decarabian. He raised the revolt against the tyrant with a tiny wind spirit and a handful of allies, and died as the tyrant fell. The spirit became Barbatos, the Anemo Archon, and remade himself in the boy's likeness.

He has no voiced lines of his own and no recorded name in plain text. Everything about him comes from Venti's own story quest, the character stories, and weapon and artifact texts. The wiki calls him 'the Nameless Bard'.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 2,600 years. He died in or just after the fall of Decarabian's tower. No grave, remains or ghost are shown. Nothing in canon through 7.1 revives or contradicts his death.

He is remembered only through Venti and a few item texts. Mondstadt's history credits the Anemo Archon, not him. His final melody is described as the origin of Mondstadt as a nation and as an ideal: 'all who hold freedom in their hearts are its musicians'.

249.content:
Narzissenkreuz (also: the Master, Incomplete Order of the New Cosmos): The "Master" of the secret Narzissenkreuz Ordo, about four hundred years before the main story: a made being holding the mind of the scholar Rene de Petrichor, meant to merge all Fontainians and escape a foretold apocalypse. The Traveler and Ann defeat him in In the Wake of Narcissus.

He is not a conventional villain. By his own account he never acted from selfishness, and the people he harmed were hurt by a plan that began as an attempt to save everyone. His followers knew him by a title ("Master") rather than a personal name. The name Narzissenkreuz is also that of the hero in a story (the hero Narzissenkreuz and the evil dragon) that Alain had Rene and his friends act out as children.

Status as of 7.1: In Rowboat's Wake (4.2) he guided the Traveler and Ann to Annapausis, was recognised by Mary-Ann as Rene, then, his power spent, said farewell and was left to rest there. Nothing later is recorded as of 7.1.

After his defeat in the Primordial Sea (Waking from the Great Dream) he lost control of it and called his work an empty dream, wishing to return to the time before the Narzissenkreuz heroes set out. He agreed to help Ann.

250.content:
Nepla Korolevitsna (also: Nepla): Nepla Korolevitsna was a human woman warrior from before the Archon War who guarded a human clan. Defeated by the young Monomakh and Filipov, she became Filipov's wife and died of illness long before him.

The Snezhnayan chronicles remember her as a formidable champion, and her memory was later used against Filipov by Rotwang and by the Abyss.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead. Thousands of years later, Filipov trusted the monk Rotwang after he summoned her apparition, and during the Cataclysm the Abyss took her form to tempt Filipov.

Filipov exposed that imitation by falsely claiming she had a mole behind her ear; the copy produced one, and he laughed and refused her.

251.content:
Nibelung (also: Dragon King, Dark Dragon King, Second Descender, Takoja Ianikuinen, Formidable Father, Dark-Winged Lord, King of all Dragon Lords, The One): Nibelung was the Dragon King, a primeval dragon born with Teyvat who ruled it before the Heavenly Principles. He made the Three Moons to govern while he searched the stars for a defence against the Abyss. He came back bearing the Abyss, waged the war of funerary flame about 6,000 years ago, and was destroyed.

He is counted as the Second Descender, and Aksinya calls him the true Primordial Human, a seat that no one has filled since. He never appears in person. Everything known comes from dragons who served him, the moon goddesses he made, murals and old books, and these sources disagree about whether he was a saviour, a tyrant or both.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. The Heavenly Principles destroyed him at the end of the war of funerary flame, about 6,000 years ago.

His seat as Primordial Human has stood vacant ever since, according to Aksinya. Attempts to fill it include Hyperborea's Belyi Tsar project (7.0). The Abyss he brought into Teyvat is still there.

252.content:
Nikolay (also: Nikolay Snezhevich, Kolya): Nikolay Snezhevich, called Kolya, was a corporal in the Fatui's Ninth Company, sent to investigate the Chasm. He was an orphan of the House of the Hearth and the brother of Katarina. He disappeared in the depths and is presumed dead.

He is never met in person. The Traveler learns of him through Katarina, fragments of his diary and a letter he wrote her.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead. His last diary entry records a severe leg wound and being found by a Shadowy Husk, ending with an apology to Katarina.

A fallen rock blocks the path where he was last known to be. Katarina went to look herself and was not found; only his treasured letter lay on the ground.

253.content:
Niwa Hisahide (also: Armory Officer Niwa, Sir Niwa, Mr. Niwa): Niwa Hisahide was Armory Officer of Mikage Furnace in Tatarasuna, Inazuma, about 400 years ago, and head of the Niwa Clan of the Isshin Art. He disappeared during the Tatarasuna Mystery and was blamed for it; in truth Dottore killed him.

He is known to the present only through documents, local belief and the memories Nahida shows the Traveler and the Wanderer in the Interlude Chapter (3.3). Official records say he was modest, clever and gifted at running people and land.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 400 years, killed in the Tatarasuna Mystery. As of 7.1 no new information about him has appeared.

Public belief at Tatarasuna and in Aqaba's paper was that he vanished or fled. The Wanderer learned the truth when Nahida showed him Dottore's own memories.

key: Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash
254.content:
Och-Kan (also: Sacred Lord, Python King, Holy Sovereign, Tide-Turning Sacred Lord, Dragon of the City of Flowing Ash, Lord of Cinder Keep, Lord of the Cinder City, Cocouik): Och-Kan was the half-dragon Python King and Sacred Lord of ancient Ochkanatlan. A follower of Xbalanque, he became a tyrant and was overthrown by the Scarlet-Eyed Youth; in 5.2 the Traveler meets what remains of him.

He was a dragon with a human soul, bred by his father Kukulkan to be the next Pyro Sovereign, who instead gave his life to protecting humans. Before his fall he split his mind from his body: the mind became the dragonspirit Cocouik, the body an Abyss-twisted dragon.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. In Moment of Awakening (5.2) he merged his mind and body, died and left his remains in Ochkanatlan. As of 7.1 no sign he is alive.

His spirit rejoined the Night Kingdom, where in Journey of Stars and Flames (5.3) he and Bona helped the Traveler's party against the corroded depths, saying the light would guide the way through the endless darkness.

255.content:
Ormazd (also: Ohrmazd, Ormazd Shah, Shah of Gurabad, the shepherd king): Ormazd was a shepherd who, favoured by King Deshret and the Jinni Liloupar, became the first vassal-king of Gurabad. He grew into an ordinary tyrant, and Liloupar's revenge started with his death at a banquet.

He is remembered in the desert as the founder of the City of Kings and, in the Eremite tales, as the doomed father of Shirin and the adoptive father of the hero Parvezravan.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years. His remains and those of his heirs are said in the Tale to lie in crypts beneath the sands of Gurabad.

Gurabad itself fell two generations after him. His murals and tablets in the ruined Temple of Deshret and the Desert of Hadramaveth are the main surviving record.

256.content:
Orobashi (also: Orobashi no Mikoto, Orobaxi, Watatsumi Omikami, Great Serpent, Serpent God, Profane Serpent, Coral-Adorned Serpent): The coral-bodied Great Serpent who was god of Enkanomiya and then of Watatsumi Island, known as Watatsumi Omikami. He fell to Ei near the end of the Archon War, and his remains still scar Yashiori Island.

Watatsumi's people still worship him as their guardian, even though he died at the hands of the Raiden Shogun who now rules them. He is known only from legends, books and ruins; he never appears alive in the game.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since about the end of the Archon War, roughly 2,000 years ago. His remains lie on Yashiori Island, with his skull at Serpent's Head.

His lingering power became the Tatarigami, the phenomenon of storms, lightning, corruption and madness on Yashiori Island. The Shogunate later used his Crystal Marrow in smelting at the Mikage Furnace. Watatsumi still worships him; its Watatsumi Goryou Matsuri, which halts the spread of Holy Soil, uses a Jade Coral Branch said to come from his body.

257.content:
Papa Wrench (also: Mr. Shesternin Sr.): Papa Wrench was the name taken by Mr. Shesternin Sr., a Snezhnayan who lost his memory and drifted through Nod-Krai with a caravan before settling by Blue Amber Lake on Lempo Isle. A gentle, generous mechanic who charged little or nothing for repairs, he was Aino's teacher. He is dead by the time of the story and appears only through other people's accounts.

He never appears in person. His workshop, built from an underground warehouse beneath Blue Amber Lake, and the machines he made for a sick child remain as his legacy; they are the setting of the world quest The Tale-Telling Heart.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He died before the events of Version 6.0, of chronic illness and grief following Tinet's death. As of 7.1 nothing further is told about him.

258.content:
Parsifal (also: Phantom Thief, gentleman thief, Chief Mate, Master Parsifal, Parsifal of Mondstadt): Parsifal was a legitimate heir of an aristocratic house of Old Mondstadt who became the city's gentleman thief, robbing the rich to give to the poor. Betrayed by his half-brother Eberhart, he fled to Liyue, became the Skipper's Chief Mate and died with him fighting a sea monster.

He is known only from item texts: the Alley Flash and Alley Hunter weapons, the Wine and Song ballad book, the Iron Sting weapon, the Heart of Depth artifact set and one line in a Dragonspine journal. The commoners' songs remember a happy ending; the artifacts tell a bleaker one.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; he and the Skipper died killing a sea monster. He has no part in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content.

Mondstadt never learned his real ending. The ballad Wine and Song, popular in the alleys and taverns, ends with the thief and the witch toppling the nobles and warming each other's days forever. The text itself calls this a vulgar, carefree tale with a happy ending that bards offered as a motivational story.

259.content:
Parsifal the Great (also: Great Magician Parsifal, the Great Magician): Parsifal the Great was the stage name of a Fleuve Cendre thief who became a famous Great Magician in Fontaine more than 500 years ago, performing with her sister, who played the assistant 'Josephine'. She joined Eduardo Baker at Poisson and, after the siege, asked for a trial by combat against the Champion Duelist Marfisa, probably dying in it.

She is known only through item texts and has no speaking role.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead, after her last duel more than 500 years ago.

She is not a character in any quest and was not found in 5.x, 6.x or 7.0-7.1 story content.

260.content:
Parvezravan (also: Kisra, Kisra Parvez, Kisra Parvezravan, Spirit of Victory, Spirit of Unceasing Victory, King of Gurabad): Kisra, called Parvezravan, was a feared conqueror known as the Spirit of Victory and the second-to-last king of Gurabad. Born of the Jinni Liloupar and raised by a divine bird, he took the throne after Ormazd died and his rule ended with Gurabad swallowed by the earth.

Eremite history remembers him as both a hero and a tyrant. His fear of his own son brought about his death and the city's destruction.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years; Gurabad fell with him.

His reign is preserved in the ruins of the Desert of Hadramaveth: the Records of Gurabad, the Dogma of the Brass Mask, labour records in the Hypostyle Desert and the Nameless Tablets, readable after the Dirge of Bilqis (3.4).

261.content:
Pervases (also: Yaksha Pervases, Copper Sparrow): Pervases was a junior Yaksha, one of Rex Lapis's adepti, who died in the Archon War. His spirit lingered in a crane statue at a ruined adepti temple near Mt. Tianheng, where the Traveler met him during the quest Butterfly's Dream.

He gave up the censer and seven-star lamps he had used for the Mortal Lingering ritual so the Traveler could perform the Dream Trawler ritual against the impostor Starsnatcher.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; his spirit has gone dormant again in the statue.

Wang Ping'an, repentant, later restored the temple. In the Hereafter quests the Traveler brings grilled fish to pay respects there; Xiao is also found at the temple, and the wiki says he returns there to ponder the Yakshas' fate.

262.content:
Petronilla (also: Protector of Justice, Protector of Order, Clorinde's master, Ms. Petronilla): Petronilla was a Marechaussee Hunter who took in and trained the child Clorinde, later Fontaine's undefeated Champion Duelist. By night she was the black-cloaked vigilante known as the "Protector of Justice". She disappeared on Clorinde's tenth birthday and her fate is unknown.

She is known only through memory: Clorinde, Navia and Furina recall her in the Silent Night story quest (4.7), and Clorinde's character stories add detail. She never appears in person.

Status as of 7.1: Missing since the night of Clorinde's tenth birthday. As of Version 7.1 canon has not said what happened to her.

She did not come to collect Clorinde from Navia's house that night. Clorinde searched her rooms and old training grounds and waited several days before asking Callas for help, but even he could find nothing. Petronilla left Clorinde a dark blue cape with the Marechaussee Hunter insignia (not the black one she wore), a necklace engraved with Clorinde's name, her sword, and one of the Hunter keys handed down through the generations.

263.content:
Phobos (also: Grand Symphony, Discordant Symphony, That-which-once-was-Sybilla, The Phobos): Phobos is the Grand Symphony Remus created from Sybilla to free Remurians from fate. It became a corrupt guide that led Remuria to war and ruin, and was destroyed in 4.6.

Called the "Discordant Symphony", it took in Remurian souls through golden Ichor and gave their owners immortal golem bodies. Its guiding voice is the origin of the war that sank the nation.

Status as of 7.1: Destroyed for good in Fortune Plango Vulnera (4.6), freeing the souls it held.

Before that, it re-emerged beneath Petrichor and replaced locals' souls with Remurian ones. The Traveler played the Requiem for Scylla, allowing Cassiodor, Boethius and the other Remurians to pass on.

264.content:
Pir Kavikavus (also: Nara Pir Kavikavus, Kavikavus): Pir Kavikavus was a celebrated scholar of the Akademiya's Kshahrewar darshan in Sumeru, a prodigy who became a Herbad before turning thirty. He is remembered as the last scholar to enter a Ruin Golem for systematic research; an accident there lost his findings, and Kshahrewar has been in decline since.

He is idolised by current Kshahrewar researchers such as Jazari, and a research prize for scholars under forty bears his name.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead; his research was lost in the accident. His reputation lives on in Kshahrewar, and the rediscovery of his paper in Version 3.0 revived hope in the darshan.

The Akademiya has not raised Kshahrewar's funding in the years since his passing, according to a public message board. Jazari hopes to win the Pir Kavikavus Prize and to follow in his footsteps.

265.content:
Preobrazhensky (also: V. A. Preobrazhensky, Professor Preobrazhensky): Preobrazhensky (V. A. Preobrazhensky) was a high-ranking researcher of the Fatui's Armory Palace who studied Kuuvahki and fallen moon fragments in Nothing Passage on Lempo Isle, Nod-Krai. He was the bitter rival of Professor Anton Zarkovich Karnatsky. A surviving soldier's note blames the experiments of the two men for a catastrophe that killed them and almost the entire Fatui 6th Company.

He appears only through written traces found in the Colors of Emptiness world quests (6.0): a furious signed note, camp diaries and a dying soldier's last letter. He never appears in person and has no profile text of his own.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He died in the Nothing Passage catastrophe, before the events of Colors of Emptiness; the Traveler finds only his notes in an area afflicted by Kuuvahki phenomena.

Nothing is known of his remains or burial. Canon through 7.1 adds no further information about him.

266.content:
Princess of Sal Vindagnyr (also: the Princess of Sal Vindagnyr, Sal Vindagnyr's princess, Varuch's daughter): She was the daughter of the high priest Varuch and the last princess of Sal Vindagnyr, a mountain kingdom buried by snow long before the Archon War. Gifted with prophetic dreams, she painted what she foresaw as frescoes; when the Skyfrost Nail fell and the great tree shattered, she tried to save it and died in the cold.

Her name is lost, and canon knows her only through the things she left on Dragonspine: three treasure boxes, the carvings, and the texts of the weapons Frostbearer and Snow-Tombed Starsilver. She is a figure of quiet, unfinished hope rather than of deeds.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, thousands of years ago; she died in the fall of Sal Vindagnyr. Nothing in canon places her in any later era.

Her grave is believed to lie near the entrance to Starglow Cavern on Dragonspine, where the Scribe's Box is found; the small island where she is said to have died has a sword in the ground, owner unknown.

267.content:
Priscilla (also: Eberhart's servant, Priscilla of Mondstadt): Priscilla was a servant in Old Mondstadt with a past she hid, taken in by the illegitimate heir Eberhart and bound to him as an accomplice in his plot against the aristocracy. She was to light a warning beacon on the cape if the plot was discovered. The nobles found out first and she is presumed to have died.

She is known only from a Dragonspine journal, a Hidden Exploration Objective and a weapon text; she has no profile or model and never speaks in game.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead, killed by the nobles who uncovered Eberhart's plot, a thousand years ago. No later appearance.

268.content:
Prokhor Trubetskoy (also: Trubetskoy, Grand Duke Trubetskoy, Governor of Nod-Krai): Prokhor Trubetskoy was a Snowland Fae Grand Duke and Governor of Nod-Krai before the Cataclysm. He is remembered as greedy and unpopular, and as the adoptive father of Brahe, who became the third Reed Miller.

He is known only second-hand, through the quest The Raven's Legacy, Brahe's notes at Reed Miller's Great Treasure and a remark by Euphrosiniya.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago. Euphrosiniya says he fell fighting alongside the Belyi Tsar.

His palace site now holds Piramida. Nothing in canon to 7.1 shows him alive.

269.content:
Ragnvindr (also: the Dawn Knight, Ragnvindr the Dawn Knight, Dawn Knight Ragnvindr): Ragnvindr, the Dawn Knight, lived in Mondstadt about a thousand years ago under the Aristocracy. A squire to a noble knight, he came to loathe the nobles' neglect of the poor, joined Vennessa's rebellion and later turned the aristocrats' baths into a library. The Ragnvindr Clan, owners of the Dawn Winery, bear his name.

He is known through ballads attributed to him and through the texts of items such as The Flute and the Favonius Codex, not through any scene in the game. His title came from a sword-dancing gladiator who inspired him.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about a thousand years. His name survives in the Ragnvindr Clan, the Dawn Winery and the ballads attributed to him.

As of 7.1 the Ragnvindr Family still runs the Dawn Winery,.

270.content:
Ravenwood (also: Second Knight of Boreas, Knight of Boreas (second), Ravenwood's Longing): Ravenwood was the second Knight of Boreas, a Mondstadt blacksmith's son who, as a boy, followed the nameless Wandering Knight around, and years later took up the heavy claymore under Boreas's name. His valor earned the Wolf Spirit's recognition, and when the old aristocracy tried to return he defended the city, making the title a lasting role in the Knights of Favonius.

He is known from a weapon text, a character story and Varka's Lupus Majoris quests; he has no profile, model or lines of his own beyond brief voice echoes. His greatsword became the model for later replicas, including the Ferrous Shadow.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; no text gives the manner or date. His sword symbol is among those at the memorial Varka crosses in 6.4, and his echo shields and guides Varka through the Ley Lines.

Rostam and, much later, Varka also held the title. In the Lonely Warrior quest Ravenwood's voice says the title of Boreas must find an heir, and later his Ley-Line shield replaces Rostam's.

271.content:
Red-Haired Warrior (also: the red-haired warrior, flame-haired warrior, warrior clad in iron): A nameless red-haired warrior who wandered into Decarabian's walled Old Mondstadt, became one of the first to plot against the God of Storms, and stood with the Nameless Bard, the wind spirit, Amos and Gunnhildr when the tower fell.

He is remembered in song but not by name, and the later Ragnvindr Family is generally taken to descend from him. After the victory he turned away from the new god.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead or lost to history; canon gives no date, place or manner of his end, and no one living remembers him by name.

His memory survives in the Windblume Festival, whose flower was once his side's secret sign, and in the red-haired line of the Ragnvindr Family.

272.content:
Reizenbou (also: Great Tengu of Mt. Yougou, chieftain of the Yougou Tengu, Yougou Tengu chieftain): Reizenbou was the Great Tengu of Mt. Yougou and chieftain of the Yougou Tengu about five hundred years ago. She mentored three young trainees (the Yougou Three), bore a daughter, Teruyo, and served as bodyguard to the Kitsune Saiguu after losing a race to her. Her bow Thundering Pulse, a gift from the Shogun, passed to the swordsman Takamine the Mistsplitter through a bet.

When the cataclysm took the Kitsune Saiguu, Reizenbou blamed her own failure to protect her, left her daughter behind and withdrew into the Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates, refusing to face humanity again. She appears only in item texts and an underground puzzle area, never in person.

Status as of 7.1: Not seen alive in the present. After the cataclysm she withdrew into the Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates beneath Araumi and refused to appear before people again. Her ultimate fate is not stated.

The Empty Boat of a Thousand Gates is a one-time domain whose description calls it a tengu warrior's final abode, and says the boat became the cage in which the person spent the rest of their days. Shaft of Remembrance records that she went into this exile enraged at her failure as Lady Saiguu's protector, leaving Teruyo behind. Earth Kitsune Statue lines near Araumi record Harunosuke and others worrying about where "Master Tengu" had gone while she was out fighting.

273.content:
Remus (also: Sebastos, God King of Remuria, Imperator, King of Fortuna, Philharmonic God, King of the Immortals, Glorious King): The God King and Sebastos of Remuria, an empire that once ruled the waters of ancient Fontaine. A god from Sumeru, he founded Remuria, created the Grand Symphony to escape a prophesied fall, and brought about the very ruin he feared.

Remuria's golden age is credited to him: farming, great cities and temples, music and art. He shared rule with four human Harmosts. Remuria is named for him, and by the time of the Traveler's visit he has been dead for millennia, remembered through legend, books and dream-memories in Petrichor.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years. He was lost when Remuria sank. In Petrichor's Canticles of Harmony quests (4.6) his memories reach the Traveler as dreams, and his Requiem finally destroys Phobos.

The Traveler shows a particular affinity for his power. Together with the freed Scylla, now in an Ichor body that still holds the Requiem's power, they carry out his last wish and destroy the Grand Symphony. The souls of the Remurians trapped in it, Cassiodor's among them, move on to be reborn as mortals in the future.

274.content:
Renault de Petrichor (also: Mayor Renault, Renault, mayor of Poisson): Renault de Petrichor was the last of the de Petrichor family to govern the town of Petrichor, and later the mayor of Poisson. He was the father of Rene de Petrichor and died with his wife in the Siege of Poisson during the cataclysm 500 years ago.

He is a mentioned figure only: Tiepolo, Petrichor's present-day Doge, tells his story, and he appears in the description of a photograph taken by the reporter Karl Ingold.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed at Poisson about 500 years ago.

With the line gone, Petrichor drifted toward becoming a forgotten fishing village until Ruggiero, its first Doge, rebuilt it. Townspeople at the time blamed closer ties with the outside world for the decline.

275.content:
Rene de Petrichor (also: Rene, René de Petrichor, Rene of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo): Rene de Petrichor was a brilliant young Fontainian from the cataclysm era. He believed his calculations pointed to a coming apocalypse, founded the Narzissenkreuz Ordo to survive it, and finally dissolved himself into a being known as Narzissenkreuz, or the Master.

He is known only through the notes, Enigmatic Pages and artifact text he left behind, through what the Master later says and does, and through later accounts such as Sandrone's. He was the son of the mayor of Poisson, a close friend of Jakob Ingold, and a childhood friend of Alain and Mary-Ann Guillotin.

Status as of 7.1: Dead as an individual; his consciousness lived on only in Narzissenkreuz, the Master, who faded away to rest in Annapausis at the end of the 4.2 "In the Wake of Narcissus" quests.

Before that, the Master was defeated by the Traveler and Ann in the Primordial Sea, helped them reach Mary-Ann in Annapausis, and was forgiven by her as Rene. Centuries earlier the Ordo had been ruled an illegal extremist group, its tower sealed, and the Master left in the Primordial Sea beneath it. His legacy outlives him: in the 6.3 Nod-Krai Archon Quest, Sandrone (the Marionette) has studied Rene's records and Alain's notes on him, adopted some of his ideas, and tries to use his Four Orthants theory to predict the world's future.

276.content:
Roland (also: Bloodstained Knight, White Knight, Mightiest Knight of Boreas): Roland, a noble-born Knight of Favonius under Arundolyn 500 years ago, was taught by Rostam, the Wolf Pup. The White Knight was expected to become the mightiest Knight of Boreas, but blood blackened his armor, he became the Bloodstained Knight and left Mondstadt for good.

Item texts trace the rest: he found Khaenri'ah's cursed people, called their fate the ultimate injustice and pledged himself to the Abyss. In 6.4 an Abyssal imitation wearing his name leads the Wild Hunt in Nod-Krai and Mondstadt, while his real final act, sealing his last comrades' resting place, is shown in a spirit scene.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 the real Roland is presumed dead, with no recorded end after he joined the Abyss in Khaenri'ah. In 6.4 only an Abyssal imitation of him fought Varka, and it dissolved.

His sword is among the swords laid out in the Ley-Line space Varka crosses, standing alone among the memorial blades of earlier Knights of Boreas and Grand Masters. Varka left Rostam's unsent letter at its foot. A wiki search found no 7.0-7.1 content about him.

277.content:
Rongzhao: Rongzhao was an exorcist of Liyue, the younger brother of Boyang and an ancestor of Yelan. He fought in The Chasm during the cataclysm about five hundred years ago and came home alive, but without his sanity.

He is known only through the Interlude Chapter (2.7), where Yelan goes looking for the ancestor who vanished and learns what happened to both brothers.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead as of the present day. No account of his death exists in canon.

Yelan's family lore says that an ancestor of theirs found brief relief from his madness only when passing Wangshu Inn, where Xiao lives. She suggests it was the comforting, evil-warding presence of the yaksha.

278.content:
Rostam (also: Wolf Pup, Knight of Boreas, Rostam the Wolf Pup): Rostam, the 'Wolf Pup', was a Knight of Favonius and Knight of Boreas in Mondstadt 500 years ago. He devised Favonius Bladework, the sword style the Knights still practise, and stood at Grand Master Arundolyn's side as his closest friend and deputy. He loved the singer Rosalyne, and died in the cataclysm.

He is known only through item texts and Varka's 6.4 story; he never appears as a living character. What survives is a stern, dutiful knight who did the quiet work for the Lion of Light, and whose death turned two people close to him, Arundolyn and Rosalyne, into very different people.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed in the cataclysm 500 years ago after twenty-three years of service.

His sword style and the Knight of Boreas title live on in the Knights of Favonius. In 6.4, Varka leaves Rostam's unsent letter at the base of the Black Sword, a shadow of Roland, and tells it that Rostam and Arundolyn never forgot him.

279.content:
Ruggiero (also: Master Ruggiero, first Doge of Petrichor, great sage Ruggiero): Ruggiero was a Fontainian scholar who set out to prove the Grand Symphonies existed, came to Petrichor looking for the legendary Faded Castle, and later rebuilt the town and founded the Consilium Sapientium, becoming its first Doge. He is long dead.

Today's Doge, Tiepolo, credits him with restoring the town's fortunes. Scholars like Bravais admired him, though Bravais thought Fontaine's poor academic climate meant his work was never fairly judged.

Status as of 7.1: Dead by the present day; he died several hundred years before it.

His legacy is the Consilium Sapientium, the elders' council that assesses all of Petrichor's affairs and from which the Doge is chosen, and the town itself. His notes in the Faded Castle, and Bravais's annotated copy of his research, survive.

280.content:
Saarelainen (also: Third Descender, Stranger of Winter's Day, the Third Descender): The Third Descender, a visitor from beyond Teyvat who loved Anastasya (the future Cryo Archon) and fathered the line that became the Khaenri'ahns. To save her he let the Heavenly Principles turn his body into the seven Gnoses, and was erased from memory.

Almost nothing of him survives except through his consequences: the Gnoses, the Archon system built on them, Stellar Linchpins and the Khaenri'ahns' descent. By 7.1 the Tsaritsa treats him as the origin of the objects she collects.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed by the Heavenly Principles after his bargain; his remains are the seven Gnoses. The Tsaritsa holds six of them as of 7.1.

Anastasya says that Gnoses cannot coexist for long with the Ley Lines and one day will be driven out; she hopes to gather all seven to open his seal. The Pyro Gnosis, which the Traveler reports (citing Mavuika) has returned to the Ley Lines, was still not in her hands in 7.1.

281.content:
