Sakkuk (also: Peace-Reforger, Chief of the Children of Echoes, Baraka bearer, Daughter of the mines): Sakkuk of the Nanatzcayan was the first hero to join the Scarlet-Eyed Youth in the rebellion against King Och-Kan, about 2,000 years ago. She outlived every companion, became Chief of the Children of Echoes, and at the youth's request erased his name from history.

She considered herself the weakest of the heroes, yet she was the last one alive. In old age she gathered treasures that her lost friends had left, honoured their graves each year, and finally vanished into the night with the Craftsman's genuine works.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for roughly 2,000 years, presumably of old age, after disappearing into the night. Her name survives on the Peak Patrol Song, the Children of Echoes' mining rhythm and the Unfinished Reverie artifacts.

Her titles of "Peace-Reforger" and Chief of the Children of Echoes survive in the item texts and wiki. No appearance or mention was found in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content as of 7.1.

282.content:
Sanhaj (also: Sanhaj Kompore, Kompore, Border Master Sanhaj): Sanhaj Kompore was a Border Master and high priest of the Masters of the Night-Wind and one of the six warriors who joined Tenoch against the Abyss in the cataclysm, about 500 years ago. He was born silent, became a storyteller of ritual and warning, and died with Tenoch when a miniature Night Kingdom was detonated at the Mare Jivari. His Ancient Name, Bidii, now belongs to Ororon.

He is remembered as cunning, quiet by nature and gifted at weaving old tales into warnings, and as a man who shaped what people were allowed to remember.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the cataclysm, about 500 years ago. His spirit persists in Natlan's clairvoyant traces: it appeared to Ororon when he awakened Bidii and again when Mavuika and the six heroes drew on the divine throne.

Citlali describes his remaining spirit as still very strong, so strong that contacting it during clairvoyance startled monsters nearby. The Traveler later found his final resting place in the Pyro Archon Temple, during The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc.

283.content:
Sasayuri (also: Great Tengu of Yougou): Sasayuri was a beloved tengu general of Inazuma, known as the Great Tengu of Yougou, who served the Raiden Shogun and was killed in the war against the Watatsumi people of the Great Serpent Orobashi.

Sasayuri is known only through second-hand text and brief cinematic glimpses; no dialogue exists.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the war against Orobashi, long before the game's present. Remembered by Ei and in Watatsumi's accounts. No later developments in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

284.content:
Scarlet-Eyed Youth (also: Crimson-Eyed Youth, Red-Eyed Youth, second Pyro Archon, Haborym, God of War): The Scarlet-Eyed Youth was the second Pyro Archon, a man of the Flower-Feather Clan from Tlalocan who rose against Och-Kan, the Python King of the Cinder City, about 2,000 years ago. He gathered heroes, burned Ochkanatlan, and afterwards returned to the sacred flames. At his request his name was erased from history.

Natlan remembers him as the proof that a human can become a god, but not by name. Even his divine name, Haborym, is a title shared by Pyro Archons in the sources.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago. By the 7.1 cutoff he is a legend and an unnamed predecessor of Mavuika; a poem foretells that he will emerge from the flame when Natlan faces crisis again, but this is a poets' belief, not an event.

Mavuika proclaims the Night Wars in the name of Haborym, the title of the Pyro Archon.

285.content:
Scylla (also: Fell Dragon Prince, Bane Dragon, Prince of Dragonborn, Prince of Vishaps): A vishap prince of Remuria's age, once Remus's secret ally, sealed in stone at the capital's gates for millennia. The Traveler freed him in the Sea of Bygone Eras.

Proud and formal, he scorns Remurian arrogance, yet is warm to the "little ones" who freed him and holds a long grudge against Boethius.

Status as of 7.1: Free and alive as a soul in the Sea of Bygone Eras after Phobos's destruction.

He plans to meet the new Hydro Dragon one day and asks the Traveler to visit.

286.content:
Sea Gazer (also: Perfected Lord Who Resounds in Sea and Lives in Rosy Clouds): Sea Gazer was an adeptus of Liyue who lived long before the present and is dead. He liked to sit and look at the ocean, travelled and dug up treasures, and made the Fantastic Compass, a device for sealing evil monsters. Shenhe says he was very close to Mountain Shaper.

He is known by his epithet alone. Liyue's folk histories remember his lost abode in Lisha, which holds his rarest finds, among them a great piece of Sunset Vermillionite sought for the Jade Chamber's rebuilding.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago; the cause and time are not given.

His abode in Lisha is abandoned but its defences still work. He is remembered by a few adepti and by scholars who read old records.

287.content:
Shirin (also: Shirin of Gurabad, Demon Queen, queen of Gurabad): Shirin was the last queen of Gurabad, in the Great Red Sand, Sumeru: the half-Jinni daughter of the tyrant Ormazd and the Jinni Liloupar, wife of Parvezravan and mother of Shiruyeh. Legend casts her as the poisoner of her father and a demon queen. Sumeru quest canon shows her instead as a pawn in her mother's revenge, who lost her mind.

Two accounts compete: a popular legend, preserved in the book The Tale of Shiruyeh and Shirin, and the sadder account Liloupar herself gives the Traveler.

Status as of 7.1: Her fate is unknown. After Gurabad fell she is not recorded dying; the legend places her as a restless spirit, while Liloupar says her children are still in Gurabad and lonely. Nothing in canon through Version 7.1 settles it.

Liloupar enters the gate of Gurabad alone at the end of Memories of Gurabad, saying her children, Shirin and Shiruyeh, are probably lonely. She later takes her own life in the Sumeru Archon Quest, apparently without finding them.

288.content:
Simurgh (also: the divine bird, Divine Bird Simurgh, master of Khvarena): Simurgh was a divine bird made from a shard of Khvarena, the purifying light Nabu Malikata created to oppose the coming cataclysm. When the Abyss threatened the Amrita, she gave up her form and became countless Khvarena, the ancestors of the Pari.

She is known only through artifact texts and the words of the Pari. She has no recorded speech in the game.

Status as of 7.1: Dead as an individual. Her form was shattered during the cataclysm roughly five hundred years ago, and her Khvarena lives on in the Vourukasha Oasis and in the Pari.

Her last wishes were carried out by Zurvan, who gathered Khvarena and fought Abyssal monsters in the wilderness. In the 3.6 quest Khvarena of Good and Evil the Traveler helped cleanse the Harvisptokhm and seal the Sign of Apaosha. Nothing found for versions up to 7.1 changes her status.

289.content:
Skipper (also: The Skipper): The Skipper was a sea captain of Liyue, about a thousand years ago, who made his name hunting sea monsters and hanging their bones from his ship. He lost his crew and his beloved navigator to one enormous beast, rebuilt a crew, and years later went out to kill it. His real name is unknown.

He is remembered through the book series Tales From the Waves, the greatsword Serpent Spine and the Heart of Depth artifact set. His chief mate in the last voyage was the exiled Mondstadt aristocrat Parsifal.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about a thousand years; his ship and crew were never seen again.

His revenge succeeded: the monster's body was found. Folk tales and the book series keep his story alive in Liyue.

290.content:
Skybracer (also: Yixiao Daotian Zhenjun, The Perfected Lord who Moves the Heavens by Guiding the Sky, the stag adeptus, the antlered adeptus): Skybracer was an adeptus of Liyue, a deer-formed illuminated beast, who died in the Archon War. He is remembered for a legend told at the Lantern Rite: to save the village below Mt. Tianheng from a collapsing mountain, he had his own antlers, a gift of Morax's divine essence, cut off and driven in to hold the peak up, then went back to fight until he died. He is known only through that legend and the deer-shaped Mingxiao Lantern of the 1.3 Lantern Rite.

Nothing is recorded of his personality, earlier life or any quest of his own. Everything about him is told second-hand by Madame Ping, who knew him, by the storyteller Xiaoyan and by the scholar Soraya, and the tellings do not fully agree.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the Archon War; only the legend and the Lantern Rite lantern remain.

In the 1.3 Lantern Rite event the city's Mingxiao Lantern was dedicated to him, a huge deer-shaped lantern. Madame Ping hoped the builders made the antlers large enough, since they were his pride, and joked that he was a show-off who would be pleased. Xiao, asked whether he would see it, brushed it off as a short-lived human creation. A search of the soil of Mt. Tianheng in the event found no sign of antler fragments. No later appearance was found as of 7.1.

291.content:
Sohreh (also: Dastur Sohreh): Sohreh was a Dastur of the Sumeru Akademiya's Amurta Darshan. Roughly four hundred years ago she joined a field research team to Ardravi Valley, partnered with the Trainee Dastur Zandik, and died during the expedition. She is known only through notes and records left in the rainforest.

Her own note is cheerful: she praises the area's biodiversity, names a micro-scarab species the "Nahidad Scarab" ("the Dendro Archon's Boon"), complains that her partner's rigid Darshan has nothing in common with Amurta, and then records a pleasant evening of talk and a planned picnic. Later records describe her injuries and death.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about four hundred years. Her cause of death was never settled in the records that survive.

The autopsy notes list lacerations, bruising and a fractured hyoid bone, with mechanical asphyxia as the stated mechanism, yet the investigators could not determine what killed her. Zandik was later suspected of murdering her, and disappeared after that.

292.content:
Sojourner (also: the Sojourner, the lyrist, the harpist, the traveler of the Wanderer's Troupe): Community name for the Fontaine-born lyrist of the Wanderer's Troupe, told in the Resolution of Sojourner artifacts. He left privilege to wander, fell in love in Mondstadt, and died covering his comrades' retreat when the troupe's uprising failed, about a thousand years ago.

Canon never gives him a personal name and refers to him as the traveler, the lyrist or the harpist. His instrument, The Stringless, was both a harp and a bow.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about a thousand years. After the uprising he stayed behind, repelling pursuit so that his comrades could flee, and fell in the fighting. He does not appear in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content as far as the sources read show.

Most troupe members were slain or captured and enslaved, and the aristocracy later cut the instrument's strings to silence it. Legend says he had no regret about dying nameless in a foreign land, only that he found true love and never got to sing another love song. Mondstadt's sky, the texts note, was the same as the sky of his homeland.

293.content:
Solovei (also: Silvestr Petrovich Solovei, Silvestr, Silve, Torchforger, the first Torchforger): Silvestr Petrovich Solovei, the Torchforger, was a Snezhnayan noble who, about five hundred years ago, fought the Abyss in Nod-Krai with the priestess Aila's aid, won the borderlands' autonomy from the new Cryo Archon and founded the Lightkeepers. Long dead, he survives in a statue, item text, letters and a recording.

He was the childhood friend of Avrelian, the first Reed Miller, and acted out of loyalty to that friend's dream of a "paradise" for Nod-Krai's poor. He became the Lightkeepers' first Starshyna. The Lightkeepers' oath and the Arrow of Terpikeraunas, given to him by Aila, are his legacy.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; apparently died peacefully of old age centuries before the present, having founded the Lightkeepers. A statue of him stands in Piramida. Nothing in canon through 7.1 brings him back.

The Lightkeepers honor him as their founding Starshyna. His funeral, held by the Lightkeepers he trained, was quiet at his own request; Brahe attended and Aila did not.

294.content:
Sonnet (also: Goddess of the Iridescent Moon, youngest of the Three Moons): The youngest of the three ancient Moon Goddesses, ruler of the Iridescent Moon. Terrified of dying after her moon was shattered, she fused her soul with the Abyss; the result was the Crimson Moon that Khaenri'ah's Crimson Moon Dynasty revered. She finally died after Columbina and the Traveler freed her marrow.

Her story is one of fear and pain turned into a source of power: the Crimson Moon was worshiped as a conduit to the Abyss, while the goddess behind it was suffering.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. She died in the Crimson Moon's hidden domain, reached from Nod-Krai, after the Traveler purified her marrow in the Crimson Moon's hidden domain (6.1).

Her marrow, the Iridescent Moon Marrow, passed to Arlecchino. Dottore later stole it, and Columbina took it back and returned it to Arlecchino after defeating him (6.2-6.3).

295.content:
Suavegothe: Suavegothe was a hardliner of Fontaine's 'old regime' who opposed the Iudex Neuvillette for letting Melusines live and serve in the Court of Fontaine. In a memory shown in the 4.1 quest Ever-Surging Memories she helps the plot that frames the Melusine detective Carole, and is later killed by the avenging Vautrin.

She is known only through that memory, which Neuvillette's Hydro power stirs up in the Fountain of Lucine. Nothing is stated about her life outside the conspiracy.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about four hundred years, killed by Vautrin according to the wiki. The remaining trace of her is the memory stored in the Fountain of Lucine.

She is not mentioned in later Fontaine Archon Quest content or in 6.x and 7.0-7.1 content as read for this file.

296.content:
Sundjatta (also: Nare Magan Sundjatta, Chief Sundjatta, 52nd Chief of the Children of Echoes): Nare Magan Sundjatta was the 52nd chief of the Children of Echoes (the Nanatzcayan miners and smiths) and one of the six heroes who followed Tenoch against the Abyss in the cataclysm, about 500 years ago. He bore the Ancient Name Baraka, now held by Xilonen, and died in the heroes' final battle.

Canon shows him as a leader who preferred stability among the tribes, a craftsman who put his knowledge into writing, and a comrade who raised a toast to his own coming death.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the cataclysm. His spirit appears in the present, in Despair Engulfs the Heavens, as one of the six heroes whose power Mavuika and the modern heroes channel in the Stadium of the Sacred Flame.

Xilonen inherited Baraka. In that scene the pairs speak together; Sundjatta and Xilonen's line is 'Bearing an ancient blessing'.

297.content:
Sybilla (also: Golden Bee, Sybilla the Golden Bee, the infallible oracle): An Angel, once Celestia's envoy guarding the silver tree at Meropis, who foretold Remuria's glory and doom to Remus and gave her life for the Grand Symphony, Phobos.

Reduced by ages to a golden bee, she greeted the wandering god Remus in the ruins and guided him to build Remuria. Her gentle wish for human happiness, without a will to shape it, became Phobos.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; her life and wisdom became Phobos in the Remurian era, long before the game. Phobos was destroyed in the 4.6 quests.

At the end of Fortune Plango Vulnera a spirit-guiding golden bee leads the Traveler up from the sea, but canon does not say it is Sybilla.

298.content:
Taika (also: Lord Taika, Taika of the Flower-Feather Clan): Taika was the strongest fighter of the Flower-Feather Clan, the mountain tribe of Natlan. When the Cataclysm began he left his pregnant wife and became an adventurer, leading a band to Ochkanatlan in search of a fabled weapon against the Abyss. He never returned.

He is known only through remnants: an artifact's flavor text, the memory of Och-Kan and an NPC's remark about "our leader". His daughter Bona later followed his trail.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He and most of his team died in Ochkanatlan during the Cataclysm era, long before the present.

A Flower-Feather Clan rescue team may have been sent for the survivors, but canon does not say if it arrived in time. Only the young mystic Liriwu is recorded as having returned alive.

299.content:
Takamine the Mistsplitter (also: Takamine, Konbumaru, Mistsplitter, the Mistsplitter, Kirigiri Takamine): Takamine the Mistsplitter was a swordsman and inveterate gambler of Inazuma who lived about five hundred years ago. Nicknamed Konbumaru, he served the Raiden Shogun as a Hatamoto, wielded the sword Mistsplitter and loved the shrine maiden Asase Hibiki. He vanished fighting the dark forces during the cataclysm.

He is remembered in a children's rhyme listing famous martial artists (Arataki of the Front Gate, Iwakura the Successor, Kitain the Serpent, Takamine the Mistsplitter). His story, a promise and a wager that went unfulfilled, is told through the texts of Mistsplitter Reforged, Thundering Pulse, Shimenawa's Reminiscence, Emblem of Severed Fate and Hamayumi.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about five hundred years. He fought the dark forces with the Shogun in the cataclysm, was cut off and overwhelmed, and did not return for many years.

Years later something returned from the Abyss to the forest where he and Hibiki had agreed to meet. She, no longer young, loosed an arrow charged with power through it. Kagura's Verity, in Yae Miko's voice, says what returned was the darkened remains of his soul and that wiping it out was needed to protect Inazuma. Hibiki appears to have seen it as saving him (Shaft of Remembrance).

300.content:
Tao Dou (also: Bune, God of the Underworld, God Tree Tao Dou, Mt. Tao Dou): Tao Dou, divine name Bune, was a god of Liyue who lived before and during the Archon War. It took the form of a giant tree on the summit of a divine mountain and stood before the realm of the dead, where it was called the god of the underworld who could pacify the forces of life and death. Dragged into the Archon War, it was defeated and purified by the Eight Adepts, and its remains became the border between the living and the dead.

Liyue still tells the story as the tale and opera "The Sanctification of Tao Dou". Its remains are said to lie beneath Mt. Qingce, held down by the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula and the Seven-and-Eight-Gates Method. Most of what is known comes from storytellers and from Liyue characters repeating legend, so treat details as folk history rather than recorded fact.

Status as of 7.1: Dead in the sense of having been defeated and purified long ago; its remains survive as the border between life and death. Those remains lie beneath Mt. Qingce, suppressed by the Hidden Palace of Zhou Formula. As of 7.1 no new information has appeared.

During Springtime Charms (5.3, limited-time) fetor leaked from that border near Wuwang Hill, sickening the elderly of Qingce Village. Hu Tao, with the Ministry of Civil Affairs and friends, re-enacted a scaled-down version of the Sanctification to repair the affected stretch of the border. In the later Lanternlit Ode to the Silver Moon epilogue, Zibai recognises the name Bune when she visits Wuwang Hill with the Traveler.

301.content:
Tenoch (also: Tenoyollotzin, The hero Tenoch): Tenoch (Tenoyollotzin) was a scarred, battle-hungry warrior of Natlan, exiled from the tribes for his battle-mania. Wielding a huge obsidian-inlaid club, the Talking Stick, he gathered a hero from each of six tribes against the Abyss about 500 years ago, and died at Mare Jivari by letting the Bakunawa eat him so Sanhaj could destroy it from within.

He is known only through legends, item text, memory scenes and one world quest; he never appears alive in the present. He accepted his exile as deserved and nonetheless put himself in front of the war.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 500 years. As of 7.1 his remains lie with Sanhaj's in the Pyro Archon Temple, which the world quest The Last Survivor of Tenochtzitoc reveals. Because he had lost his Ancient Name before dying, the Ode of Resurrection could not return him.

Mavuika says he was laid to rest in the soil of his homeland with other fallen warriors and civilians, and that his story is still told. His club was among the mementos Mavuika sacrificed for the Contending Fire, according to the weapon page's account of the Archon Quest.

302.content:
Tholindis (also: Tholindis of Khaenri'ah, Rerir's fiancee): A Khaenri'ahn researcher in the Universitas Magistrorum's Moon Marrow lab and the woman Rerir loved. She secretly descended from the Crimson Moon Dynasty, helped other descendants escape, and vanished into the moon's reflection on the day the Cataclysm began.

She is known only through memories in the Song of the Welkin Moon Archon Quest chapter (Nod-Krai, 6.1) and as a surviving soul in 6.3. Her story explains why Rerir became a Sinner.

Status as of 7.1: Dead in body since the fall of Khaenri'ah. As of 7.1 her soul persists in the moon's reflection, separated from Rerir by time.

Her research helped Columbina move through the reflection toward the past. Nothing after 6.3 shows her again.

303.content:
Tupac (also: Tupac the Giant, Giant of the People of the Springs, Umoja bearer of the cataclysm): Tupac, called the Giant, was a mountain-sized warrior of the People of the Springs. He was the last of six heroes to join Tenoch against the Abyss, fought in the final battle, and brought the fallen Mavuika to the Sacred Flame before dying on his feet.

He bore the Ancient Name Umoja, "unity", which now belongs to Mualani. Tribal songs remember him for hot springs raised from the ground and a fight with a two-tailed whale; in the animated short he is cheerful, loyal and unafraid of death.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He died on the steps of the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, still standing, about 500 years before the present day. His Ancient Name Umoja is now borne by Mualani.

As of 7.1 nothing contradicts his death. He survives as a Name projection, tribal ballads, item texts and the memory of the other cataclysm heroes.

304.content:
Uenuku (also: Treader of the Rainbow, Rainbow King, Rainbow Treader): Uenuku, the Treader of the Rainbow, was a hero of the People of the Springs and the first known bearer of the Ancient Name Umoja, "unity". Legends about his bond with a water sprite disagree on how his story ended.

He is counted among the original Six Heroes of Natlan, who stood beside Xbalanque against the dragonlord Xiuhcoatl. Later Meztli lore calls him the Rainbow King; his descendant Tupac and, five hundred years after Tupac, Mualani carried his Name.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead as a historical person; canon does not say how he died. He lives on as the first bearer of Umoja and in Meztli legend.

Nothing about him has appeared in canon since the 5.0 texts, and nothing places him in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

305.content:
Ukko (also: the scribe of Sal Vindagnyr): Ukko is a figure from the final days of Sal Vindagnyr, the civilization of Dragonspine. The Princess' Box text names Ukko as someone the dying princess felt sorry to have seen her in her state. Ukko is probably the scribe whose bitter words fill the Scribe's Box and who recorded the fall in the Ancient Carvings, and the last survivor.

Canon never states Ukko's role directly; the scribe identification is an inference.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years, last survivor of Sal Vindagnyr. A Frostarm Lawachurl bearing the name Ukko can be fought on Dragonspine, but canon does not confirm it is the same person. No connection to 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content found.

The Scribe's Box mention of Khaenri'ah, a new nation without gods, is among the oldest in-game references to it.

306.content:
Unnamed Gladiator (also: the gladiator, Eberhart's gladiator, Eberhart's slave): The Unnamed Gladiator was Eberhart's slave champion in Old Mondstadt, about a thousand years ago, a peerless fighter in the arena who nearly won his freedom. He kept fighting out of attachment to his master and fell to Vennessa, a gladiator of the Lawrence Clan. His story is told by the Gladiator's Finale artifact set and the polearm Deathmatch.

Canon gives conflicting accounts of how his last fight ended.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about a thousand years. Most texts say Vennessa pierced his heart in his last bout. Luther's journal on Dragonspine fears the same fate for himself. No 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content connects to him.

Gladiator's Destiny gives a different ending, in which he is spared and sets off free; treat these as unresolved accounts.

307.content:
Urakusai (also: Yuurakusai, Urakusai of the Six Kitsune, the Daiyouko Urakusai): Urakusai was a kitsune in Inazuma, a cultured Daiyouko famed for his stories, art and tea, and author of the original Chronicles of the Six Kitsune. The Kitsune Saiguu befriended him, then banished him five hundred years ago for a "grave mistake". In 2.5, his memory, preserved in the Ley Lines, wrote a novel through a human author and spoke through the Traveler.

He is warm, theatrical and teasing, delighted by humans' striving, and prone to practical jokes. He called Yae Miko a mischievous little kitsune, and conceded defeat to her in friendly fashion.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; his memory lingers in the Ley Lines at the Sacred Sakura's roots, and after 2.5 he is gone again, saving energy for the Hyakkiyakou.

He is no longer present after A Centuries-Long Dream. The wiki says his memory stirred after rifthounds gnawed at the roots of the Sacred Sakura in the earlier quest Transient Dreams, leaking memories from the Ley Lines. The one-time Hyakkiyakou happened in Banquet of Parting, in which the youkai memories were sent off.

308.content:
Varuch (also: Varuch of Sal Vindagnyr, the priest of Sal Vindagnyr, the Priest's Box narrator): Varuch was the priest of Sal Vindagnyr, a mountain nation that once stood on what is now Dragonspine, and the father of its princess. The wiki treats him as probably its last king-priest. He is known from a single item text in which he climbs the peak for guidance while his nation freezes, and he is never heard from again.

He has the least recorded about him of the figures in Sal Vindagnyr's story; most of what is said of him comes through his daughter's texts. He is presumably dead and does not appear in any quest.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead, thousands of years ago, probably on the mountain.

His traces vanish after he sets out for the summit; no source says he returned or what he found.

key: Lady of the Vila of Veneter
309.content:
Vaselisa von Strivozha (also: Vaselisa Strivozha, The Pure One, Saint Strivozha, Grand Duchess of the Vila, Lady of the Vila of Veneter, Sword Saint): Vaselisa von Strivozha, called the Pure One, was the first Grand Duchess of the Vila and ruled the Silver Court of Veneter, a haven as renowned as Kitezhgrad. Many fae hailed her a merciful saint.

In the story told by the weapon Breezeborne Refrain, her gentleness hid a calculated plan to keep the wind free.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about three thousand years. Her house and the Vila still exist.

House Strivozha kept power under the Pale Star Court and after the Cataclysm. Her songs and her sainthood are remembered. Her fate is not stated.

310.content:
Vautrin (also: Captain Vautrin, Special Security and Surveillance Captain): A human Garde captain of Fontaine roughly 400 years ago who worked beside the Melusine Carole, killed those who framed her, was found guilty by Neuvillette, and founded the Mutual Aid Network in prison.

Cold and stern on the surface, he was a loyal and earnest officer who quietly came to share Carole's dream of humans and Melusines living together.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about four centuries; remembered through Neuvillette's memories and the Mutual Aid Network.

His Medal of Peace design survives as the Network's badge. Neuvillette still regrets the verdict.

311.content:
Venerare (also: Venerare of the Lawrence Clan, Venerare Lawrence): Venerare led the Lawrence Clan in the early days of Mondstadt, roughly 2,600 years ago. Under her guidance the people raised a tall statue in the city plaza for the Anemo Archon's descent, with an oath to protect Mondstadt carved beneath it. She is known from item text only.

She is a named ancestor, not a voice: no quest or voice-over features her. Her descendants later betrayed the ideals she stands for.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about 2,600 years; the manner of her death is not recorded.

She does not appear in any present-day quest, and no text for 6.x or 7.0-7.1 mentions her.

312.content:
Vennessa (also: Falcon of the West, Lionfang Knight, Liontooth Knight, first Dandelion Knight, Hero of Mondstadt): A Muratan enslaved in Mondstadt about a thousand years ago, she fought as a gladiator, then with Barbatos' help led the rebellion that ended the aristocracy and founded the Knights of Favonius as its first Grand Master.

Her legend lives in the song The Legend of Vennessa, Jean's title, the sword Aquila Favonia and the great oak at Windrise. She is a mentioned figure only.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; said to have ascended to Celestia at Windrise, where a vast oak now stands. Mondstadt honours her as its hero.

The great oak, called the Symbol of Mondstadt's Hero, is thought to have grown where she ascended; Dr. Edith repeats the legend that she became the goddess who protects Mondstadt for eternity. Legend says she became the Falcon of the West, one of the Four Winds. The Temple of the Falcon at Windrise is dedicated to that title.

313.content:
Viaghara (also: Lord of the Forest, Greater Lord of the Labyrinths, Owner of the Moon-Mirrored Spring, Lord of All Animals, true tiger): Viaghara was the first lord of the forest, a divine "true tiger" born in Dharma Forest in the age when Greater Lord Rukkhadevata founded her rainforest. It was both her friend and the ruler of the forest's animals, and it helped protect the Varuna Contraption.

Its stripes were said to resemble blazing flames, or to change constantly like the forest's branches. After Viaghara, a line of other lords of the forest followed, each reshaping the palace of the labyrinth, until the last of them died defending the forest during the cataclysm 500 years ago. Rishboland Tigers have borne the "tiger" name since.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long ago. How Viaghara died is not recorded.

Successor lords of the forest continued the line and the last died in the cataclysm. Afterwards Rishboland Tigers took up the "tiger" name and still protect the forest and the Aranara in imitation of the old lords, with only a fraction of their might.

314.content:
Wandering Knight (also: Wolf Knight, First Knight of Boreas, Knight of Boreas (first), nameless knight of Boreas): The Wandering Knight was the first Knight of Boreas, a nameless warrior who arrived in Mondstadt about a thousand years ago, in Vennessa's time, with the wolf Boreas as his companion. He drank in taverns, hunted beasts and demons, refused the Knights of Favonius' repeated offers and left without a successor. The tales of the Wolf Knight grew from him.

He is known mostly through three weapon texts and a 6.4 echo. Canon never gives his name, face or origin, and Mondstadt's own tellings of him disagree with each other.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed dead; his time is a millennium past. His sword symbol is among the Knights of Boreas and Grand Masters commemorated in the memorial space Varka crosses in 6.4, and his echo in the Ley Lines still tells Varka that his path is not finished.

He left no succession plan. Ravenwood later earned the wolf spirit's recognition and the title passed within the Knights, though few holders were ever truly recognised by Boreas. A wiki search found no 7.0-7.1 content about him.

315.content:
Wanjiru (also: the great runner, Uwezo bearer of the cataclysm, Kayeke's companion): Wanjiru, "the great runner", was a warrior of the Collective of Plenty and the first of six heroes to join Tenoch against the Abyss. She bore the Ancient Name Uwezo, "power", with her Tatankasaurus companion Kayeke, and died in the final battle five hundred years ago.

She was Mavuika's friend and wrestling partner before Mavuika became Pyro Archon. Iansan now carries her Name.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, about 500 years before the present day; her Name Uwezo now belongs to Iansan.

She is known only through memories, a Name projection tied to Iansan, item texts and the 5.3 short. Nothing places her in 6.x or 7.0-7.1.

316.content:
Waskar (also: Waskar the younger twin, the younger of the twin heroes): Waskar was the younger of the twin heroes of Natlan's Collective of Plenty. He joined the Scarlet-Eyed Youth against the insane king of Ochkanatlan, stood first against the darkness on the day of the revolt, and was killed in the fighting.

Every detail comes from Unfinished Reverie artifact text. His elder brother Atawallpa mourned him loudly and bitterly.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He was slain in the war against the king of Ochkanatlan, long before the Cataclysm.

Atawallpa died sometime afterwards, and Sakkuk, whom the text calls the frailest of the heroes, outlived them all.

key: One Entombed With the Primal Fire
317.content:
Xbalanque (also: Haborym, First Pyro Archon, The First Sun, Lanque, One Entombed With the Primal Fire, Dear Beloved Sun): Xbalanque (divine name Haborym) was the first Pyro Archon and God of War of Natlan, about 2,000 years ago. He began as a mortal outlander, slew the Pyro Dragon Xiuhcoatl, and bargained with Ronova, the Shade of Death, to write the rules Natlan uses against the Abyss. Natlanese remember him as "The First Sun".

Natlan's records describe him as wise, brave and upright. When he returned for one day in 5.3, he turned out to be warm, joking and informal. He introduced himself as "Dear Beloved Sun", or "Lanque" for short, and called himself an old man.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; as of 7.1 his soul is in the Night Kingdom. In 5.3, after Natlan defeated the Abyss, Ronova honoured his bet and he returned for a single day in a borrowed body, then departed at sunset.

He possessed a boy named Mausau, entered the Pilgrimage tournament, dueled Mavuika and rode her flamestrider across Natlan. Before he left, he said he would take Mavuika's words, that the peaks reached by earlier generations become the everyday goals of later ones, back to share in the Night Kingdom. Nothing in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 brings him back on-screen. Later content mentions him only in texts and memories.

318.content:
Xiphos (also: Blade of Tulaytullah, Hero of Tulaytullah): Xiphos was a legendary hero of Tulaytullah, a prosperous desert city of sapphire domes and emerald gardens, in the age after King Deshret's kingdom fell. Born a crown prince and hidden as a servant, he became its famed "Blade of Tulaytullah" and was killed in a duel by an exiled prince hired by the city's rivals.

He wielded a sword said to hold a bloodthirsty Jinni, saved many maidens from monsters and took treasure from them in the process. After his death Tulaytullah fell within a few years, leaving only its garden, which survives as the Garden of Endless Pillars.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years, slain in a duel.

His killer left the desert for the rainforest afterwards. The Key of Khaj-Nisut was lost in the desert, and Tulaytullah fell within a few years.

319.content:
Xiuhcoatl (also: Flamelord, Pyro Dragon Sovereign, Pyro Dragon, Lord of Light and Heat, Master of Light and Flame, Master of Flame and Wisdom, Fallen Dragon): Xiuhcoatl, the Flamelord, was the Pyro Dragon Sovereign. He ruled Natlantea, ancient Natlan's dragon civilisation, and wielded light, heat, wisdom and the primal flame (Phlogiston).

In his last, Abyss-corrupted era he built Huitzilopochtli, meant to burn all Natlan into pure Phlogiston so the Abyss could never touch it. Kukulkan and Xbalanque opposed it. Saurians with the Flamelord's Blessing carry his bloodline.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. His remains lie in the Heart of the Sacred Mountain beneath the Great Volcano of Tollan; no new Pyro Dragon Sovereign exists as of 7.1.

During the 5.5 world quests, the Traveler and the Saurian Little One, who carries his blood, brought both Golden Entreaties to Huitzilopochtli. Kukulkan offered Little One the chance to become the Pyro Dragon Sovereign renewed, but the activation was cancelled and the array shut down. In the 5.3 Archon Quest, Gosoythoth briefly took his form and was defeated by Mavuika and the Traveler.

key: the crimson princess of the snow
320.content:
Yalyane Morevna (also: Knyazhna of Blood, Princess of Blood, Morevna, first of the Snegovik, the crimson princess of the snow): Yalyane Morevna, the "Knyazhna of Blood", was the first of the Snegovik and princess of the House of Hesperides in the age after Hyperborea fell. She was feared for slaughtering fae kindreds, yet sheltered human clans, and she taught the young future Belyi Tsar the spear.

She is a figure of legend more than record. The General History of Snezhnaya admits she barely appears in authentic annals and that most accounts come from folk song. She vanished without a trace before Kitezhgrad was founded, and later Snegovik remember her as their ancestor.

Status as of 7.1: Missing and presumed lost long ago: she vanished without trace before Monomakh founded Kitezhgrad, and no canon account says what became of her.

As of 7.1 she has never appeared in person. She survives in the General History of Snezhnaya, in two weapon stories (Frostbreath, 7.0; Winter's Heavy Heart, 7.1) and in the Snegurochka's own memory of her as ancestor.

321.content:
Yelena (also: Vijava, the scholar Vijava): Yelena was a former Fatui member and the elder sister of Kirya. To spare him the rapid aging that a Delusion inflicts, she deserted with him and settled in Fontaine, where she posed as a Sumeru scholar named Vijava. She grew the flower used in the Auguste perfume, which drove Fontaine's 'Perfume Mania' about twenty years ago, and died in a fire she set to hide the secret.

Her story is told entirely in retrospect through Emilie's Story Quest, 'Floral Debt, Blood Due' (4.8), mainly via Kirya and the surviving partners.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for about twenty years as of the Pomum de Ambra Chapter; she died by self-immolation to protect the perfume's secret.

Weeks after the quest, Emilie released a modified Auguste named 'Yelena' in her honour. Kirya concluded her death was ultimately his own fault, since she died protecting him. Nothing in versions through 7.1 adds more.

key: eighth head of the Yun Family
322.content:
Yun Huang (also: Huang of the Yun Family, eighth head of the Yun Family): Yun Huang was the eighth head of the Yun Family, a Liyue house of weaponsmiths, about five hundred years ago. The only child of Yun Hui, she was a headstrong martial artist who took over the forge herself when her father joined the Liyue Qixing. With Han Ce she is one of the two central figures in the Blackcliff weapon descriptions.

She is known only from those item texts: a woman who inherited a family business at a hard time and, with Han Ce, found a way to keep it alive.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; her death is not described. What remains is the Blackcliff line of weapons and her house, which later drifted from smithing towards the performing arts.

Yun Jin is a later member of the same family, whose generation has few forgers left.

key: seventh head of the Yun Family
323.content:
Yun Hui (also: Hui of the Yun Family, seventh head of the Yun Family): Yun Hui was the seventh master of the Yun Family, a Liyue house renowned for forging weapons. After the Cataclysm he and the smith Han Wu designed the improved Prototype weapons, and he later left the forge to his daughter Yun Huang when he joined the Liyue Qixing.

He is known only through weapon descriptions: the Prototype series, Prototype Amber (the catalyst he named), and the Blackcliff weapons in which his daughter and the Han family appear.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead. Nothing describes his death; his work survives as the Prototype weapons and the Yun Family's later history.

Over the centuries the Yun Family drifted from weaponsmithing towards the performing arts, and by Yun Jin's generation few members still forged.

324.content:
Yupanqui (also: Firethief, Fire-Bringer, Yupanqui the Firethief, Yupanqui the Fire-Bringer): Natlan's legendary Firethief: a boastful young swordsman who grew into a quiet, one-eyed veteran and died after stealing the Turnfire from the tyrant Och-Kan. The Scions of the Canopy claim him as their ancestor.

He is known only through tales and relic texts, never in person. The tribe tells it as the story of a hero who set his people free and paid with his life.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead, he is remembered as a hero and as a cautionary story about looking back.

His fire burned a hundred days, according to the Scions' story, until it pierced the Ley Lines and fell into the Night Kingdom, where it is said to burn still. The elders say it lights the way to the next life and that the dead must be purified by it before they are reborn. Children say it is just a story.

325.content:
Zumurud (also: Verdant Lord, the Verdant Lord Zumurud): Zumurud, called the Verdant Lord, was a ruler of several desert city-states in the Great Red Sand, in Sumeru, thousands of years ago. He is known solely from Primal Obelisk inscriptions. He was the son of Muzaffar, one of the Deys of Orghana (the city later called Port Ormos), and was raised in the forest, so he did not speak the desert language. He dreamed of turning the desert green and fathered 99 children.

Nothing is recorded of his personality, appearance or death; what survives is a dream, a royal duty to produce heirs, and the glory later claimed for his children. He is long dead and cannot be portrayed as a speaking character from canon voice material.

Status as of 7.1: Dead for thousands of years. He is mentioned only in ruin inscriptions and has no known presence in the present day.

Nothing about him appears in Version 6.x (Nod-Krai) or 7.0-7.1 (Snezhnaya) content that this entry could confirm.

326.content:
Acatl (also: Chief Acatl, Chief of the Collective of Plenty): Acatl is the chief of the Collective of Plenty, Natlan's farming and bodybuilding tribe. He is a tall, muscular man in a horned wrestling mask who welcomes visitors warmly and answers doubts with an invitation to the ring.

His tribe lives beside the Great Volcano of Tollan in Atocpan, the tribe farthest from the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. He treats formalities lightly and prizes courage, perseverance and the will never to back down.

Status as of 7.1: Alive; chief of the Collective of Plenty in Atocpan as of 7.1.

After the Abyss war's end (5.3) he hosts guests at his tribe. No later appearance in 6.x or 7.0-7.1 content was found.

327.content:
Adorno (also: Benevolent Knight, Grandpa Adorno, Captain Adorno): The genial, aging 'Benevolent Knight' and 5th Company Captain of the Knights of Favonius; dies in 6.6.

He has outlasted his fighting days and refuses to be treated as finished.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since A Knight's Resolve (6.6).

His headstone reads 'Here rests the Benevolent Knight'; the title was buried with him.

328.content:
Aedon (also: Illuga's nightingale, Solovei's nightingale): A glimmering golden nightingale who lights the way for the Lightkeeper Illuga, and who was once the bird of the legendary Torchforger Solovei.

Aedon is no ordinary messenger bird: Alia says he travelled with Solovei five hundred years ago and was changed by the Sampo Mill into a kuuvahki being. Today he warns Illuga of danger, shows hidden paths and drives off the fog of the Wild Hunt.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and with Illuga in Nod-Krai.

Still Illuga's companion at the cutoff; no separate role.

329.content:
Ajaw (also: K'uhul Ajaw, Almighty Dragonlord, Aj Imuch' Paxlaq Lahun, Undying Wings of Lofty Isolation, Kinich's companion): A tiny pixel dragon in sunglasses bound to the Saurian Hunter Kinich. He calls himself the Almighty Dragonlord and insults everyone; in truth he is probably the Tenth Sovereign Lord, weakened and sealed in a wristband.

He cannot act without Kinich's command, but he lends Dendro-flame in battle and hovers at Kinich's side the rest of the time. Most of Natlan finds him vulgar; many simply ignore him.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and bound to Kinich in Natlan, still unwilling to name which Lord he was.

He accompanies Kinich everywhere, including a smuggling case in Fontaine and Natlan's celebrations. Nothing shows a change in the contract as of 7.1.

330.content:
Aksinya (also: Court Jester of the Belyi Tsar, Royal Jester): A human survivor of Hyperborea raised by the Belyi Tsar as his "Court Jester", who led the Hvergelmir institute and tried to freeze love unchanging until the Traveler stopped her.

Courteous and wry, she introduces herself as a lowly jester while quietly planning to blanket the world in shadow.

Status as of 7.1: Missing in the Shadow Realm as of 7.1, having fallen there with the Primordial Human.

Her plan failed. Before the fall she reflected on her philosophy and wished only for a small world with the Primordial Human.

331.content:
Alice (also: A, Merry-Witch, Dodo-King, Great Adventurer of the Realms, Mother of the Most Adorable Klee, Sustainer of the World's Borders, Crimson Chronicle, Defender of Old Mondstadt): Cheerful, theatrical founder of the Hexenzirkel (codename "A"), author of the Teyvat Travel Guide, mother of Klee and keeper of Teyvat's borders.

Long heard only through objects, she came in person in Nod-Krai (6.2) because the three moons were straining Teyvat's borders.

Status as of 7.1: Alive; called back to Teyvat's borders after Nod-Krai (6.2).

Reachable through the Dodocommunication Device.

332.content:
Alkindi (also: Sage of Spantamad, Spantamad Sage): Alkindi is the current Sage of Spantamad, the Akademiya's school of elementalism and ley lines. Blunt, elderly and industrious, he is an old rival of the retired professor Cyrus.

In Version 6.6's Archon Quest Act IX he helps the Traveler investigate the Irminsul anomaly through the ley lines.

Status as of 7.1: Alive; part of the Akademiya's response to the Irminsul crisis.

He helped dissect an abnormal ley line blossom and later argued that the Akasha Terminal must be reactivated with a substitute for the Dendro Gnosis.

333.content:
Allpa (also: Elder Allpa, Tepal (assumed identity)): Flower-Feather Clan elder and veteran Qucusaur rider who, after her son Tepal died chasing flight, built the Phlogiston Wings and tried to seize the tribe from Chief Mutota.

Publicly the respected organiser of the flying trials; privately she masked herself as "Tepal" and ran a workshop fuelled by Phlogiston from captured Qucusaurs.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, jailed with her followers in part of the workshop after the failed coup.

The workshop is mostly dismantled.

334.content:
Amina (also: Chief Amina, Chief of the People of the Springs): Amina is the chief of the People of the Springs, the hot-spring tribe of Natlan. She is earnest, inventive and responsible, the self-declared serious one among carefree people.

She took over from her grandfather after the elders voted for her, and she tries to lead the tribe towards a different future.

Status as of 7.1: Alive; chief of the People of the Springs at Toyac Springs as of 7.1.

After the war she says many people were lost; she is busy designing a new stage and reinforcing patrols.

335.content:
Andrei (also: Northland Bank manager in Liyue, Andrei of the Northland Bank): Andrei manages the Northland Bank's Liyue Harbor branch. By day he pitches loans and savings; off the clock he relaxes at the docks and admits he is growing fond of Liyue.

He is a minor open-world NPC. His dialogue sets the Northland Bank's polished sales line against the resentment many Liyue locals feel toward a foreign bank, and shows an ordinary Snezhnayan abroad who is charmed by Liyue but keeps repeating his loyalty to Snezhnaya.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1: manager in Liyue Harbor, at the bank by day, the docks by night.

His lines have not changed with the story; he is not tied to the Snezhnaya chapter events.

key: Great Wolf King of the North
336.content:
Andrius (also: Boreas, Lupus Boreas, Wolf of the North, Great Wolf King of the North, Dominator of Wolves, God of the North Wind, Lord of Wolvendom, Kingwolf of Boreas): An ancient wolf god of the far north, now a spirit in Wolvendom: the Wolf of the North among Mondstadt's Four Winds.

He rarely shows himself and guards Wolvendom's wolves, among whom the human boy Razor grew up.

Status as of 7.1: A spirit in Wolvendom, watching his wolves and Razor.

In 6.4 an Abyssal assault from the north weakened him and he sent a Wolf Spirit token to Varka.

337.content:
Ann (also: Oceanid Ann, Ann of Narzissenkreuz, Knight Ann): A small Oceanid of Fontaine, once the storybook 'knight' sent to rescue a princess, who learned the story was a dream and became her own person.

She is a gentle, brave, slightly naive companion who admits she is bad at thinking things through but chooses to believe the truth when it is offered honestly.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, travelling with Mary-Ann.

After the 4.2 quests she and Mary-Ann plan a trip; the group later separates (Seymour and Mamere reach Nod-Krai). In 6.7 (limited) she joins Sandrone's tea party.

338.content:
Antei (also: Antigonus, Antigone, Transgressor): Antei (Antigonus) was an apprentice Jibashiri, one of the judges and enforcers of Byakuyakoku in Enkanomiya. Convicted of stealing "Before Sun and Moon", he broke out of the hanging prison to prove his innocence. He is now a fierce-tempered, blunt Shade of Tokoyo afterimage who does not know he is dead. He appears only in the world quest Antigonus.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; only a Sinshade afterimage remained in Enkanomiya. After the Traveler tells him he is an afterimage and is innocent, he accepts it and fades while reciting broken lines about divine law and unfortunate people relying on the gods. No later appearance was found. The Traveler promised to tell the world he was innocent.

339.content:
Anthon (also: Tartaglia's younger brother): Anthon is one of Tartaglia's younger siblings, the second-youngest of the family: elder sister Tonia is above him and little brother Teucer below. He never appears on screen; he is known from Tartaglia's letters and from Tartaglia calling him and Tonia great kids.

His only detail in canon is a joke at his expense: he apparently believed Liyue's people were made of stone, and possibly that they ate stones, until Tartaglia wrote home to correct him.

Status as of 7.1: Presumed to be with his family in Snezhnaya as of 7.1. No canon scene shows him; his fate and activities after Tartaglia's letters are unstated.

340.content:
Apep (also: Dendro Dragon, Dendro Dragon Sovereign, Devourer of Divinity, Dragon of Verdure): Ruled Sumeru before the Heavenly Principles; a proud, scornful survivor of the dragons' lost war who holds a world of elemental lifeforms inside her.

She owes Nahida and the Traveler, and pays on her own terms.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in the Desert of Hadramaveth. She chose to observe the world rather than destroy it, and in 6.6 repaid Nahida with life force.

Her Heart of Oasis was revived in 3.6. She wants no visitors unless absolutely necessary, still hates the Heavenly Principles and says dragonkind will one day reclaim the world.

341.content:
Apepi (also: Uncle Apepi): Apepi is a cheerful man of the Shimti tribe who writes songs. He is seen only in the 6.1 Archon Quest 'Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion', in a memory of Nefer's childhood, where the girl calls him Uncle Apepi.

He wants to perform a new song at the next festival but needs the chief's approval, so he asks the girl what her father has been doing.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. He appears only in the memory, before the Shimti's end.

Nothing about him has appeared since 6.1, and no later content to 7.1 mentions him.

342.content:
Arama (also: Aranara Arama, New Ashvattha Tree): A small Aranara of Vanarana, shy at first and then fiercely loyal. He guides the Traveler through the Aranyaka quests and becomes the new Ashvattha Tree so a Bija can be made to save the ailing Rana.

Humans are "Nara" to him, and the Traveler is the "Golden Nara". After he eats the Vasoma Fruit his speech changes from simple and halting to clear and measured.

Status as of 7.1: The Aranyaka quests end with Arama as a sapling: the new Ashvattha Tree in the Land of Grounded Dreams.

He cannot move or speak now. Arana and the Traveler can play the Rhythm of the Great Dream to him.

343.content:
Ashru (also: Nefer's cat, the Curatorium cat): Nefer's pet cat, who sits on the counter of the Curatorium of Secrets in Nasha Town and welcomes clients in his own way.

He is an ordinary cat with an unusual history: the Ibis King once borrowed his body to speak with Nefer. He sleeps, begs for fish and brushing, and has no interest in the human schemes around him.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and sitting at the Curatorium of Secrets counter in Nasha Town.

He is usually found on the counter or beside Nefer and Jahoda.

344.content:
Asmoday (also: Sustainer of Heavenly Principles, Unknown God, God of Space, Master of Space, Lord of Emptiness): A Shade of the Heavenly Principles who, in the Cataclysm, stopped the twin travelers leaving Teyvat, took the sibling and sealed the Traveler. She has since left Celestia and is seen with the sibling.

She called herself the Sustainer of the Heavenly Principles, yet she has missed every Shade meeting since the Cataclysm and left her Temple of Space to its Watchers.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and at large; whereabouts unknown.

In 6.5 the Traveler freed her abandoned temple from Melanta. In 7.1 the Tsaritsa reported seeing her in Snezhnaya with a hooded figure; Ronova died still waiting for her return.

345.content:
Atea (also: Candlekeeper, Auntie Atea): Atea, the Candlekeeper of the People of the Springs, was a veteran warrior famed for her love of hot springs and strict rules about them. An Abyssal wound left her unable to fight or bathe, but she kept guarding her tribe until she died in the 5.0 story.

A stern neighbour and teacher to the tribe's children, especially Mualani. Her hot spring parties drew warriors she called her "hot spring buddies".

Status as of 7.1: Dead of Abyssal corrosion days after the 5.0 party; Mavuika saw her one last time. Her spirit later helped the Traveler in the Night Kingdom (5.3).

Her talisman is with Mavuika. The tribe carries on her legacy of parties.

346.content:
Avaz (also: Northland Bank scammer, Avaz of the Northland Bank): Avaz is a Northland Bank employee in Snezhnograd. During the 7.1 Archon Quest he tried to sell Seals of Life to a supposed dying old man, was cornered by Alyosha, Odette and Vodyanitsa, and confessed that he had noticed Seals missing from the bank vault.

He is a small-time opportunist rather than a mastermind: seeing the vault count mismatch and assuming Regrator was behind it, he decided to make some quick Mora of his own.

Status as of 7.1: In custody after the sting, to be handed to Fatui Internal Affairs on the Tsaritsa's word. As of 7.1 he is not seen again.

Odette decides to keep him in their custody so he cannot tip anyone off while they report to the Tsaritsa and plan with her permission.

347.content:
Azar (also: Grand Sage Azar, Sage Azar, Rtawahist Sage): Former Grand Sage of the Sumeru Akademiya. He led the sages' secret plan with a Fatui Harbinger to build a new god, and fell when it failed.

A proud scholar who equates wisdom with the Akademiya's authority, he distrusted the real Archon, Lesser Lord Kusanali, and sealed her in the Sanctuary of Surasthana. After Chapter III he was removed and sent to Avidya Forest to spend his life cultivating wisdom.

Status as of 7.1: Alive. Removed from office and sent to Avidya Forest to cultivate wisdom after the Archon spared him. No present-day appearance since 3.2.

Alhaitham was offered the Grand Sage's post and refused it; he served as Acting Grand Sage while new sages were chosen. The sages who backed Azar were replaced. By 6.6 Rtawahist's sage is Shakir and Naphis has been appointed Grand Sage.

348.content:
Azhdaha (also: Geo Dragon, Earth Dragon, Sealed Lord of Vishaps, Ancient Geovishap Ancestor, Dragon King Azhdaha, Geo Dragon Sovereign): A colossal Geo dragon, once Morax's friend, driven mad by erosion and sealed beneath the Dragon-Queller at Nantianmen.

In "No Mere Stone" (1.5) his power took the girl Jiu's shape to break the seal; Zhongli, the Traveler and a benevolent fragment of Azhdaha resealed the raging body.

Status as of 7.1: Resealed beneath the Dragon-Queller after "No Mere Stone"; the wrathful body is dormant.

Zhongli says that if he wakes, Liyue must face him.

349.content:
Babel (also: Matriarch of the Tanit): Matriarch of the Tanit Eremites: gracious, devout in word, and a schemer in fact. Jeht killed her once her plot for the Eternal Oasis was exposed.

She hosts the Traveler in The Dirge of Bilqis, then tries to have them killed in Her Foes Rage Like Great Waters... to take the Jinni Liloupar's mastery for herself.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: Jeht killed her at the Tanit Camps after the Traveler exposed her lies.

The Tanit fell with her; a few survivors remain among those she sent out or exiled.

350.content:
Baishi (also: Baishi the secretary, Hundred-Knowing, Ningguang's secretary): Baishi is one of Lady Ningguang's three secretaries in the Jade Chamber, a prim and fervently loyal aide who is happiest fussing over Ningguang's image.

She is a minor but memorable Liyue Harbor fixture: formal when caught off guard, flustered when teased, and certain that Ningguang's mind should never be spent on trivial choices.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and employed at the Jade Chamber as of 7.1; no change in canon.

She is among the staff who resumed work after the Jade Chamber's restoration.

351.content:
Baiwen (also: Baiwen the secretary, Hundred-Hearing, Ningguang's secretary): Baiwen is one of Lady Ningguang's three secretaries in the Jade Chamber, responsible for gathering and organising the intelligence that flows into it.

Courteous and exacting, she greets visitors with the air of someone who already has a file on them, and reflects aloud on any error in her estimates.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and employed at the Jade Chamber as of 7.1; no change in canon.

She returned to her normal duties after the Jade Chamber's restoration.

352.content:
Baixiao (also: Baixiao the secretary, Hundred-Understanding, Ningguang's secretary): Baixiao is one of Lady Ningguang's three secretaries in the Jade Chamber, a discreet, polite aide who receives guests and keeps business confidential.

She tells visitors the little she is allowed to, sends them to Ningguang for the rest, and rewards honest respect with a few pieces of her own advice about gold.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and employed at the Jade Chamber as of 7.1; no change in canon.

She resumed her place there after the restoration and says it is good to be back.

353.content:
Baizhu's Master (also: Hu Tao's great-uncle, Old Hu's younger brother, the Chenyu Vale doctor): A Chenyu Vale physician from the Hu family of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. He bore Changsheng's contract, trained Baizhu and Jiangli, and died young. He exists only as a memory.

His last question, whether the contract is medicine or poison, set Baizhu on the path to defy it.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long before the Traveler's time; his tomb is where Baizhu vowed to end the contract.

Cinematic and flashback only: he has no living appearance in the game as of 7.1.

354.content:
Baladhuri (also: Sage Baladhuri, Uncle Baladhuri, Vahumana Sage): Sage of the Vahumana Darshan at the Sumeru Akademiya: a kind, gentle scholar devoted to his students and family, jailed with Naphis for opposing the old regime.

One of two "old guard" sages who held office before Azar's fall. Known for steadiness: he stays with his students through an evacuation and supplies historical knowledge when the Irminsul crisis demands it.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and in office as Vahumana Sage; last seen in 6.6 at Caravan Ribat during the Irminsul crisis.

He joins the plan to search the Temple of Silence for a substitute power source for the Akasha System.

355.content:
Barbeloth (also: Astromancer Barbeloth Trismegistus, Barbeloth Trismegistus, Barbeloth Megistus, Seer-Witch, Goddess of Prophecy, Barbie, Mona's master): Barbeloth, called B, is the elderly Hexenzirkel Seer-Witch, an astrologer and diviner who taught Mona.

She is Alice's old friend and rival, a fortune-teller who admits what she cannot see.

Status as of 7.1: Alive at 7.1, running a fortune booth in Fontaine through a Dodoco stand-in.

She roams and sends stand-ins; no fixed home is stated.

356.content:
Beisht (also: The Avenger of the Vortex, Osial's wife, Final follower of the Overlord of the Vortex): A giant Hydro sea monster, Osial's wife and the last follower of the Overlord of the Vortex. She rose from a storm to avenge him when the Jade Chamber was rebuilt, and fled gravely wounded.

Known as the Avenger of the Vortex. She is a monster, not a speaker: canon shows her only by her attacks, and others tell her story.

Status as of 7.1: Fled severely wounded in 2.4. Her whereabouts are unknown; Liyue remains watchful.

Shenhe judged that she would seek refuge elsewhere and not soon return. Ningguang told her officers to stay ready.

357.content:
Belozersky (also: Councilor Belozersky, Snezhnograd Veche Councilor): Belozersky is a councilor of the Snezhnograd Veche. In the 7.1 Archon Quest he faces a crowd outside Zapolyarny Palace asking why the Tsaritsa is collecting Seals of Life, confirms the Druzhna's donation, withholds the purpose, and is then told to return to his duties by Regrator.

His scene shows the Veche's public face during the Seals affair: reassuring, guarded and subordinate to Regrator (Pantalone).

Status as of 7.1: Alive and presumably still on the Snezhnograd Veche as of 7.1; not seen after the Palace scene.

358.content:
Benben (also: the strange machine, Jeht's construct): Benben is a small, friendly machine from the ruins of King Deshret's civilisation. It only beeps, but Jeht, who found and named it, says she understands what it feels. It can open the sealed doors of the old ruins.

Unlike the hostile Primal Constructs around it, it attacked no one and carries no weapon-like attachments. It first appears in the Sumeru quest series Golden Slumber (3.1) and returns in the 6.6 Archon Quest.

Status as of 7.1: Active and travelling with Jeht as of its last appearance in 6.6.

Jeht leads a mercenary group; Benben is with her. No later content to 7.1 shows it.

359.content:
Bennu (also: Saint Bennu, Most-Radiant, Bennu the Most-Radiant, Pillar Bennu): Saint Bennu, the Most-Radiant, is an intelligent construct made by King Deshret to guard the gates of Aaru: a serious, earnest and proud guardian of the late king's legacy.

Unlike the three Kings of the Seven Pillars, he was built, not born, yet he has a will and a vivid personality. He fell still when Deshret died and was reawakened in 6.6 to vote on opening Aaru.

Status as of 7.1: Awake since 6.6 and helping maintain Aaru with Shesepankh.

Aaru has been reconfigured and now serves the information role Irminsul once held.

360.content:
Biram (also: Chief Biram, Chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind, Mictlan chief): Chief of the Masters of the Night-Wind, Natlan's shaman tribe: courteous, reform-minded, eager to understand his tribe's mysteries without losing its traditions.

Calm and a little oracular, he lets questions stew before they are asked. His chief concern is the woven scrolls that record Natlan's great events and whose strange coloring he has long tried to explain.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, chief at the Sacrificial Altar of Enigmatic Land, after the Abyss was driven back.

No appearance in the Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content was found.

361.content:
Birgitta (also: Beep-Boopitta, Beep-Boopitta the Carrier Robot, Little Robot): A small cleaner-carrier combat robot made by Aino, who tags along with Ineffa, fixing, cleaning and fighting.

Her name was once a long string of noises and job titles that grew with every upgrade, until Ineffa shortened it to Birgitta.

Status as of 7.1: Operating and travelling with Ineffa.

No change through 7.1 is on record. She was last seen in the Natlan quests and Ineffa's kit.

362.content:
Callirhoe (also: Spring Fairy, Fairy of Springvale): The Spring Fairy of Springvale: a gentle Oceanid from Fontaine who loves listening to people's dreams.

She rarely shows herself. She befriended two lonely children, Finch and Diona, then stepped away from both.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in spirit at Springvale after meeting Finch in 4.1.

Her physical form expired after the reunion. The wiki says she and Finch continue to speak.

363.content:
Capitano (also: Il Capitano, The Captain, Thrain, Sentinel Knight): Thrain, a cursed Khaenri'ahn knight. In Natlan he went from Mavuika's rival to her ally, then died in her place (5.3).

He led the Fatui armed forces. He judged Mavuika's war with the Abyss hopeless, lost his duel with her, then fought beside Natlan; his hidden aim was to give the souls he carried rest.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 dead or beyond reach: in 5.3 he merged with the Lord of the Night in Mavuika's place. His body sits dormant on the Throne of the Primal Fire.

Natlan engraved him on a monument to the fallen; his subordinate Rotchev attended. Fatui gossip says the Tsaritsa has kept his position as it was, and his key people and Veche seat went to Tartaglia.

364.content:
Cardinal Calvin (also: Calvin): A cardinal of the Church of Favonius who runs its affairs while Seneschal Seamus Pegg is away. Barbara says he is so busy he seldom leaves his room.

He is known only by report. Everything canon says of him comes from one conversation with Barbara.

Status as of 7.1: Last known as acting Seneschal while Seamus was away. His current fate is unknown.

Seamus returns to Mondstadt in later stories, but nothing says what happened to Calvin's role.

365.content:
Chang the Ninth (also: Chang the Ninth of Feiyun Slope, Big Nine, Old Chang): A pompous, down-on-his-luck ore merchant in Qingce Village who boasts of his Feiyun Slope glory days. Devoted book collector and author of First Apprentice of Guhua.

His pride hides real tenderness: he writes in hope of reaching Little Nine, the neighbour girl who vanished long ago. After the sale he is warm and grateful, though he still looks down on his neighbours.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Qingce Village. His novel won, but the sakoku decree blocked Yae's royalties; he later received Mr. Nine's buried savings. He keeps writing.

As of 6.2 he lives modestly in Qingce Village and has recovered his book collection. After the Traveler dug up Mr. Nine's savings he returned to work.

366.content:
Changsheng (also: Herblord, Yao Jun, the Jade Snake, Baizhu's snake): Baizhu's white snake companion, once the Herblord, an adeptus of Chenyu Vale. Her contract trades a doctor's health for the power to cure.

Few in Liyue Harbor know she is more than a pet. Her name, Changsheng, means "longevity", a bitter irony since each contractor has died young.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, at Bubu Pharmacy in Liyue Harbor with Baizhu.

Baizhu's promise that the contract ends with him still stands as of 7.1; no change is shown.

367.content:
Charles (also: Angel's Share bartender, Angel's Share's bartender): Charles is the bartender of Angel's Share, the Dawn Winery's tavern in Mondstadt. Courteous and practical, he has worked there for over a decade.

He sells drink-based food, turns away underage customers, and is quietly grateful when Diluc covers his shift.

Status as of 7.1: Alive as far as canon shows; tends the bar at Angel's Share.

No later change in his role is shown.

368.content:
Chef Mao (also: Mao, Boss of Wanmin Restaurant, Xiangling's father): Proud, easygoing owner and chef of Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor, a veteran with over two decades in the kitchen. He is Xiangling's father and first teacher.

He sells food, ingredients and recipes to travellers, believes food exists to feed the hungry and is happy to admit his daughter has surpassed him.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and running Wanmin Restaurant in Liyue Harbor; open at all hours.

He brags that Xiangling won the Masterful Chefs in the Moonlight Merriment period (limited-time event, 2.1).

369.content:
Chlothar (also: Chlothar Alberich, Eide): A Khaenri'ahn Alberich noble who tried to save his cursed hilichurl son Caribert, turned to the Abyss, and founded the Abyss Order. Seen only in the sibling's memory.

He met the sibling in Sumeru, calling himself Eide. By the end he had recognised them as the Prince or Princess of Khaenri'ah and named his son the 'Loom of Fate'.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. He vanished a century after founding the Order; remains in his old field may be his.

His legacy persists: the Order, the Loom of Fate project, and the Defiled Statue Dainsleif calls his product.

370.content:
Chugunov (also: Director Chugunov, Iskra Manufacturing Plant Boss, Iskra Plant owner): A wealthy, short-tempered Snezhnayan owner of the Iskra Manufacturing Plant who boasts of a loving family, long since lost.

Fellow theater-goers know him as the rude man who demands the best seat. After the Korolevskiy Theater ordeal he drops the act and agrees to close his plant.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Snezhnaya as of 7.1, having ordered his factory wound down.

371.content:
Chuychu (also: Chuychu of the Flower-Feather Clan): A Flower-Feather doctor who treated Abyssal contamination, adoptive younger sister of Chasca. She died of Abyssal injuries in the invasion of Natlan.

She nagged and worried over Chasca out of love, backed her on the Night Kingdom expedition, and died telling Chasca she was proud of her.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since the Abyssal invasion (5.1); listed among the memorialised. A spirit in a Night Kingdom dream (5.3).

Her death shaped Chasca and grieved the clan; Mutota tried to call her for help after the attack, forgetting she was dead.

372.content:
Clymene (also: Sunchildren's attendant): Clymene was a female official of Byakuyakoku who looked after the Sunchildren's daily lives inside the Dainichi Mikoshi. Forbidden to speak to them and to marry, she still came to love them as her own. As a shade she asks the Traveler to help lay them to rest. She appears in the permanent Enkanomiya world quest The Phaethons' Syrtos. Her tone is sorrowful and formal, her guilt for failing to speak up to the children is the heart of her story.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. After the Traveler delivers the Divine Bridle and the Sunchildren are laid to rest, she says her wish is fulfilled and fades. No later appearance was found. A later hidden objective, Sunchildren Hide and Seek, mentions her indirectly through Orupeusu's promise to never sing until he heard her voice.

373.content:
Comonqui (also: Scorching Star, Abyss Lector: Fathomless Flames): A Pyro Abyss Lector called the Scorching Star who invaded the Night Kingdom, killed Mallko and was defeated by Kachina and Mualani.

He mocked the idea of Ancient Names and friendship, saying only raw power matters, and craves the Abyss's destruction as art.

Status as of 7.1: Defeated in the Night Kingdom; no later appearance.

His fate after defeat is not stated.

374.content:
Crepus (also: Crepus Ragnvindr, Master Crepus, Master of the Dawn Winery): Crepus Ragnvindr, called Master Crepus: late owner of the Dawn Winery, Diluc's father and Kaeya's adoptive father. He died shielding Diluc about four years before the story.

Knights and winery staff speak of him with respect. His death took Diluc out of the Knights of Favonius and into years of wandering.

Status as of 7.1: Dead since Diluc's eighteenth birthday; his manor still holds the art he collected.

As of Version 7.1 no living scene shows him.

375.content:
Cusco (also: Chasca's father, Chasca's adoptive father, Uncle Cusco): Cusco is a Flower-Feather Clan man who became Chasca's adoptive father. He is a loving, anxious parent grieving a daughter and worrying about another.

He is warm and talkative and tends to ramble about his daughters, especially when he thinks Chasca is hiding injuries.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in the Flower-Feather Clan, still worried about Chasca. No later appearance found.

His wife is away on business with the Masters of the Night-Wind and writes him letters about his fussing.

376.content:
Dainsleif (also: Dain, Bough Keeper, Twilight Sword, Captain Dain): Immortal former Royal Guard captain, the Twilight Sword, five centuries into his fight against the Abyss Order. Curt and guarded, he sells help for a price and honest answers.

A quest NPC announced as a future playable character; he is not playable as of 7.1. He narrates the Collected Miscellany videos.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, in Snezhnaya after helping defeat Ronova, eager to leave.

Pierro asked him to come to Snezhnaya; he said Snezhnaya had every right to consider its victory absolute, but that the era to come would not be peaceful.

377.content:
Danica (also: Danica Postelnitskaya, Head Maid of Zapolyarny Palace): Danica Postelnitskaya is the head maid of Zapolyarny Palace and one of the Tsaritsa's two closest attendants. Exacting, formal, deadpan; a former wandering mercenary.

Vesna handles military decrees; Danica handles state affairs and the household.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and serving as head maid at Zapolyarny Palace as of Version 7.1.

Stays at the Tsaritsa's side through 7.1.

378.content:
Demyan (also: The Flagship Bartender, "The Flagship" Bartender): The friendly young bartender and innkeeper of The Flagship tavern in Nasha Town, selling food, drinks and recipes.

A genial host who runs a clean business, keeps up with local rumours, and treats regulars like Flins as friends.

Status as of 7.1: Behind the bar at The Flagship in Nasha Town, serving customers.

After the Fatui bureau's setback, he treats it as welcome but private news.

379.content:
Descartes (also: Prune's imaginary friend, the purple puppy): A small purple dog, Prune's imaginary friend, born of her need for someone to talk to about her books.

He faded as Prune tried to grow up too fast. Alice staged his 'kidnapping' to push her into reclaiming her childhood, and he returned when Prune joined the Little Hexenzirkel.

Status as of 7.1: Restored and with Prune after the Phantasmal Pals event.

Prune is now a member of the Little Hexenzirkel, which keeps him safe.

380.content:
Dex (also: Dexter, juvenile Watcher): Dex (Dexter) is a juvenile Watcher of the Temple of Space, shaped like a hand with an eye, who helps the Traveler free the temple from Melanta.

It cannot talk, but it can bend the temple's space, take apart the Keepers and Maranasati Caskets guarding it, and carry living people between the surface and the temple. The temple's people raised it.

Status as of 7.1: In the Temple of Space after Melanta's defeat.

Istoria asked Dex to remember the temple's kindness as it grows up. Nothing after 6.5 is shown.

381.content:
Donskoy (also: Donskoy the snow giant, the giant of ice and snow, the chained giant, Eitr-Altered Snegovik): A Snegovik who became a giant of ice and snow through Pavlina's forbidden Eitr, was chained, and was freed to keep a promise at a lighthouse.

Status as of 7.1: After lighting the lighthouse he walks into the sea and is not seen again. His fate is unknown at the cutoff.

Paimon feels the Traveler will never see him again. The Eye of Graeae reports him seen by the shore after the chains are broken.

key: Exalted Master of the Heretical Path
382.content:
Dottore (also: Il Dottore, The Doctor, Zandik, Escher, Omega Build, Segment 35, Heretic of the False Moon, False Moon God): Il Dottore, 'The Doctor', is the Second of the Eleven Fatui Harbingers: a brilliant, amoral researcher whose given name is Zandik. Expelled from the Sumeru Akademiya for unauthorised, unethical work, he joined the Fatui to get the resources to turn humans into something godlike, and treats people, allies and enemies alike as parts of an experiment. In the story he is a recurring adversary through Sumeru and Nod-Krai. He is dead as of Version 6.6: Columbina killed his body with a moonbeam, and he burned away when Nahida set Irminsul alight.

Almost everyone in the Fatui either fears or loathes him. He speaks smoothly and cheerfully, is rarely angry, and does not interfere with an experiment's outcome even when the outcome is his own death. The figure players know is the 'Omega Build', the 35-year-old Segment, one of several independent copies of Zandik that he built to carry on his work.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. Columbina incinerated his body with a moonbeam in Nod-Krai (6.3), which was half of his plan; Pantalone then uploaded his data into Irminsul. There he merged, took over the system, and was burned with it when Nahida used the Pyro Gnosis in Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana (6.6). He said goodbye to Pantalone and Nahida first.

In 7.1 (Etched in Time) Sandrone calls him 'that monster' and uses him as the yardstick for a researcher turned madman, and Pierro does not dispute it. When Anastasya summoned Pantalone and Pulcinella over the affair, Pantalone pinned the blame on Dottore, who was not there to defend himself.

383.content:
Dr. Edith (also: Edith, Edith Musk, Doctor Edith): A Mondstadt historian and folklore researcher who can be found by the Statue of The Seven at Windrise gathering material for her new book. She loves telling the legend of Vennessa.

She is the younger sister of the hilichurl scholar Ella Musk and a colleague of Dr. Livingstone. Her stories are Mondstadt folklore as people tell it, not Archon Quest truth.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Mondstadt, found beside the Windrise Statue of The Seven by day. Nothing in canon through 7.1 changes her situation.

384.content:
Draff (also: Draff Kätzlein, Oddears the Incredible Hunter, Uncle Brown Cat, Head of the Hunters): The head hunter of Springvale and Diona's father. By day he sells fresh game; at night he drinks to the hunt.

He is one of the Four Drunkards of Mondstadt and the man whose hunters supply most of the meat served at the Good Hunter restaurant.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and working in Springvale, unchanged by anything in canon through 7.1.

After meteorites struck, he told a customer that supply to the Good Hunter was strained and that he feared losing hunters (limited event, 1.1).

key: Lesser Lord Kusanali's most faithful follower
385.content:
Dunyarzad (also: Dunyarzad Homayani, Miss Homayani, Miss Dunyarzad, Lesser Lord Kusanali's most faithful follower): A gentle, stubbornly hopeful young woman of Sumeru City's wealthy Homayani family. Born with the incurable illness Eleazar, she slipped out to revive the neglected Sabzeruz Festival for Lesser Lord Kusanali.

She befriends the Traveler and Paimon on their first day in the city, and her illness becomes the human cost of the Akademiya's dream-harvesting plot. She is cured when Eleazar vanishes from Sumeru.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and cured: Eleazar vanished from Sumeru after Rukkhadevata's tainted consciousness was cleansed from the Irminsul.
