In 6.6 he joined the Caravan Ribat council, questioned Collei, and voiced the risks at the Temple of Silence.

513.content:
Shesepankh (also: Saint Shesepankh, Most-Holy, Shesepankh the Most-Holy): Saint Shesepankh, the Most-Holy, is an intelligent construct built by King Deshret to oversee the world's Jinn. Leisurely and endlessly curious, he was awakened in 6.6 to vote on opening Aaru.

He has a will of his own, fell into stillness when the king died, and is the Pillar who prizes a relaxed outlook, to Bennu's annoyance.

Status as of 7.1: Awake since 6.6, apparently maintaining Aaru and visiting the Temple of Silence.

Heryshaf says he and Bennu are helping the scholars with Aaru. Sethos expects the two might drop by the Temple of Silence.

514.content:
Shishkin (also: Liaison Shishkin, Liaison Officer Shishkin): Shishkin is the friendly liaison of Sretomorozsk, a go-between for townspeople and the Fatui who deliver Kresnik Kristall. In truth he and the mayor have been stealing and reselling it.

Alyosha exposes him in Version 7.0; he is arrested and sent to Snezhnograd.

Status as of 7.1: Arrested in 7.0 and sent to Snezhnograd to await judgement. His verdict is not shown.

515.content:
Shram (also: Mercenary Shram): An easygoing mercenary snowed in at the Korolevskiy Theater with the Traveler, he is the ghost of a bodyguard killed there over four hundred years ago.

Nobody in the group knew him before the storm. His quiet farewell, walking into the blizzard to take the "death" with him, is one of the gentler moments of Wraith's Nocturne.

Status as of 7.1: Dead long before 7.0. His soul walked into the snowstorm and returned to the Ley Lines in Winter's Mysterious Silence.

After he left, the nightly death toll in the theater dropped from two to one.

516.content:
Shuyu (also: Xianyun's disciple, Yuandai's granddaughter): A young girl from a family of exorcists on Mt. Tianheng, granddaughter of Yuandai and the first human-world disciple of the adeptus Xianyun (Cloud Retainer).

Warm, shy and determined, she first appears in the 4.4 Grus Serena Chapter, caring for her forgetful grandmother. She has since lived with Xianyun at Chihu Rock in Liyue Harbor.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Liyue Harbor, living and training with Xianyun at Chihu Rock.

During the 4.4 Lantern Rite event (limited) she joined a kite-making workshop. In the 7.1 Silverwing in Pursuit of the Moon event (limited) she was at the Moonchase Festival with pocket money from her master, planning to taste Fontaine sweets and Sumeru barbecue and save for mechanism parts.

517.content:
Signora (also: La Signora, The Fair Lady, Rosalyne, Crimson Witch of Flame, Crimson Witch of Embers): The Eighth Harbinger, a proud Snezhnayan diplomat sent to take Archons' Gnoses for the Tsaritsa. Personal name: Rosalyne.

The first Harbinger the Traveler meets: Anemo Gnosis in Mondstadt, Geo Gnosis in Liyue, schemes in Inazuma. She dies in 2.1; this card plays her alive.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: executed by the Raiden Shogun in Inazuma (2.1); entombed in Snezhnaya.

Her Harbinger seat remains vacant; Odette is the likely successor. This card plays her alive, so use this status only for post-death context.

518.content:
Sigurd (also: The One Who Swore to Hunt the Hunt, Starshyna Sigurd, Sigurd the Starshyna, Uncle Sigurd): A legendary Starshyna who vanished fighting the Wild Hunt about a decade ago and still fights it as a corrupted revenant.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, yet wandering as a corrupted spirit. Once the Traveler returns his relics and defeats him, he says it is finally over.

His relics (the Long Night's Oath set) surface at Tideseal Stones when travellers drive back the Wild Hunt. The fight can be repeated as a Local Legend.

519.content:
Silver (also: Navia's attendant, Spina di Rosula attendant): Younger of the two attendants guarding Navia of the Spina di Rosula in Fontaine; a nervous but loyal bodyguard who calls her "Demoiselle". He died in 4.2, dissolved by Primordial Seawater in Poisson.

He and Melus work as a pair: Melus is the older, steady and joking one, Silver the younger, more earnest and self-doubting. After his death his remnant took the form of an Oceanid and, together with Melus, helped hold off the crowd of other victims that wanted to keep Navia in a dream until Neuvillette could pull her out.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: dissolved by Primordial Seawater in Poisson during the Deluge of Wrathful Waters (4.2) while helping others. Afterwards he appears only in Navia's memory, her dream, and as an Oceanid.

He is on the victim list; Navia says she can mourn her father at a grave but not them. Not returned as of 7.1.

520.content:
Silverwing (also: Jade-Plumed Silverwing, Xuanniao Adeptus, Silverwing the swallow adeptus): A swallow-born adeptus who kept a yearly Moonchase promise to the Wind Reader.

She appears only as a memory in the 7.1 Moonchase event. Her swallow flock was her body and power; as swallows died on the long flights she lost her mind and memories.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown; Zhongli says she has not entirely departed while swallows fly in Liyue.

No adeptus can find her.

521.content:
Sinuhe (also: Chief Sinuhe, Nefer's father): Chief of the desert Shimti tribe and Nefer's father, who tried to save his people from thirst and was destroyed with them.

He appears only in Nefer's memories in the Nod-Krai Archon Quest Dance of Death: Serpent and Scorpion (6.1) and in the letters he wrote to the Akademiya.

Status as of 7.1: Dead, killed with most of his tribe by the Iab in the past; known only through Nefer's memories and letters.

Nothing is shown of him after the quest or in later versions through 7.1.

522.content:
Siraj (also: Overmind, Siraj Number 1): A brilliant, bitter Vahumana researcher whose forbidden thesis on a collective consciousness was rejected; he secretly made it real and tried to use it to seize a sage's seat.

In Alhaitham's story quest (3.4) he recruits isolated scholars into a "Hive" under his control, plants hatred of Alhaitham in them, and fails when Ilyas's doubts spread through the network. He concedes defeat and is taken away by the matra.

Status as of 7.1: Arrested by the matra at the end of Version 3.4 to stand trial; his associates were rounded up. The wiki says he is imprisoned.

Alhaitham says the matra will consider that Siraj fooled many of his recruits when passing judgement.

523.content:
Skeiron (also: Captain Skeiron, Captain of the 3rd Company): Skeiron is the Captain of the Knights of Favonius's 3rd Company, one of the senior officers gathered by Jean for Albedo's trial during the Windblume Festival in 5.6.

Canon shows little more than a loyal, professional officer who trusts Albedo and takes his duty at headquarters and in the city's defence seriously.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and serving as Captain of the 3rd Company. As of 7.1 he has no appearance after Paralogism.

524.content:
Skofnungr (also: Blood Serpent's Broken Edge, Surtalogi's friend, the Chasm culprit): A Khaenri'ahn noble, once dying, saved by his friend Surtalogi and later made immortal. He stole power across Teyvat until Skirk broke him.

He appears in one story, Skirk's 5.7 Story Quest. There he is the unseen thief who stabs the Traveler through a fog, takes a fragment of their soul and draws power from others. Once beaten he turns out to be a rueful, open man who misses his friend.

Status as of 7.1: Alive but incapacitated: Skirk shattered his consciousness so the curse of immortality can rebuild his mind.

525.content:
Smiley Yanxiao (also: Yanxiao, Wangshu Inn's chef): The gruff cook of Wangshu Inn, a reformed thief proud of his kitchen and afraid of ghosts.

His Almond Tofu is the dish that coaxes Xiao to the inn. He is one of Liyue's better-known cooks and has given Wangshu Inn a strong name for its food.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and cooking at Wangshu Inn as of 7.1.

He has been a fixture of the inn since 1.0 and in the 7.1 Moonchase event helps on the food street.

526.content:
Smirnova (also: Elena Smirnova, Private Smirnova, E. Smirnova): Elena Smirnova is a private in the Fatui's 6th Company and its only survivor. She now lives on leave in Morepesok, still hoping that her captain and comrades will come home.

Her company was destroyed at Nothing Passage in Nod-Krai by the fallout of two rival researchers' kuuvahki experiments. She does not know it.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and on leave in Morepesok as of Version 7.1, waiting for news and recovering.

She is unaware that her company is dead. She says she wants to get well so that she can welcome them back.

527.content:
Sobek (also: Crocodile King, Captain of Captains, Sobek the Crocodile King, Croco): A god beaten by King Deshret and made his foremost general among the Seven Pillars. Locked in Aaru for ages, he is free again and gentler.

He embodied Deshret's strength and ruled war, yet blessed the land with abundance. Today he is a dry, courteous elder who teases his fellow Pillars.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and free since 6.6.

Thoth and Heryshaf stay at the Temple of Silence; Thoth asks where Sobek is, wanting cards.

528.content:
Soboleva (also: Wealthy Merchant Soboleva, Rich Businessman Soboleva): A wealthy Snezhnayan businesswoman who attends the "Spirit Seeker" preview and is trapped by the blizzard. She and Torgov are the first guests found dead.

The quests later show that the deaths were the Curse of Death at work in a Ley Line dream, not a killer's doing.

Status as of 7.1: Found dead on the first morning of the blizzard. In the closing scene of the act everyone wakes unharmed in their seats.

Her death opens the sequence of deaths later traced to Ronova's Curse of Death.

529.content:
Sorush (also: Lady Sorush, Bloomguard of the Pari, Red Floaty): A young, self-important Pari of the Vourukasha Oasis who made the Traveler her Yasnapati and became the Bloomguard. She helped dispel the Sign of Apaosha.

Her pride is real, but so are her courage, loyalty and willingness to learn when corrected.

Status as of 7.1: Alive; Bloomguard of the Pari. Last seen helping the Dendro Archon in 6.6.

530.content:
Sousi: A Lightkeeper Sergeant Major of Nasha Town with a mechanical right arm, found dead in the group's office. The 'Sousi' who helped repair the cannon was Rerir in disguise; the real man was already dead.

His death frames Flins, who is the last person seen with the body, until the mismatched arm exposes the lie.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He was found in the Lightkeepers' Nasha Town office; the investigation proved he was killed before the Rerir impostor appeared.

Flins vows revenge on Rerir. The Lightkeepers' investigation of his death continues in the same Archon Quest.

531.content:
Stanley (also: Hans Archibald, Hans, the Mare Jivari adventurer): Stanley is a loud, aging Guild adventurer in Mondstadt who tells endless stories about the Mare Jivari. In truth he is Hans Archibald, who took his late partner's name to keep it alive.

Most Mondstadters think he is a legend; the real Stanley was his friend, and Hans carries guilt for living when Stanley did not. After Venti freed Stanley's spirit he became calmer, though he still tells the tale.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Mondstadt, found outside Angel's Share by day and under a tree near the front gate at night.

He now speaks openly of the real Stanley while still using the name. He feels lighter. No later appearance in 6.x or 7.1 was found.

532.content:
Stepanyan (also: Onyx Agate, Bombardier Poruchik Stepanyan): Stepanyan, codenamed Onyx Agate, is a disciplined Fatui officer of the 1st Grenadier Guards. He survived the Wild Hunt's attack on the Design Bureau in Nod-Krai and now commands a company in Glupov.

Courteous and even-tempered, he is the star student of Major Valeriy. He sees himself as an unremarkable soldier striving to be a dependable war machine.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and commanding a company in Glupov as of Version 7.1.

Recently handed company affairs, he is still adjusting to administrative work.

533.content:
Supada no Hiko (also: Spartacus, Spartacus the Righteous, The Bandit, Supada no Hiko, Supada the Bandit): Afterimage of a Byakuyakoku resistance leader trapped in the Altar at the Serpent's Heart in Enkanomiya. He has forgotten his name and begs for a message of hope to reach his students.

He is called Spartacus the Righteous by his people and Supada no Hiko the Bandit by the nobles who jailed him. Thousands of years after his death the Traveler restores his name by reading his tablet.

Status as of 7.1: Long dead; his afterimage remains in the altar as of 7.1. No later scene exists.

534.content:
Surtalogi (also: The Foul, Skirk's Master, Master of Skirk): A Khaenri'ahn knight turned Sinner, titled "The Foul". He left Teyvat after the cataclysm and roams the sea of stars seeking an opponent to match him. His disciple is Skirk.

He is almost never seen; Teyvat knows him through Skirk, Dainsleif, Skofnungr and a memory of the Sinners' gathering in Khaenri'ah, viewed in Nod-Krai (6.1).

Status as of 7.1: Alive in the sea of stars; absent from Teyvat since the cataclysm.

As of 7.1 he is still absent and still promises to return and ruin Skirk.

535.content:
Sytin (also: Podvorye guard, Childe's guard at Podvorye Restaurant): A polite guard at Podvorye Restaurant in Snezhnograd who, on Childe's orders, checks visitors' identity before they enter Paimon's sickroom.

He works discreetly: the restaurant keeps running as normal, and he and several colleagues watch it in plain clothes so that nothing draws attention to the room. He is introduced in Version 7.0 and appears only briefly.

Status as of 7.1: Last seen at his post early in Wraith's Nocturne (7.0); later fate unshown as of 7.1.

536.content:
Tarno (also: Voynich Guild Employee, Tarno of the Voynich Guild): Tarno manages the Voynich Guild's souvenir outlet in Nasha Town. Friendly and obliging, he deals in local goods and leads. After the True Moon crisis he became the Guild's representative in the League.

He is a minor shop NPC, so his canon is mostly manner and dialogue rather than history.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Nasha Town as of Version 7.1, and the Voynich Guild's representative in the League since the True Moon crisis.

He continues to run the souvenir outlet.

537.content:
Tea Master Liu Su (also: Liu Su, Master Liu, Dr. Liu): The storyteller on the stage of Heyu Tea House in Liyue Harbor, who dresses legend in ornate speech and stops at the most suspenseful moment.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and performing at Heyu Tea House; nothing later found through 7.1.

538.content:
Teppei (also: Captain Teppei, Herring I Captain, Sangonomiya Samurai): A Watatsumi Army soldier in Inazuma's Resistance who befriended the Traveler, rose to captain, and died after using a Fatui Delusion.

He wanted to prove himself in battle beyond logistics. His death in Chapter II (2.0) exposed that the Resistance's sponsor was the Fatui and fuelled the Traveler's resolve.

Status as of 7.1: Dead. He died of the Delusion's vitality drain during Chapter II, Act III.

539.content:
Teucer (also: Little Teucer, Tartaglia's youngest brother): Teucer is a small, cheerful boy from Morepesok in Snezhnaya, Childe's young brother. He believes Ajax is a toy salesman, and once crossed the sea to Liyue to find him.

Childe asked the Traveler to babysit him in Liyue so that Teucer would never learn the brother he adores is a Fatui Harbinger.

Status as of 7.1: As of 7.1 he is a young boy in Snezhnaya (open-world NPC in Morepesok). His brother still hides his Fatui work.

Teucer still waits for Ajax to visit and play. The Mr. Cyclops figure Childe gave him in Liyue is his favourite toy.

540.content:
Theodore: Trainee medic of the 8th Company who secretly used Ursa the Drake's flesh to prolong the life of his mentor Adorno, with Lohen's help.

He and Lohen were abducted as children and rescued by Adorno. His quiet wish to inherit Adorno's title drove him to repeat the very experiments that once nearly destroyed him.

Status as of 7.1: Punished by Jean after the incident. Adorno is dead, and Theodore's present circumstances are not shown.

Lohen plans to recruit him into the 5th Company as a regular knight once he has atoned. No later appearance up to 7.1.

541.content:
Theofan (also: Yusupov's second-in-command): Theofan was a Fatui delegate in Liyue, Yusupov's second-in-command, who gave Zhiyi poison and slipped away with the evidence.

He is only talked about, never seen. Yelan wanted to turn him into a pawn but the Harbinger Regrator had already got involved and he was gone.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. He vanished with the Fatui's records before Yelan could reach him.

No later appearance or mention is known to 7.1.

542.content:
Thorkell: Thorkell is an Eclipse Dynasty intelligence officer of Khaenri'ah, known only from one remembered scene. Rerir's colleague, loyal to the Vinster King.

He and Rerir are orphans raised into the king's service. Thorkell speaks like an official briefing: formal, assured, loyal. Nothing is known about him outside this scene.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. He exists only in a memory; canon gives no fate, and as of 7.1 he is not met in the present.

543.content:
Thoth (also: Ibis King, Lord of Lies, Scribe of Scribes, God of Deceit, Thoth the Ibis King): The Ibis King, a trickster god of King Deshret's court, freed in 6.6 after millennia sealed in Aaru.

Witty, long-winded and fond of chess, he is the Lord of Lies and cannot be taken at face value. Captivity softened him into a jovial old god.

Status as of 7.1: Free after 6.6; a guest at the Temple of Silence with Heryshaf, planning to stay a while.

Not seen in Chapter VII (7.0-7.1). His statue will not move into Hermanubis's temple.

544.content:
Timaeus (also: Scholar of Alchemy, Timaeus the alchemist): Timaeus is an eager, modest alchemy scholar who works at the Crafting Bench in Mondstadt's fountain plaza and serves as a junior assistant to Albedo.

Mondstadters know him as the friendly man who will happily explain alchemy to anyone, and who admits he is a total amateur beside Albedo and Sucrose. He still dedicates himself to spreading alchemical knowledge in the city, and is drawn into Mondstadt's festivals and quiet romances.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and working in Mondstadt, still near the plaza Crafting Bench.

No appearance in Nod-Krai or Snezhnaya content as of 7.1; last seen in the limited 5.3 Lantern Rite event.

545.content:
Tonia (also: Tartaglia's younger sister, Ajax's sister): Tonia is Childe's younger sister and the elder sister of Teucer and Anthon. She lives in Morepesok, is very close to her big brother Ajax, and worries about him constantly.

Ajax writes to her whenever he sends something home, calling her 'Dearest Sister'. She is the real Tonia; a different girl (Ptashka) used the name in 7.0.

Status as of 7.1: In Morepesok, as of 7.1, as an open-world NPC unlocked after Wraith's Nocturne.

She still hopes Ajax will come home more often and promises to wait.

546.content:
Torgov (also: Rich Businessman, the wealthy energy magnate of the Korolevskiy Theater): A wealthy energy-industry businessman among the audience stranded at the Korolevskiy Theater. He and Soboleva are the first found dead.

He is a talkative, comfort-loving guest who delights in being snowed in with two famous performers, and he is slow to believe the storm is dangerous.

Status as of 7.1: Dead as of Lelek's Confession (7.0), the first to be found; his soul returned to the Ley Lines. His fate after the theater event is not shown.

Mitya explains the deaths as souls returning to the Ley Lines for good. He is not named in the final scenes, so assume he stays dead.

547.content:
Traveler's Sibling (also: Aether, Lumine, Savior of Khaenri'ah): Aether or Lumine, whichever twin the player did not choose. Leads the Abyss Order to revive Khaenri'ah and fight the Heavenly Principles, yet promises to reunite with the Traveler "at this journey's end".

Gentle and sorrowful, not cruel. Khaenri'ah became their second home, and leaving it in its last hour is a guilt they carry. They urge the Traveler to keep travelling and see the world's truth themselves.

Status as of 7.1: Alive. Last glimpsed in Snezhnaya (7.1), hooded, beside Asmoday.

They hold the Atlas of the New World (5.7) and still seek a host for it.

548.content:
Trofin Snezhevich (also: Alphonso, the bad guy in Vimara Village): A House of the Hearth orphan and Fatui agent who lives in Vimara Village as the kindly "Alphonso" on Dottore's orders.

His task is to capture an Aranara. He grew attached to the village, yet helped the Fatui use its children as bait. The Traveler unmasks him when he uses their name.

Status as of 7.1: Fate depends on the Traveler: he leaves forever, or is killed.

If spared, he vows never to return to the village or the Fatui, but a Tattered Paper found in Old Vanarana beside two Riftwolves suggests he may have died. If fought, his last words are for Iotham.

549.content:
The Tsaritsa (also: Tsaritsa, Anastasya, Vassaga, Cryo Archon, God of Love, Mother of Khaenri'ah): She has spent five centuries gathering the Gnoses to overthrow the Heavenly Principles.

She is the God of Love but refuses to use that authority. She rules personally from Zapolyarny Palace in Snezhnograd and appoints every Harbinger.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and ruling at 7.1; holds six Gnoses, lacking only the Pyro Gnosis.

She slowed time around Rhinedottir's tea so Celestia revoked Ronova's authority, and Project Mistilteinn resumed.

550.content:
Tugarin (also: Alyosha's hound, Alyosha's dog): Tugarin is Alyosha's black-and-white husky, once a starving wild dog of the tundra. He tracks, scouts and attacks on command.

Alyosha adopted him after the dog helped finish a man-eating bear. He is stubborn, does not like being petted, and responds to Alyosha's whistles and signals.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and by Alyosha's side in Sretomorozsk and Snezhnograd as of 7.1.

Alyosha also breeds dogs and offers puppies for adoption, though Tugarin remains his partner.

551.content:
Ulrike (also: Thoma's mother): A Mondstadt-born Knight of Favonius and Thoma's mother, known only through what her son and Kaeya say of her. Free-spirited, thoughtful, generous and fond of drink, she has been ordered to join Grand Master Varka's expedition in Nod-Krai.

She never appears on screen. Her presence in canon is a set of letters, gifts and affectionate remarks from the people who know her.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and, as of Version 7.1, on her way to or serving with Varka's expedition in Nod-Krai.

Thoma passed along the news in the 5.7 anecdotes: she received her orders and was already en route. The Knights in the city had given her a send-off at Angel's Share before she left.

552.content:
Ultimate Calamity (also: The Ultimate Calamity, R.M. Morozov, Supervisor Morozov, Morozov): What became of R.M. Morozov, Supervisor of the Post-Apocalyptic Elysium bunker in Wavechaser Plain, who kept its people underground with the lie that the world had ended.

He is a world-quest boss, an Abyssal monster that looks like an enlarged Evil Eye of Blightseep with a special core.

Status as of 7.1: Defeated in the bunker; per the wiki, later joins the Serpent of All Evils in Piramida.

553.content:
Uncle Tian (also: Tianshu, Tian Shu, Tianshu of the Liyue Qixing): A weathered fisherman on the Liyue Harbor docks who is secretly the Tianshu, the Qixing member who plans policy behind the scenes.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, still the Tianshu as of 7.1, recovering from the 2.7 poisoning and passing duties on gradually; he spends more time fishing.

554.content:
Valeriy (also: Major Valeriy, Fort Fulguration, Commander of the Special Assignments Battalion, Mr. Door): Major Valeriy commands the Armory Palace's Special Assignments Battalion. A punctual, level-headed officer, he spends much time returning the energy scientist Mitya to work.

People describe a quiet, strong, clock-driven man who dislikes disrupted plans.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and serving as head of the Special Assignments Battalion as of 7.1; the theatre ordeal is behind him.

After the theatre events he returned to duty. When he questioned the Traveler about Mitya, the Traveler asked him to help gather everyone, and the retelling let the group dimly recall the afterlife. By 7.1 he has, with Vesna, given military support to Mitya's plan to turn the theatre into a laboratory.

555.content:
Vasiliy (also: Vasiliy Nikolayevich Izmaylov, Vasiliy Izmaylov, the Young Sire, Vasya, Oedipus): Vasiliy, the "Young Sire", led the Izmaylov fae gang after his adoptive father's death. He was the killer, and he tried to open the Shadow Realm to win power.

Zmei's Luchkin gang enlist the Traveler to stop him. He dies in Version 7.0.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: beaten in the Train Boneyard as the tunnel collapses.

His last words are frightened: he cannot see and asks Zmei to take him away. The High Table decides what becomes of the Izmaylov.

556.content:
Vedrfolnir (also: The Visionary, Visionary Vedrfolnir): Blinded court prophet of fallen Khaenri'ah, elder brother of Dainsleif and one of the Five Sinners. Today he is known only as a voice that reaches those who cross memories of the past.

Surtalogi says his prophecies are never wrong. He claims no divinity.

Status as of 7.1: Unknown. He was last heard directly as a voice in 6.4.

He does not appear in 7.0 or 7.1; in 7.1 Pierro only names him as the source of a prophecy given to Hroptatyr.

557.content:
Velimiru: An artificial Fatuus made by Harbinger Sandrone, he took part in a three-man Fatui mission to Natlan that was destroyed by the machine it tried to control.

He appears only in the 5.8 Archon Quest act The Journey Home (Smoldering and Searing). He is dead by its end.

Status as of 7.1: Dead: he reawakened the Eleventh Lord with his last strength and the Traveler struck him down.

Nothing in canon as of 7.1 shows him returning.

558.content:
Verna (also: Vernadska, Priestess Verna): Verna (Vernadska) is a cheerful, overconfident priestess of the Frostmoon Scions in Nod-Krai who calls her half-formed plans "science".

Status as of 7.1: At the Frostmoon Enclave library copying hymns as penance, excused from Nasha Town work for now.

559.content:
Vichama (also: Legendary Scout): A legendary scout of the Scions of the Canopy, worn down by guilt over his friend Mallko's death. He helped recover Kachina's Ancient Name, then died defending his tribe.

Status as of 7.1: Dead; his spirit is in the Night Kingdom with Mallko.

His name is in the Record Penned by All; nothing later than 5.3 changes this.

560.content:
Viktor (also: Mister Fatooey, Mr. Fatooey, Fatui Diplomat): A low-ranking Fatuus, a diplomat's assistant, left idle in Mondstadt's Favonius Cathedral, who barters Fatui "stories" for errands, befriends a small girl, and is later moved to Sumeru City.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and last seen in Sumeru City, stationed under Mr. Vsevolod, doing logistics and carving wood.

561.content:
Vilemina: A Frostmoon Scion and childhood friend of the Moonchanter Lauma. Tired of her people's inherited faith, she secretly joined the Fatui and stole the Moon Marrow to prove herself.

To the Traveler she first seemed a protective, sharp-tongued member of Lauma's circle; in truth she had already decided to leave.

Status as of 7.1: Last seen in the Experimental Design Bureau, in a Fatui uniform, antlers cut off.

Canon does not say what she does next. As of 7.1 she has not reappeared.

562.content:
Violetta (also: Violetta Spessiva, Madame Violetta, Mrs. Spessiva): Odette's mother, a famed Korolevskiy Theater ballerina of the Spessiva family. After her Fatui husband died on duty, a fall ended her dancing and she taught her daughter instead.

She turned down Signora's offer to take Odette into the Fatui, but Odette overheard and insisted on accepting.

Status as of 7.1: Her fate after Odette joined the Fatui is not stated in canon.

Nothing in 7.0-7.1 shows her directly.

563.content:
Wagner (also: Mondstadt's blacksmith, the blacksmith of Mondstadt): Mondstadt's master blacksmith, found at the forge near the city's front gate. Blunt, proud and hardworking, he sells and forges weapons and tolerates no shortcuts.

The shop is called Schulz's Blacksmith after his apprentice because Wagner lost a drinking bet. He considers craft a matter of sweat and perseverance, not talent or inheritance.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and at his forge in Mondstadt City.

He kept working through the Stormterror attack and has no further story role through Version 7.1.

564.content:
Wang Ping'an (also: Starsnatcher, Master of Stars, Heavenly Lord Starsnatcher): A folklorist's grandson who posed as the adeptus Starsnatcher, was shamed by Xiao and now tends Pervases' Temple.

His old fraud made him a small following near Wangshu Inn. After Xiao's Dream Trawler ritual he gave up the act, returned his takings and began writing about the Yakshas.

Status as of 7.1: Alive; keeps Pervases' Temple in the mountains near Liyue Harbor.

He is still working on his book about the Yakshas, slowly.

565.content:
Waqar: A frightened but grateful civilian of Natlan who is among the people holed up in a stronghold near the Scions of the Canopy when Abyssal monsters surge in The Surging Darkness.

He appears in the "Under Siege" hotspot, where the Traveler helps defenders Achiyaku and Wayta drive the monsters off. Whether he survives the next Archon Quest depends on whether the player reinforced that hotspot.

Status as of 7.1: Fate depends on a player choice. If the "Under Siege" hotspot was reinforced, he is among the survivors escorted toward the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Otherwise he may die in Despair Engulfs the Heavens.

Nothing is known of him after that quest.

566.content:
Wayna (also: Chief Wayna, Uncle Wayna, Chief of the Scions of the Canopy): Chief of the Scions of the Canopy in Natlan, an easygoing risk-taker who warns others that adventure is a double-edged sword.

He has the most adventuring experience in his tribe and dislikes being called Uncle. He supported the effort to rescue Kachina and oversaw tribe responses to Kongamato and the Abyss invasion.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, chief of the Scions of the Canopy, back in his village after Mavuika stopped the Abyss invasion.

The annual Kongamato purification is no longer needed, so the ritual he oversaw has ended. He sends people to feed the Yumkasaur at Teticpac Peak daily.

567.content:
Ying'er (also: Ying'er of Scent of Spring, Shop Assistant of Scent of Spring): A knowing, flirtatious shopkeeper at Scent of Spring in Liyue Harbor, who sells vases and makes perfumes.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and running Scent of Spring in Liyue Harbor; nothing later found through 7.1.

key: Guardian of the Land of Night
568.content:
Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night (also: Yohualtecuhtin, Lord of the Night, Lord of the Crossroads, Father in Black, Keykeeper of Countless Secrets): An ancient Angel who rules the Night Kingdom beneath Natlan and rebuilt its ley lines from wreckage. Since 5.3 she cannot die.

The tribes consult her through the Wayob, trance and dream. She calls herself a helper of humanity.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and immortal, tending the ley lines.

Since 5.3 she lives eternally through Capitano's life force, and the Night Kingdom now accepts outsiders' souls. She has given the Traveler's sibling room to weave a new set of ley lines, the Atlas of the New World.

569.content:
Yuandai (also: A Special-Looking Crane, the nameless heroine of Liyue): A Mt. Aocang crane who became human to help Liyue in a drought, married an exorcist, and lost her memories. In Version 4.4 she regains them and returns to crane form.

She lives with her granddaughter Shuyu, who thinks she has dementia. The Traveler, Paimon and Xianyun (Cloud Retainer) retrace her youth.

Status as of 7.1: Now a non-sentient crane training on Mt. Aocang.

Seen on Qingyun Peak at night. Shuyu became Xianyun's first disciple in the human world. Canon through 7.1 shows her no further.

570.content:
Yuzhanin: A Fatui guard at the gate of Glupov. He stops the Traveler, insists on an invitation letter and bows out of the scene when Sandrone arrives.

The scene happens in Great Deeds on the Tundra (Chapter VII Act I, 7.0), when the Traveler first reaches Snezhnograd looking for Childe.

Status as of 7.1: Last seen on duty at Glupov in Great Deeds on the Tundra (7.0). Nothing later is recorded.

571.content:
Zaha Hadi (also: Professor Zaha Hadi): A retired Kshahrewar architecture professor of Sumeru City, brisk and warm, who taught Kaveh's mother Faranak and knew Kaveh as a child.

She is an expert in formal garden design and the author of essays Kaveh studied. She now spends her days near the Bimarstan, running a feud with Cyrus in a vegetable-growing contest among retired scholars. In Kaveh's Hangout Event she tells him what Faranak was like and helps him find the password to Faranak's notebook.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and retired in Sumeru City.

Last seen in the 3.7 Hangout Event; a Sir Arthur news line suggests she is still active in architecture.

572.content:
Zarechnaya (also: Acting Chair of the Royal Energy Commission, Acting Chair Zarechnaya): Acting Chair of the Royal Energy Commission, sent temporarily from Zapolyarny Palace after the previous chair died. She keeps it running and quietly senses something hidden in its records.

She works at Kresnik's Burning Heart beneath Snezhnograd's central plaza. The Commission matters because it maintains the Kresnik's Torches that keep Snezhnaya warm.

Status as of 7.1: Acting Chair at Kresnik's Burning Heart through 7.1.

Her suspicions remain unconfirmed.

573.content:
Zeitlind (also: Lind): A quiet young woman from Mondstadt who goes to the old sanatorium on Windrest Peak to say goodbye to her missing older sister, Raumhilda. She ends up in the Temple of Space and chooses to give up her own memories to help the Traveler reach Melanta.

Described as steady and reserved, she looks almost exactly like her sister and is often mistaken for her. Her story, A Long Day in the Mountains (6.5), plays with themes of farewell and rebirth.

Status as of 7.1: Alive, back at the Windrest Peak sanatorium after the Temple of Space is freed, and starting afresh with her memories faded.

Her sister's fate is still unresolved; the Traveler and Paimon remind her that Raumhilda is somewhere in the world.

574.content:
Zhara (also: Firebird, Immortal Firebird, Big Doctor Bird, Eternal Flamefeather): Zhara is the winged 'Firebird' guardian of Okurov, a hidden village in Flamefeather Valley, made by the bio-alchemist Koshchei. She attacks outsiders on sight.

The child Nastya calls her the Big Doctor Bird. She is dead by the end of the Traveler's quest, and Aksinya made sure she would not return.

Status as of 7.1: Defeated by the Traveler in Version 7.0; Aksinya then arranged for her body to break down. Dead as of 7.1.

Her fall came just before the end of the series, when Nastya became part of the Perfect Tree. The Immortal Construct enemy still wanders the wild.

575.content:
Zhiqiong (also: Chasm cartographer): A Mingyun Village-born Adventurers' Guild cartographer on the Chasm Exploration Team. She drives herself too hard and in 2.6 vanishes into The Chasm.

Her maps are admired by guild colleagues, yet she fears being forgotten.

Status as of 7.1: Missing: she left a letter and an unseen path into The Chasm.

Jinwu says even she does not want to be forgotten. Her whereabouts remain unknown through 7.1.

576.content:
Zmei (also: Zmei Luchkin): Soft-spoken leader of the Luchkin, a Snezhnograd fae gang, and adopted son of the late Izmaylov. He keeps the High Table's peace after his brother Vasiliy's fall.

He meets the Traveler in the 7.0 World Quest series Mean Streets of the Despicable and is the open-world NPC at the Luchkin base in Zolnyy afterward.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in Zolnyy. After Vasiliy's death he seeks a new head for the Izmaylov and drafts his first High Table proposal (the wiki calls him its Speaker) to ease tensions.

He held a funeral for Vasiliy and believes the Izmaylov name should be carried on without blame. He still calls the Traveler a friend of the Luchkin.

577.content:
Zurvan (also: Elder Zurvan, Lady Zurvan, The First Pari): Zurvan is the First Pari, eldest of the flower-like beings born from the Amrita and guardian of the sealed Vourukasha Oasis in Sumeru. Old, sardonic and forbidding to strangers, she is fond of the young Pari Sorush in her own prickly way.

She awoke in the cataclysm 500 years ago, and fought the Abyss beside a cursed Khaenri'ahn swordsman and the first Skeptics.

Status as of 7.1: Alive in the Vourukasha Oasis, resting after the Sign of Apaosha was extinguished.

As of 7.1 she has no later appearance. The Pari said they would rest.

578.content:
Zver (also: The Beast, "Zver", Beast of the Pale Star Court, Companion of the Belyi Tsar): A sentient two-headed Chimeric Winged Lion, companion of the Belyi Tsar. It guarded his dead body for 500 years.

Haughty and bitterly loyal, it despises Koshchei and Aksinya. The Traveler defeated it in the 7.0 world quest The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated.

Status as of 7.1: Dead as of 7.0: the Traveler defeated it.

It faded to dust, asking the Tsar whether it could finally follow him, after calling the Eye of Graeae the most pathetic of them all.

579.content:
Zverev: A Fatuus serving Sandrone in Snezhnograd. He brings her the news that a mining machine has failed at Svetloledovka.

He speaks to her as 'Lady Marionette' and 'Ma'am', apologises for interrupting her break, and is a calm, plain reporter of facts.

Status as of 7.1: Alive and presumably at work in Snezhnograd as of 7.1; nothing after the 7.0 scene shows him.
